About You:

We want individuals who support our mission of eliminating unsafe abortion by 2030 and who work with us to build an enabling environment to increase access to safe services everywhere. We expect all team members to share our vision and commitment to achieving our mission whilst promoting equality and safeguarding the welfare of all clients and colleagues.

1.       JOB SUMMARY

Working with and reporting to The MCH Center Manager, the Senior Finance & Administration Officer will be responsible for all financial, procurement, property administration, Fixed Asset, and human resources activities and for technically supporting the Centre Receptionist/Cashiers, Centre Storekeepers and Centre Heads operating under the central area office in all such matters. 

This includes handling all financial and procurement transactions and preparing, verifying, consolidating and subsequently submitting the financial reports to the Commercial Service Finance Manager and Finance Director, ensuring that sufficient petty cash is available at service outlets to cover routine activities, advising the center Managers in implementing HR and Financial Policies and Procedures, recording and posting of financial data; maintaining and controlling stock movements at the centers operating, vehicles, buildings and all other fixed assets management and keeping up-to-date pertinent records of books of accounts.

2.      DUTIES/TASKS

Financial Activities:

·         Properly codes and records MCH Centre expenditure, income, and any other related transactions in the books of accounts

·         Receives payment requests, checks supporting documents and coding for completeness and proper authorization; and writes cheques and corresponding payment vouchers.

·         Handles and properly keeps cheque books in safe custody.

·         Effects payment of cheques against receipts/invoices and proper signature of the recipient

·         Ensures valid cash receipts/invoices are delivered to finance for all cheques issued to Payees.

·         Follows-up and ensure working & travel advances at MCH Centre are liquidated timely.

·         Records stock receipts, transfers, and consumptions of MCH Centres activities in ICM and send monthly reconciliation reports to the Senior Finance Officer - Stock and Asset & Commercial Service Finance Manager.

·         Perform clearance of long outstanding advances and stock variances on SUN system.

·         Handles and properly keeps chequebooks in safe custody.

·         Ensures that monthly stock count is carried out by the stores, obtain the count result, check count against ICM Software stock record balances and MSIE’s Reconciliation Report and take or present to the management for timely appropriate action on variances.

·         Records and report all transactions incurred to be uploaded to SUN and send summary of Bi-weekly transactions with supporting documents to the Commercial Service Finance Manager within the set deadline.

·         Review monthly income against deposits to banks and identify collections other than service income.

·         Prepares monthly bank reconciliation for the MCH-Centre bank accounts on SUN system.

·         Perform clearance of long outstanding advances and stock variances on SUN system.

·         Prepare payroll for temporary and contract employees and other regular payments with due consideration to deductions (taxes, advance, loan....)

·         Check all clinic receipt, invoices, and petty cash payments.

·         Keep up to date and orderly controlling records of receipts and issuance of goods.

·         Participate in the annual physical count of stock and fixed assets.

·         Ensure maintenance of memorandum records for all capital goods (long-term assets) with a value below the organizations capitalization policy with proper and easy identification.

·         Sequentially arranges, files and labels financial records in a professional and easily retrievable manner.

·         Assist the Commercial Service Finance Manager and Finance Director in the preparation and revision of budget estimates and targets, processing, and following-up timely transfer of budget requests from MCH Centres.

·         Provide technical assistance to Centre Receptionist/Cashiers, Storekeepers and Centre Heads and MCH Centre Manager in the areas of cash, stock and asset management and human resources.

·         Advise centre Manager on financial policies and procedures as well as procurement rules and regulations.

·         Ensure that all financial and procurement transactions at the Centres are conducted per MSIE’s financial policies and procedures and procurement regulations as well as following donor compliance requirements.

·         Undertakes any other related duties that may be assigned by immediate supervisor.

Human Resources activities:

  • Ensure the proper implementation of MSIE’s Human Resources Policy Manual and the Labour Code of Ethiopia in field office.
  • Prepare Human Resources Planning to ensure sustainable supply of the right personnel.
  • Ensure the timely renewal/termination of staff contracts as per MSIE HR Policy; Liaise with all service outlets of Area Office to ensure proper follow up on HR issues and prepare list of professional pool for duty and weekend activities to fill gaps.
  • Prepare annual leave plan and ensure that all team members have submitted their leave plan each year and follow up the implementation of the plan accordingly.
  • Update and maintain all records of team members' leave, in their personal files and ensure that leave is taken as per the plan of the organization.
  • Assist the Human Resources unit and the Area Office in handling disciplinary issues of center staff.
  • Assist in Conducting training needs assessment.
  • Assist in administering team members’ entitlements, allowances, benefits, and incentives.
  • Prepare periodic reports on Human Resources-related activities.
  • Ensure service outlet staff KPI settings and performance appraisal is conducted according to the guideline and performance Management cycle of MSIE.

Procurement and Property Administration:

  • Manage procurement activities at the service outlets level.
  • Prepare and review specifications and other necessary documents related to local purchasing of materials, supplies, and equipment based on MSIE regulations and procedures with the highest possible expected quality.
  • Raise purchase requisitions and orders for purchases at the MCH Centre level.
  • Leads the MCH Centre procurement committee.
  • Ensure that purchases are made in the best interest of MSIE considering best value for money.
  • Maintain record on purchase price information on both open market and contract purchases and revises these as conditions change; opens contracts for re-bidding when needed.
  • Establish and administer contracts and purchase orders to ensure compliance with bid specifications and requirements such as quality of materials and services, payment scheduling, vendor performance.
  • Establish efficient and cost-effective procurement system for the MCH Centre based on - procurement regulations and procedures.
  • Prepares Procurement Plan for the MCH centres operating under the Centres.
  • Files all procurement documents in an orderly manner for control and reference purposes.
  • Prepares weekly procurement status report and submits to the supervisor.
  • Regularly update the supervisor on matters related to procurement.
  • Ensure that government taxes and fees relating to ownership of MSIE building facilities are timely paid and the title deeds are timely renewed.
  • Regularly make visits to MSIE’s building facilities under the Field Office to assess their status/condition and make recommendation for any renovation, maintenance or modification that may be needed.
  • Ensure that proper safety and security mechanisms are in place at all MSIE MCH Centres locations under the Centres.
  • Maintain fixed asset register and keep a custodian sheet signed by users for property under their custody.
  • Record newly received fixed assets and updates the record regularly.
  • Facilitate the stock replenishment process in consultation with storekeepers and Centre Managers.
  • Assist in the proposal and disposal process of damaged, obsolete, expired materials.
  • Check completeness and accuracy of vehicle logbooks and put signature every day.
  • Check the timely fuelling, maintenance, and servicing of vehicles.
  • Make sure daily and monthly vehicle related checklists and reports are used and submitted on time.
  • Perform other related duties as requested by immediate supervisor.  

Compliance Assessment and System Strengthening, with a scheduled or unscheduled visit to MCH Centers, review, assess and report on.

·         Clients/visitors are efficiently handled, and their information is captured in E-HR on a real-time basis.

·         Review all clinic incomes are collected with MSIE's legal receipts, reconciled on daily cash collection, and deposited daily without any delays. 

·         Conduct scheduled or surprise cash count on cash collected as income & held ad petty cash and ensure cash balance agrees with daily cash collection summary and reports kept on payments respectively,

·         Review and ensure monthly summary report of daily cash collection and deposit is supported with signed off daily cash reconciliation, monthly cash collection summary report and bank statement,

·         Review petty cash and bank records for accuracy and compliance with MSIE policies.

·         Ensure staff debtors for MCH Centre are reviewed monthly and liquidations are processed and reported timely and accurately.

company.name: Marie Stopes International Ethiopia
company.description:
About the company

Marie Stopes International (MSI) is one of the largest international Sexual Reproductive Health (SRH) and Family Planning (FP) organizations in the world. We are a results oriented social enterprise that develop efficient, effective and sustainable SRH/FP programmes around the world.

Marie Stopes International Ethiopia (MSIE), a partner of MSI, is currently undertaking a dramatic scale-up of health service delivery for low income women and couples in Ethiopia. This includes expanding services in clinics and rural outreach programs into new regions of Ethiopia and creating social franchising networks of private quality service providers.  MSIE announces information about job vacancies widely and encourages applications from all sectors of the community.  MSIE considers all applicants based on their abilities and will ensure no group is disadvantaged on the basis of disability, gender, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race (which includes colour, nationality and ethnic or national origins), religion or belief, economic or social class, sex, HIV/AIDs status and political affiliation.

MSIE also implements a Safeguarding Policy to safeguard and protect the rights of staff, children, young people and vulnerable sections of the community and to this end, successful candidates will need to sign MSIE’s ‘code of conduct’ and undergo a background check. The Safeguarding Policy includes an adult Safeguarding, dignity at work place, child safeguarding, human trafficking and anti-slavery, sexual harassment, equality and diversity.  MSIE applies zero tolerance approach for the violation such policies. 

MSIE is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to hiring and retaining female employees. The organization has flexible policies including: travel policy for pregnant and lactating women, flexible work hour for non-clinic staff without reducing the total working hour. Women employees have access to on-job mentorship which aim to create gender-sensitive and inclusive work environment. As such, qualified women are encouraged to apply 

 

Our Mission

Ensuring the Individual’s Right to Children by Choice not Chance.

Vision
To become a sustainable nationwide provider of high quality, integrated reproductive health/family planning services.

Our Values

1 Mission driven
With unwavering commitment, we exist to empower women and men to have children by choice not chance.

2 Client centred
We are dedicated to our clients and work tirelessly to deliver high-quality, high-impact services that meet their individual needs.

3 Accountable
We are accountable for our actions and focus on results, ensuring long term sustainability and increasing the impact of the Partnership.

4 Courageous
We recruit and nurture talented, passionate and brave people who have the courage to push boundaries, make tough decisions and challenge others in line with our mission.
 

Why work for us

MSI works in 37 countries around the world to help women and girls to have children by choice, not chance.

For an individual woman or girl, being able to choose when she has children means having the power to take control of her future.
It can mean having the ability to finish her education, pursue a career, look after the children she already has and ensure she remains healthy. MSI was founded in 1976 to provide the contraception and safe abortion services that give women and girls a choice. Since then, choice has been at the heart of everything that we do and our mission remains clear: to help women and girls to have children by choice, not chance.

MSI is a global organisation with 11,000 team members working in 37 countries to deliver our mission. Starting from one single clinic in London, our organisation has grown from one clinic in central London to become one of the world’s largest providers of high quality, affordable contraception and safe abortion services.
Over the last 40 years, we have touched the lives of more than 120 million women and girls, giving them the power to take control of their futures. But we know that there is much more to do, today there are over 230 million women who want to use contraception but can't and that number continues to grow.

fields.title: Creative Content Growth Strategist (Video Marketing)
fields.description: About Tinova Tinova helps founders build startups that customers trust, investors back, and markets adopt. Alongside working with startup founders, we're building a founder-first personal brand that educates, inspires, and reaches entrepreneurs globally through high-quality content across LinkedIn, TikTok, Instagram, and Meta. We're looking for a Creative Content Growth Strategist to become the strategic partner behind our founder's personal brand. About The Role This is more than a social media or video planning role. You'll combine content strategy, audience psychology, trend research, storytelling, and analytics to turn the founder's expertise into content people watch, share, and remember. You'll work directly with the founder from idea to publication and continuously improve content based on performance data. Responsibilities Develop long-term content strategies, content pillars, and weekly/monthly calendars aligned with business goals. Research startup trends, AI, fundraising, entrepreneurship, audience pain points, competitors, and creator strategies. Identify trends and viral content opportunities and develop research-backed ideas. Create stronger hooks, storytelling, CTAs, and content structures based on audience psychology. Develop video concepts and shooting briefs; recommend pacing, editing, captions, B-roll, and visual storytelling. Manage and optimize content across TikTok, Instagram, and Facebook (Meta) , including publishing, scheduling, and engagement. Track reach, watch time, retention, engagement, and conversions to identify what works and recommend improvements. Collaborate with the founder, writers, designers, and editors to turn ideas into publish-ready content. Requirements 3+ years in content strategy, creator marketing, personal branding, or social media growth. Deep understanding of TikTok, Instagram Reels, LinkedIn, and Meta. Strong research skills. Excellent storytelling ability. Understanding of content psychology and audience behavior. Ability to recognize content trends early. Strong communication skills. Experience working with founders or personal brands is highly preferred. Success in This Role Within your first 90 days, you'll: Build a repeatable content strategy. Create a high-performing content calendar. Improve video retention and engagement. Increase reach across TikTok and Meta. Become the founder's strategic partner for content decisions. What We're Looking For We're looking for someone naturally curious, highly creative, and obsessed with understanding why content performs . You should enjoy researching, spotting trends before they become mainstream, analyzing audience psychology, and continuously experimenting with new ideas. If you watch a viral video and immediately start breaking down why it worked, you'll fit right in. How to Apply Please send the following to tinovahr@tinovagency.com Your Resume and LinkedIn profile A short introduction about yourself (2–3 paragraphs) Links to 3–5 personal brands or companies you've helped grow (include your role and contribution) One piece of content (video, post, or campaign) you're most proud of, and explain why it performed well A 60–90 second Loom video introducing yourself and telling us why you're the right fit for this role Bonus (Highly Recommended) Choose one of Tino's recent videos and share: How you would improve the hook What you'd change in the storytelling How you'd edit it differently to improve retention How you'd repurpose it for TikTok, Instagram Reels, and LinkedIn We care more about how you think than how polished your answer is.

fields.title: Research, Monitoring and Evaluation (RM&E) Advisor
fields.description: Ipas is a non-profit organization working to improve women’s lives by focusing on improving access to information and services to basic sexual and reproductive health across the globe. Since the year 2000, Ipas Ethiopia has been collaborating with the Ministry of Health (MOH), Regional Health Bureaus (RHBs), Community Based Organizations (CBOs) and various local and international partners to reduce maternal mortality and morbidity resulting from unwanted pregnancy and unsafe abortion. In light of the need to strengthen our relationship with stakeholders and expedite programme implementation, we are planning to hire for the following position: Job Title : Research, Monitoring and Evaluation (RM&E) Advisor Place of Work: Addis Ababa Report to: Senior Research and Evaluation (R&E) Advisor Position Type: Full-time Grade : S1 Terms of Employment: One year with possibilities for extension Salary : Negotiable General Description The Research, Monitoring & Evaluation (RM&E) Advisor is responsible for providing technical support for Ipas Ethiopia’s research, monitoring and evaluation efforts and collaborating with the technical and program units to ensure high-quality Research, Monitoring, and Evaluation (RM&E) processes and methodologies. Additionally, this position guarantees that best practices are implemented in all RM&E activities. The RM&E Advisor will ensure that data are shared to and used by internal and external audiences through routine review of findings and dissemination in conferences and publications. Duties & Responsibilities Provide technical support for the development and implementation of RM&E systems, including data collection, data management and documentation, and results reporting. Work closely with M&E Coordinator to follow up data collection and timely availability of data, addressing data related queries and preparing and dissemination of dynamic dashboards and fact sheets. Ensure quality control and consistency with Ipas global standards for MR&E, review periodic Global reports, respond and rectify data quality issues and approve Global M&E report timely. Follow up any technical update and country office concerns about local and global RM&E systems and provide technical leadership and follow up for its proper implementation. Contribute to the preparation for donors and other stakeholder documents, including data and narrative inputs. Works closely with Senior Research and Evaluation Advisor in establishing log frames, RM&E work plans, and targets during the drafting of project proposals. Create and update Stata codes for data cleaning and analysis for all projects. Actively participate in the design, ethical approval, implementation, data analysis, drafting reports, and preparing dissemination materials of research and evaluation projects. Conduct dissemination of MR&E findings, both internally and externally, including workshops and review meetings. Represent Ipas at local, regional and global professional meetings and conferences. Collaborate with other Ipas units and country programs to achieve overall organizational objectives. Carry out other duties as assigned. Note : Female applicants are highly encouraged to apply. Ipas management reserves the right to modify the contents of this position description at any time. Ipas is strongly committed to providing a work environment that is free from all forms of harassment, discrimination, and inequity. company.name: Ahadu Bank S.C
company.description:
Why work for us?


By joining us, you'll help empower Ethiopians through our pioneering cutting-edge financial services. Join our passionate team, driven by purpose, integrity, and a desire to make a real difference. We offer a dynamic environment, opportunities for growth, and the chance to be part of something revolutionary. Embrace your purpose and build a fulfilling career. This is your chance to shape the future of Ethiopian finance.


Employee Benefits

  • Competitive salary and benefits package
  • Medical Coverage
  • Salary Advance Loan
  • Consumer Loan
  • Mortgage and Vehicle Acquisition Loan.



The Company

Established by visionary entrepreneurs and professionals, Ahadu Bank provides a different model of banking centered on the philosophy of Inclusive Intermediation.

Founded by over 10,000 shareholders and incorporated under the Ethiopian Banking Business Proclamation, Ahadu Bank offers full-fledged commercial banking services. The Bank is domiciled in Ethiopia with its Head Office located on Africa Avenue, Sunshine Building, Addis Ababa.

Ahadu Bank completed the National Bank of Ethiopia's (NBE) initial capital requirement on January 2, 2021, and received its banking license on October 5, 2021. On June 29, 2022, the bank received authorization from the NBE to begin operations and officially opened its doors on July 16, 2022.

According to a June 2024 report, the bank now boasts over 100 branches and a workforce exceeding 900 employees nationwide.


Mission

Pioneer avant-garde financial services for promoting the economic welfare of Ethiopians.


Vision

Take a lead role in the financial sector, in 2025 E.C, in support of the aspirations of the citizenry and the country.


Core values

  1. Fear of God
  2. Passion for Serving
  3. Honesty
  4. Organizational Learning
  5. Proactive Accountability
  6. Humaneness


Our way

We strive to drive the development of Ethiopia's financial services to benefit Ethiopians in a sustainable and inclusive way. We strive to have a positive socio-economic impact in every aspect of our business. We believe that addressing the needs of the unbanked and underbanked by reaching out to rural communities, supporting and nurturing small businesses, practicing responsible banking principles, and investing in innovative technology to digitize our operations helps us create value for our customers, shareholders, and the broader community.


Culture

At Ahadu Bank, our culture thrives on a unique blend of purpose and progress. We're driven by a deep desire to make a positive impact, evident in our core values of social responsibility and financial empowerment for all Ethiopians. We're a passionate team, working together to pioneer cutting-edge financial solutions. Our commitment to innovation goes hand-in-hand with integrity, ensuring we operate with honesty and ethical practices. We believe in fostering a growth mindset, embracing "Organizational Learning" to continuously develop ourselves and each other. This collaborative spirit is core to our success, as we build a supportive and dynamic environment where everyone can thrive. If you're looking to make a real difference and be part of something revolutionary, Ahadu Bank is the place for you.

The bank was established with the largest initial shareholder base in the history of Ethiopia's private banking sector, comprising over 167,000 shareholders. Operations and Services

Amhara Bank operates a network of over 322 branches across Ethiopia, serving a customer base of approximately 2.9 million individuals.


Digital Banking

The bank provides digital financial services, primarily through a proprietary mobile banking application. The digital platform has registered over 1.2 million subscribers.


Interest-Free Banking

Amhara Bank operates a full-fledged interest-free banking (IFB) window under the brand name "Marhaba," which was launched on March 18, 2023. The service offers Sharia-compliant financial products tailored for customers seeking non-interest financial solutions.

fields.description: Senior Solution Architect (B2B Enterprise Systems) Reporting To: Project Manager & B2B Engineering Head Job Type: Full-Time About the Role: We are looking for an experienced Senior Solution Architect with a strong backend engineering background and expertise in large-scale B2B systems . In this role, you will design scalable, secure, and high-performing enterprise architectures. You will serve as the core technical bridge across our delivery teams, working directly with our Project Manager, Business Analyst (BA), Backend Tech Lead, and Frontend Tech Lead to translate complex business needs into clear, buildable system designs. Core Responsibilities: • Enterprise Architecture Design: Architect high-throughput, resilient B2B platforms using microservices, event-driven architecture, robust API strategies, and scalable database schemas. • Backend Leadership: Leverage your deep backend background to guide database design, API design (REST, gRPC), messaging pipelines (Kafka, RabbitMQ), and cloud infrastructure (AWS/Azure/GCP). • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with the Project Manager on timelines, risk management, and effort estimations. Work with the Business Analyst to translate B2B logic and functional specs into technical blueprints. Collaborate with Backend and Frontend Tech Leads to establish clean integration standards, API payload contracts, and system boundaries. • Governance & Strategy: Work with the CTO to ensure software designs align with long-term tech strategy, security standards (OAuth2, RBAC), and cloud cost efficiency. Key Requirements: Experience: 6+ years in software engineering, with 2+ years in a Solution Architect or Principal Engineer role. Backend Expertise: Proven background in backend development (Java, Go, C#, Python, Node.js) with distributed systems design. B2B Experience: Demonstrated experience architecting large enterprise systems, multi-tenant SaaS, or complex integrations. Cloud & Modern Stack: Hands-on experience with Cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP), Docker, Kubernetes, microservices, and databases (PostgreSQL, Redis, NoSQL). Team-Oriented: Exceptional communication skills and a proven track record of bridging technical discussions between PMs, BAs, and Engineering Leads.

fields.title: Sales Agent
fields.description: Company: RE/MAX Ethiopia Department: Sales Location: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia Employment Type: Full-Time About RE/MAX Ethiopia RE/MAX Ethiopia is the Ethiopian franchise of RE/MAX®, one of the world’s largest and most recognized real estate franchise organizations. As part of the global RE/MAX network, we connect property owners, developers, investors, buyers, tenants, and members of the Ethiopian diaspora with international best practices in real estate sales, marketing, consulting, and investment advisory. We are committed to raising the standard of real estate in Ethiopia through professional, transparent, technology-driven, and client-focused services. About the Role We are looking for Sales Agents to join our Sales Team and play a key role in driving property transactions at RE/MAX Ethiopia. Sales Agents will work across both the property acquisition and buyer-facing sides of the sales process , from prospecting property owners and building our property inventory to qualifying buyers, conducting property tours, managing negotiations, and supporting transactions through closing. The ideal candidate will be confident, persistent, client-focused, and comfortable working in a target-driven environment that requires both active prospecting and strong relationship management . This role involves significant field work, client interaction, follow-up, negotiation, and the use of digital tools and CRM systems. Key Responsibilities Prospect and engage property owners and potential buyers through cold calls, WhatsApp, referrals, social media, field visits, and other channels. Build and maintain a strong pipeline of property owners, buyers, and sales opportunities. Conduct listing presentations, explain RE/MAX services, and secure signed listing agreements. Qualify buyers by understanding their property requirements, budget, financing status, priorities, and purchase timeline. Match qualified buyers with suitable properties based on their needs and preferences. Verify properties through physical inspection and collect accurate property information, owner identification, title documents, photos, and other required documentation. Ensure properties are accurately presented with complete information, appropriate pricing, professional visual assets, and updated listing status. Coordinate with marketing and back-office teams to ensure properties are prepared and published effectively. Arrange and conduct property tours and walkthroughs for prospective buyers. Maintain proactive communication with property owners, buyers, and other relevant parties throughout the sales process. Lead and support negotiations between buyers and sellers, including offers, counteroffers, and deal coordination. Prepare offers and support transactions through the closing process. Collect buyer feedback and use it to improve property matching and sales opportunities. Collaborate closely with other Sales Agents to communicate property availability, buyer requirements, viewing schedules, pricing changes, seller requirements, and negotiation updates. Coordinate with Finance, Legal, Operations, and Marketing teams to facilitate smooth transaction progression. Maintain accurate CRM records, activity logs, follow-up schedules, client information, and sales pipeline updates. Deliver a professional and transparent client experience from initial contact through listing, property viewing, negotiation, and transaction completion. raw_data.title: RMNCH Commodity and Service-Delivery Lead
raw_data.description:
About Opian

Opian is an Ethiopian health-technology and innovation company building decision infrastructure for stronger health systems. We combine deep knowledge of how care and supply chains operate, human-centred product design, data engineering and responsible artificial intelligence. Our work helps health workers, managers and public institutions turn fragmented data into timely decisions—so essential medicines, vaccines and services are available where and when people need them.

Our philosophy

We believe useful innovation is not novelty for its own sake. It is the disciplined work of understanding a real problem, challenging assumptions, building and testing a better response, measuring what changes, and strengthening the institutions that must sustain the result. Technology is valuable only when it improves a decision, a workflow or an outcome in the real operating environment.

· Start with reality: design around the health workers, workloads, incentives, infrastructure and constraints that actually exist—not an imported ideal workflow.

· Build with people, not for them: government counterparts and frontline users are co-designers, decision-makers and eventual owners, not passive recipients.

· Strengthen the system, not a standalone application: connect workflows, data, institutions and incentives so information can lead to action across every level.

· Push boundaries responsibly: make ambitious but testable bets, protect safety and privacy, and change direction quickly when evidence contradicts the original idea.

· Make capability local and durable: transfer knowledge, product ownership and operational responsibility so progress continues without permanent dependence on an external project team.

· Be honest about impact: distinguish deployment from adoption and activity from results; make claims specific, measurable and open to verification.

What this means for candidates

Opian is looking for accomplished specialists who are also builders. Candidates should bring exceptional depth in their discipline, intellectual courage, practical judgment and the humility to learn from users and evidence. We value people who can move from ambiguity to a testable approach, from a workshop to an operating routine, and from a promising pilot to an institutionally owned system. The standard is simple: show not only what you know, but what you personally built, changed, tested, learned and left stronger.

· Work across public health, supply chain, policy, product, technology and field implementation boundaries.

· Turn expertise into usable products, processes, decisions and measurable improvements—not reports alone.

· Operate with urgency while preserving quality, public trust, data protection, service continuity and government ownership.

Government Partnership and Institutionalization Lead

Role purpose

Ensure that the program addresses the distinct forecasting, availability, quality, accountability and service-readiness requirements of maternal, newborn and child health commodities, including their relationship to family planning and primary-healthcare services.

Key responsibilities

· Map priority RMNCH commodity pathways, service protocols, consumption signals, resupply processes and causes of missed service opportunities.

· Define and maintain the prioritized commodity list, product attributes, kit relationships, substitutions and service-readiness rules.

· Translate clinical and program requirements into transactional workflows, data elements, alerts and performance indicators.

· Ensure alignment between commodity data, service-delivery events, eCHIS or other service systems and national product and facility registries.

· Support forecasting, quantification, inventory policy, redistribution and replenishment approaches for priority commodities.

· Work with facilities and program teams to test whether digital information results in timely operational decisions.

· Design and support training, supportive supervision, review meetings and corrective-action processes.

· Identify gender, equity and access implications of commodity gaps and proposed digital workflows.

· Support evaluation, learning and development of scale-up and sustainability recommendations.

Expected results

· A validated RMNCH commodity and service-readiness requirements package.

· Improved visibility and response to priority commodity gaps at service-delivery points.

· Operational linkages between commodity availability, service plans and performance reviews.

· Institutionalized SOPs and decision routines for RMNCH commodity management.

fields.title: Procurement Officer
fields.description: Ethio-BioPharma Enterprise (EBPE) is Ethiopia’s state-owned pharmaceutical manufacturing enterprise, established to build the nation’s capacity to manufacture vaccines, essential medicines, diagnostics, medical supplies and other healthcare technologies locally. Operating under EIH, EBPE is developing an integrated pharmaceutical campus at the Kilinto Special Economic Zone in Addis Ababa, co-locating multiple manufacturing units that share infrastructure, talent, and corporate services. Addis Ababa, co-locating multiple manufacturing units that share infrastructure, talent, and corporate services. I. GENERAL POSITION DESCRIPTION Main Purpose of the post The Procurement Officer is responsible for the timely and cost-effective acquisition of goods, services, and works necessary for the operation of Ethio-BioPharma Enterprise. The Officer ensures that all procurement activities are conducted in strict compliance with the Federal Public Procurement and Property Administration Proclamation, the Public Procurement Directive, and the enterprise’s internal manuals. The role focuses on ensuring "Value for Money," transparency, and fairness in the selection of suppliers, while maintaining the technical and quality standards required for pharmaceutical and administrative inputs. I. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES / ACCOUNTABILITY A. Procurement Planning and Requisition Handling 1. Assists in the preparation of the Enterprise’s Annual Procurement Plan based on inputs from various departments and projects. 2. Reviews and verifies purchase requisitions to ensure specifications are clear, authorized, and supported by budget availability. 3. Consolidates requirements to achieve economies of scale and updates the procurement schedule regularly. B. Sourcing and Tendering Operations 1. Prepares Bid Documents, Requests for Quotations (RFQ), and Requests for Proposals (RFP) in accordance with government standard formats. 2. Identifies and maintains a database of reliable suppliers and contractors, ensuring they are registered on the Federal Public Procurement and Property Administration Agency (FPPA) suppliers' list. 3. Coordinates the advertisement of tenders and manages the bid opening process in the presence of the Tender Committee and bidders. C. Evaluation and Contract Award 1. Serves as a technical member or secretary for the Procurement Endorsing/Evaluation Committee. 2. Performs commercial evaluations of bids and coordinates with technical units for quality/technical assessments. 3. Prepares evaluation reports and recommendations for award based on the "Lowest Evaluated Bid" or "Quality and Cost-Based" criteria. 4. Drafts purchase orders and formal contracts, ensuring all legal and performance security requirements are met. D. Contract Management and Follow-up 1. Monitors the delivery timelines of goods and services, ensuring suppliers adhere to the terms of the contract/PO. 2. Coordinates with the Property/Store unit to ensure that delivered items match the technical specifications and quantities ordered (Inspection and Receiving). 3. Handles claims, liquidating damages, and disputes with suppliers in consultation with the Legal unit and the Manager. E. Compliance and Record Keeping 1. Ensures that the "Five Pillars" of public procurement (Value for Money, Transparency, Non-discrimination, Accountability, and Fairness) are strictly upheld. 2. Maintains comprehensive and organized procurement files for every transaction to ensure readiness for audit by the Federal Auditor General or internal auditors. 3. Prepares periodic procurement status reports for management. II. Authority The Procurement Officer is authorized to: a. Communicate with potential suppliers to obtain market information and price estimates. b. Reject requisitions that do not meet the enterprise’s procurement guidelines or lack technical specifications. c. Propose the disqualification of bidders who fail to meet mandatory legal or technical requirements. d. Verify the accuracy of supplier invoices before they are forwarded to the Finance department for payment. Effort required 1. The position requires high integrity, negotiation skills, and the ability to work under pressure to meet project deadlines. 2. Work involves frequent market visits, attending bid openings, and detailed scrutiny of technical documents.

Main Purpose of the post

The Procurement Officer is responsible for the timely and cost-effective acquisition of goods, services, and works necessary for the operation of Ethio-BioPharma Enterprise. The Officer ensures that all procurement activities are conducted in strict compliance with the Federal Public Procurement and Property Administration Proclamation, the Public Procurement Directive, and the enterprise’s internal manuals. The role focuses on ensuring "Value for Money," transparency, and fairness in the selection of suppliers, while maintaining the technical and quality standards required for pharmaceutical and administrative inputs.

I.        KEY RESPONSIBILITIES / ACCOUNTABILITY

A. Procurement Planning and Requisition Handling

1. Assists in the preparation of the Enterprise’s Annual Procurement Plan based on inputs from various departments and projects.

2. Reviews and verifies purchase requisitions to ensure specifications are clear, authorized, and supported by budget availability.

3. Consolidates requirements to achieve economies of scale and updates the procurement schedule regularly.

B. Sourcing and Tendering Operations

1. Prepares Bid Documents, Requests for Quotations (RFQ), and Requests for Proposals (RFP) in accordance with government standard formats.

2. Identifies and maintains a database of reliable suppliers and contractors, ensuring they are registered on the Federal Public Procurement and Property Administration Agency (FPPA) suppliers' list.

3. Coordinates the advertisement of tenders and manages the bid opening process in the presence of the Tender Committee and bidders.

C. Evaluation and Contract Award

1.  Serves as a technical member or secretary for the Procurement Endorsing/Evaluation Committee.

2.  Performs commercial evaluations of bids and coordinates with technical units for quality/technical assessments.

3.  Prepares evaluation reports and recommendations for award based on the "Lowest Evaluated Bid" or "Quality and Cost-Based" criteria.

4.  Drafts purchase orders and formal contracts, ensuring all legal and performance security requirements are met.

D. Contract Management and Follow-up

1.  Monitors the delivery timelines of goods and services, ensuring suppliers adhere to the terms of the contract/PO.

2.  Coordinates with the Property/Store unit to ensure that delivered items match the technical specifications and quantities ordered (Inspection and Receiving).

3.  Handles claims, liquidating damages, and disputes with suppliers in consultation with the Legal unit and the Manager.

E. Compliance and Record Keeping

1. Ensures that the "Five Pillars" of public procurement (Value for Money, Transparency, Non-discrimination, Accountability, and Fairness) are strictly upheld.

2. Maintains comprehensive and organized procurement files for every transaction to ensure readiness for audit by the Federal Auditor General or internal auditors.

3. Prepares periodic procurement status reports for management.

II.     Authority

The Procurement Officer is authorized to:

a. Communicate with potential suppliers to obtain market information and price estimates.

b. Reject requisitions that do not meet the enterprise’s procurement guidelines or lack technical specifications.

c. Propose the disqualification of bidders who fail to meet mandatory legal or technical requirements.

d. Verify the accuracy of supplier invoices before they are forwarded to the Finance department for payment.

Effort required

1. The position requires high integrity, negotiation skills, and the ability to work under pressure to meet project deadlines.

2. Work involves frequent market visits, attending bid openings, and detailed scrutiny of technical documents.

fields.title: (ToR) Development of a Standardized Paralegal Training Curriculum and Manual for EWLA Volunteer Committee Members
fields.description: TERMS OF REFERENCE (ToR) Development of a Standardized Paralegal Training Curriculum and Manual for EWLA Volunteer Committee Members Background The Ethiopian Women Lawyers Association (EWLA) has been working for over three decades to advance women's rights, access to justice, and legal reform in Ethiopia. EWLA provides free legal aid services to women and girls through its Head Office, regional branch offices, and volunteer committees operating at zonal and woreda levels across nine regional states. These services are further supported by a network of volunteer members, including lawyers, law graduates, and community-based paralegals. EWLA's volunteer committee members often serve as the first point of contact for women seeking legal assistance on matters such as family law, gender-based violence (GBV), property and inheritance disputes, sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR), and other human rights issues. They play a critical role in facilitating access to justice for women and girls within their communities. It is therefore essential to strengthen their capacity to deliver quality, gender-responsive, and survivor-centered legal aid services. Although EWLA has provided training to volunteers on basic laws, legal procedures, and the legal frameworks that safeguard the rights of women and children, there remains a need to standardize the training content and delivery methods. A comprehensive and consistent training program should be provided regularly to all EWLA volunteers to ensure the quality and effectiveness of legal aid services across all regions. To this end, EWLA seeks to engage qualified expert(s) to develop a standardized paralegal training manual and curriculum that will serve as the foundation for capacity-building initiatives for its volunteer committees nationwide. Objectives of the Assignment Overall Objective To develop a standardized, practical, and Ethiopia-specific Paralegal Aid Training Manual that strengthens the knowledge, skills, and ethical grounding of EWLA's volunteer paralegal aid providers. Specific Objectives Develop a curriculum, modular training manual covering core legal knowledge, referral pathways, and paralegal skills relevant to EWLA's legal aid mandate Ensure the manual reflects current Ethiopian law, including family law (federal and regional laws), criminal law provisions on GBV/HTPs, property/inheritance law (including land rights), labor laws and SRHR-related legal protections Incorporate survivor-centered, trauma-informed, and confidentiality-based approaches consistent with EWLA's institutional values Produce accompanying facilitation tools (trainer's guide, session plans, case scenarios, assessment tools) to support consistent delivery across branch offices Ensure the manual is written in accessible language for volunteers without formal legal training in (Amharic and English) Main Tasks Inception and Planning Develop an inception note outlining methodology, scope, structure, and timeline Review existing EWLA materials and identify content areas to be prioritized Desk Review and Content Mapping Conduct a comprehensive review of relevant Ethiopian laws Review prior training or induction materials used by EWLA, if any Identify core substantive and procedural content areas to be covered in the manual Training Needs Consultation Conduct consultations (interviews/focus group discussions) with EWLA staff, branch office coordinators, and a sample of current volunteer paralegals Identify existing capacity gaps, common case types, and practical challenges faced by volunteers in the field Document findings in a brief training needs summary Manual Drafting Develop a detailed curriculum and manual outline/table of contents for EWLA review and approval Draft the full training manual, covering at minimum: Roles, responsibilities, and ethical conduct of paralegal aid volunteers, including confidentiality and do-no-harm principles Overview of the Ethiopian legal system and relevant institutions (courts, police, prosecutors, social affairs bureaus) Core substantive law modules: family law, GBV-related criminal law, property and inheritance, labor and SRHR legal protections Client interviewing, basic case documentation, and referral pathways Survivor-centered and trauma-informed communication techniques Case studies and practice scenarios grounded in the Ethiopian context Trainer's Guide Development Develop a companion trainer's guide with session plans, timing, suggested methodology, and pre/post-training assessment tools Prepare PowerPoint Presentation Pilot test the manual through the provision training to paralegals Pilot raw_data.description:
TERMS OF REFERENCE (ToR)

Development of a Standardized Paralegal Training Curriculum and Manual for EWLA Volunteer Committee Members

Background

The Ethiopian Women Lawyers Association (EWLA) has been working for over three decades to advance women's rights, access to justice, and legal reform in Ethiopia. EWLA provides free legal aid services to women and girls through its Head Office, regional branch offices, and volunteer committees operating at zonal and woreda levels across nine regional states. These services are further supported by a network of volunteer members, including lawyers, law graduates, and community-based paralegals.

EWLA's volunteer committee members often serve as the first point of contact for women seeking legal assistance on matters such as family law, gender-based violence (GBV), property and inheritance disputes, sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR), and other human rights issues. They play a critical role in facilitating access to justice for women and girls within their communities. It is therefore essential to strengthen their capacity to deliver quality, gender-responsive, and survivor-centered legal aid services.

Although EWLA has provided training to volunteers on basic laws, legal procedures, and the legal frameworks that safeguard the rights of women and children, there remains a need to standardize the training content and delivery methods. A comprehensive and consistent training program should be provided regularly to all EWLA volunteers to ensure the quality and effectiveness of legal aid services across all regions.

To this end, EWLA seeks to engage qualified expert(s) to develop a standardized paralegal training manual and curriculum that will serve as the foundation for capacity-building initiatives for its volunteer committees nationwide.

Objectives of the Assignment

Overall Objective

To develop a standardized, practical, and Ethiopia-specific Paralegal Aid Training Manual that strengthens the knowledge, skills, and ethical grounding of EWLA's volunteer paralegal aid providers.

Specific Objectives

  • Develop a curriculum, modular training manual covering core legal knowledge, referral pathways, and paralegal skills relevant to EWLA's legal aid mandate
  • Ensure the manual reflects current Ethiopian law, including family law (federal and regional laws), criminal law provisions on GBV/HTPs, property/inheritance law (including land rights), labor laws and SRHR-related legal protections
  • Incorporate survivor-centered, trauma-informed, and confidentiality-based approaches consistent with EWLA's institutional values
  • Produce accompanying facilitation tools (trainer's guide, session plans, case scenarios, assessment tools) to support consistent delivery across branch offices
  • Ensure the manual is written in accessible language for volunteers without formal legal training in (Amharic and English)

Main Tasks

Inception and Planning

  • Develop an inception note outlining methodology, scope, structure, and timeline
  • Review existing EWLA materials and identify content areas to be prioritized

Desk Review and Content Mapping

  • Conduct a comprehensive review of relevant Ethiopian laws
  • Review prior training or induction materials used by EWLA, if any
  • Identify core substantive and procedural content areas to be covered in the manual

Training Needs Consultation

  • Conduct consultations (interviews/focus group discussions) with EWLA staff, branch office coordinators, and a sample of current volunteer paralegals
  • Identify existing capacity gaps, common case types, and practical challenges faced by volunteers in the field
  • Document findings in a brief training needs summary

Manual Drafting

  • Develop a detailed curriculum and manual outline/table of contents for EWLA review and approval
  • Draft the full training manual, covering at minimum:
    • Roles, responsibilities, and ethical conduct of paralegal aid volunteers, including confidentiality and do-no-harm principles
    • Overview of the Ethiopian legal system and relevant institutions (courts, police, prosecutors, social affairs bureaus)
    • Core substantive law modules: family law, GBV-related criminal law, property and inheritance, labor and SRHR legal protections
    • Client interviewing, basic case documentation, and referral pathways
    • Survivor-centered and trauma-informed communication techniques
    • Case studies and practice scenarios grounded in the Ethiopian context

Trainer's Guide Development

  • Develop a companion trainer's guide with session plans, timing, suggested methodology, and pre/post-training assessment tools
  • Prepare PowerPoint Presentation
  • Pilot test the manual through the provision training to paralegals

Pilot test, Review and Validation

  • Incorporate feedback from EWLA Head Office through at least two rounds of review and revision
  • Facilitate an internal validation session with relevant staff and volunteer representatives
  • Finalize the manual based on the pilot test and validations feedback.

Scope of the Training Manual

The manual will cover (but is not limited to):

1 Substantive and Procedural Legal Content

  • Family law (marriage, divorce, inheritance)
  • Criminal law provisions related to GBV/VAW
  • Property and inheritance rights (including land rights
  • Extra contractual liabilities
  • SRHR-related legal protections
  • ADR/ customary court laws and guides
  • Relevant procedural and referral frameworks
    • Criminal procedure and evidence law relevant to GBV/VAW
    • Civil procedure law – basic procedural and evidence requirement

2 Paralegal Skills and Conduct

  • Client interviewing and basic case documentation
  • Referral pathways and case management
  • Ethical conduct, confidentiality, and do-no-harm principles
  • Survivor-centered, trauma-informed communication

3 Audience and Use

  • Primary audience: EWLA volunteer paralegal aid members (community-based paralegals, law graduates, volunteer lawyers)
  • Use context: induction training, refresher training, and ongoing reference at Head Office and branch offices

Key Deliverables

  • Inception note (methodology and work plan)
  • Training needs summary
  • Draft manual outline/table of contents
  • First full draft of the training manual
  • Trainer's guide (session plans, methodology, assessment tools)
  • Pilot test
  • Final training manual and trainer's guide, print-ready  and PPP (Amharic and English

company.name: Ethiopian Women Lawyers Association(EWLA)
company.description:
The Ethiopian Women Lawyers Association (EWLA) is a non-profit women's advocacy group founded by Ethiopian women lawyers. It was legally registered in 1995 and began operation in 1996. EWLA is headquartered in Addis Ababa and has six branches in Bahir Dar, Assosa, Hawassa, Adama/Nazareth, Diredawa and Gambella. The branch/regional offices are supported by 53 trained voluntary committee members organized at woreda and zonal levels; these offices provide structures to reach women at grass root level in Ethiopia.

EWLA’s vision is to see a country where women are equal to men and articulates its mission as promoting the economic, political, social and legal rights of women and assist them to secure full protection of their rights under the Constitution of Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia and other international human rights conventions. 

 

The Association, to achieve its mission, works through three core programs:

Under its Legal Aid Program EWLA assists women, particularly disadvantaged women, who are victims of gender-based violence free of charge. The service includes legal advice/counseling, writing court briefs (court charges and affidavits) as well as representing clients in courts.  

The second program, Public Education and Capacity Building Program works on raising awareness on women's rights. This program conducts training and advocacy workshops on the legal, social and political rights of women for students, government, and civil society organization (CSO) employees.

Through the third program, Research and Law Reform Advocacy, EWLA conducts various researches on women's rights issues and findings are used as a major resource for law reform advocacy and public education.

fields.title: Vaccine Supply-Chain Lead
fields.description: About Opian Opian is an Ethiopian health-technology and innovation company building decision infrastructure for stronger health systems. We combine deep knowledge of how care and supply chains operate, human-centred product design, data engineering and responsible artificial intelligence. Our work helps health workers, managers and public institutions turn fragmented data into timely decisions—so essential medicines, vaccines and services are available where and when people need them. Our philosophy We believe useful innovation is not novelty for its own sake. It is the disciplined work of understanding a real problem, challenging assumptions, building and testing a better response, measuring what changes, and strengthening the institutions that must sustain the result. Technology is valuable only when it improves a decision, a workflow or an outcome in the real operating environment. · Start with reality: design around the health workers, workloads, incentives, infrastructure and constraints that actually exist—not an imported ideal workflow. · Build with people, not for them: government counterparts and frontline users are co-designers, decision-makers and eventual owners, not passive recipients. · Strengthen the system, not a standalone application: connect workflows, data, institutions and incentives so information can lead to action across every level. · Push boundaries responsibly: make ambitious but testable bets, protect safety and privacy, and change direction quickly when evidence contradicts the original idea. · Make capability local and durable: transfer knowledge, product ownership and operational responsibility so progress continues without permanent dependence on an external project team. · Be honest about impact: distinguish deployment from adoption and activity from results; make claims specific, measurable and open to verification. What this means for candidates Opian is looking for accomplished specialists who are also builders. Candidates should bring exceptional depth in their discipline, intellectual courage, practical judgment and the humility to learn from users and evidence. We value people who can move from ambiguity to a testable approach, from a workshop to an operating routine, and from a promising pilot to an institutionally owned system. The standard is simple: show not only what you know, but what you personally built, changed, tested, learned and left stronger. · Work across public health, supply chain, policy, product, technology and field implementation boundaries. · Turn expertise into usable products, processes, decisions and measurable improvements—not reports alone. · Operate with urgency while preserving quality, public trust, data protection, service continuity and government ownership. Government Partnership and Institutionalization Lead Role purpose Provide authoritative technical leadership on vaccine forecasting, allocation, storage, distribution, cold chain, wastage, accountability and the connection between vaccine availability and immunization service delivery. Key responsibilities · Map vaccine flows, decision rights, information flows and performance bottlenecks from national level to service-delivery points. · Define functional requirements for vaccine receipts, issues, adjustments, stock counts, batch and expiry tracking, temperature events and outreach allocation. · Ensure that digital workflows support forecasting, replenishment, redistribution, new vaccine introduction and immunization microplanning. · Specify indicators and business rules for stock availability, wastage, expiry, cold-chain excursions, emergency resupply and session readiness. · Work with product and technical teams to validate data models, workflows, alerts and decision-support logic. · Support pilot-site selection, baseline assessment, training, supportive supervision and performance reviews. · Facilitate coordination among EPI, supply-chain agencies, cold-chain functions, regional bureaus, woredas and facilities. · Document and test SOPs and accountability mechanisms for responding to vaccine-supply risks. · Support evaluation, interpretation of findings, national learning and scale-up recommendations. Expected results · Validated vaccine supply-chain workflows and digital requirements. · Improved visibility of vaccine stock, batch, expiry, wastage and cold-chain risks in pilot areas. · Documented evidence that data are used for allocation, replenishment, redistribution and service planning. · Vaccine-management SOPs and competency-development materials integrated into routine practice.

About Opian

Opian is an Ethiopian health-technology and innovation company building decision infrastructure for stronger health systems. We combine deep knowledge of how care and supply chains operate, human-centred product design, data engineering and responsible artificial intelligence. Our work helps health workers, managers and public institutions turn fragmented data into timely decisions—so essential medicines, vaccines and services are available where and when people need them.

Our philosophy

We believe useful innovation is not novelty for its own sake. It is the disciplined work of understanding a real problem, challenging assumptions, building and testing a better response, measuring what changes, and strengthening the institutions that must sustain the result. Technology is valuable only when it improves a decision, a workflow or an outcome in the real operating environment.

· Start with reality: design around the health workers, workloads, incentives, infrastructure and constraints that actually exist—not an imported ideal workflow.

· Build with people, not for them: government counterparts and frontline users are co-designers, decision-makers and eventual owners, not passive recipients.

· Strengthen the system, not a standalone application: connect workflows, data, institutions and incentives so information can lead to action across every level.

· Push boundaries responsibly: make ambitious but testable bets, protect safety and privacy, and change direction quickly when evidence contradicts the original idea.

· Make capability local and durable: transfer knowledge, product ownership and operational responsibility so progress continues without permanent dependence on an external project team.

· Be honest about impact: distinguish deployment from adoption and activity from results; make claims specific, measurable and open to verification.

What this means for candidates

Opian is looking for accomplished specialists who are also builders. Candidates should bring exceptional depth in their discipline, intellectual courage, practical judgment and the humility to learn from users and evidence. We value people who can move from ambiguity to a testable approach, from a workshop to an operating routine, and from a promising pilot to an institutionally owned system. The standard is simple: show not only what you know, but what you personally built, changed, tested, learned and left stronger.

· Work across public health, supply chain, policy, product, technology and field implementation boundaries.

· Turn expertise into usable products, processes, decisions and measurable improvements—not reports alone.

· Operate with urgency while preserving quality, public trust, data protection, service continuity and government ownership.

Government Partnership and Institutionalization Lead

Role purpose

Provide authoritative technical leadership on vaccine forecasting, allocation, storage, distribution, cold chain, wastage, accountability and the connection between vaccine availability and immunization service delivery.

Key responsibilities

· Map vaccine flows, decision rights, information flows and performance bottlenecks from national level to service-delivery points.

· Define functional requirements for vaccine receipts, issues, adjustments, stock counts, batch and expiry tracking, temperature events and outreach allocation.

· Ensure that digital workflows support forecasting, replenishment, redistribution, new vaccine introduction and immunization microplanning.

· Specify indicators and business rules for stock availability, wastage, expiry, cold-chain excursions, emergency resupply and session readiness.

· Work with product and technical teams to validate data models, workflows, alerts and decision-support logic.

· Support pilot-site selection, baseline assessment, training, supportive supervision and performance reviews.

· Facilitate coordination among EPI, supply-chain agencies, cold-chain functions, regional bureaus, woredas and facilities.

· Document and test SOPs and accountability mechanisms for responding to vaccine-supply risks.

· Support evaluation, interpretation of findings, national learning and scale-up recommendations.

Expected results

· Validated vaccine supply-chain workflows and digital requirements.

· Improved visibility of vaccine stock, batch, expiry, wastage and cold-chain risks in pilot areas.

· Documented evidence that data are used for allocation, replenishment, redistribution and service planning.

· Vaccine-management SOPs and competency-development materials integrated into routine practice.

company.description:
About the company

Teklehaimanot General Hospital is a patient-centered private hospital in the center of Addis Ababa that provides trusted multi-disciplinary medical services. With a focus on quality and customer care, it has a distinctive, compassionate, and honest approach to serving the need of all patients. Devised with experienced and compassionate medical staff, TGH is a health coach and medical partner to cater to all medical care needs. “An earnest deed is worth more than silver and gold” so fairness in price, quality, and flexibility creates a shelter for hope and recovery.
Through decades of unwavering endeavor to be a patient-centered private hospital, TGH is proud to offer over 70 General, specialty, subspecialty, and supportive services with 402 dedicated staff, of which 329 are full-time employees and 73 are part-time and contractual employees equipped with a culture of medical teamwork. Its credit program serves over 100 companies, Local and international companies, sharing in the grandeur of full hospitality that builds lasting patient-to-care provider relationships. For seven consecutive years, TGH has been ranked “Green Level” general hospital.

Our Mission

  • To be among the premium and most preferred healthcare providers in East Africa

Our Vision

  • To provide quality health care services at a reasonable price 

Our Values

“To nurture all human beings principled in honesty through compassion with the utmost respect”
TGH, with a strong commitment to nurturing all human beings, upholds the principles of honesty, compassion, and utmost respect. Through its unwavering dedication to providing exceptional healthcare services, The Hospital strives to become a trusted institution, a place where patients find solace, comfort, and the promise of a brighter future.
At Teklehaimanot General Hospital the core value of “nurturing all human beings’’ resonates throughout every aspect of the organization. From the moment patients step through the doors, they are greeted with warmth and empathy. The hospital's dedicated team of healthcare and Customer service professionals understands the critical importance of treating patients not just as medical cases, but as individuals deserving of kindness, compassion, and personalized attention. Every patient is regarded as a unique story, and the hospital's mission is to provide holistic care that addresses both physical and emotional well-being.
“Honesty” is the bedrock upon which Teklehaimanot General Hospital stands. Transparent communication, ethical practices, and integrity are the guiding principles that shape every interaction within the hospital. Patients and their families can trust that they will receive accurate information about their conditions, treatment options, and the overall care process. The hospital's commitment to honesty ensures that patients are empowered to make informed decisions and actively participate in their healthcare journey.
“Compassion” is the lifeblood that flows through the veins of Teklehaimanot General Hospital. The hospital's healthcare professionals are not only highly skilled and knowledgeable but also deeply empathetic and understanding. They recognize that patients may be experiencing fear, pain, or uncertainty and go above and beyond to provide comfort and support. Whether it's holding a hand, offering a listening ear, or providing words of encouragement, the hospital's staff is devoted to fostering an environment that promotes healing and emotional well-being.
Above all, Teklehaimanot General Hospital treats every individual with “utmost respect”. Regardless of age, gender, socioeconomic status, or background, every patient is valued and treated with dignity. The hospital's commitment to respect extends to its commitment to cultural sensitivity and inclusivity. The diverse needs and beliefs of patients are honored, and efforts are made to create an environment that is welcoming and accommodating to all.

Why work for us

Choosing to work for Teklehaimanot General Hospital means joining a healthcare institution that values its employees, patients, and the community at large. We provide an environment that fosters professional growth, collaboration, and innovation, while emphasizing the importance of delivering exceptional patient care. With our commitment to excellence, cutting-edge facilities, and a supportive work culture, Teklehaimanot General Hospital offers a fulfilling and rewarding career path for healthcare professionals seeking to make a difference.  The following facts highlight the numerous benefits and opportunities that await prospective candidates who choose TGH.
1. Commitment to Patient Care:
At Teklehaimanot General Hospital, our primary focus is on delivering high-quality patient care. Our employees are driven by a shared mission to make a positive impact on the lives of individuals and their families. By working with us, you will have the opportunity to contribute to the well-being of the community and play a crucial role in saving lives and improving health outcomes.
2. Collaborative and Supportive Work Environment:
We foster a collaborative and supportive work environment that encourages teamwork, communication, and professional growth. Our hospital values the contributions of each employee and believes in a culture of respect, inclusivity, and continuous learning. You will have the chance to work alongside skilled professionals from diverse backgrounds, creating a stimulating and enriching atmosphere that allows for personal and career development.
3. Opportunities for Professional Development:
We believe in investing in our employees' growth and development. Teklehaimanot General Hospital offers a range of opportunities for professional advancement, including ongoing training programs, workshops, conferences, and mentorship initiatives. We encourage our employees to expand their knowledge and skills, fostering a culture of continuous professional development that supports career progression within the organization.
4. Competitive Compensation and Benefits:
We understand the importance of recognizing and rewarding our employees' hard work and dedication. Teklehaimanot General Hospital offers competitive compensation packages that are commensurate with industry standards, ensuring that employees feel valued and motivated. Additionally, we strictly adhere to privilege package that are stated on Ethiopian labor law.
5. Ethical and Transparent Practices:
As an organization, we prioritize ethical conduct and maintain transparency in our operations. Teklehaimanot General Hospital upholds the highest standards of integrity, ensuring that our employees work in an environment built on trust, honesty, and accountability. We are committed to maintaining a positive reputation and upholding the trust placed in us by our patients and the community.

Team Benefits

Teklehaimanot General Hospital has implemented a comprehensive range of employee benefits aimed at promoting employee well-being and job satisfaction. This write-up will explore the various employer benefits offered by Teklehaimanot General Hospital:
  • Partial medical coverage (including family)
  • Attractive Remuneration
  • Allowances (transportation, representation, and others)
  • Service charge
  • Successive training programs that are tailored to enrich professional, leadership and self-development skills of candidates.

fields.title: Senior Project Manager
fields.description: Ipas is a non-profit organization working to improve women’s lives by focusing on improving access to information and services to basic sexual and reproductive health across the globe. Since the year 2000, Ipas Ethiopia has been collaborating with the Ministry of Health (MOH), Regional Health Bureaus (RHBs), Community Based Organizations (CBOs) and various local and international partners to reduce maternal mortality and morbidity resulting from unwanted pregnancy and unsafe abortion. In light of the need to strengthen our relationship with stakeholders and expedite program implementation, we are planning to hire for the following position: Job Title : Senior Project Manager Place of Work : Addis Ababa Report to: Country Director Position Type: Full-time Grade : Expert Terms of Employment: One year with possibilities for extension Salary : Negotiable Position Purpose and Summary of Responsibilities The Senior Project Manager (SPM) develops and implements strategies and work plans related to the project entitled “Reducing unsafe abortion by up to half in Ethiopia” project to ensure that the overall goals and objectives of the project are met. The SPM is responsible for planning and managing the implementation and execution of activities under the project following the agreement entered with the donor and Ministry of Health, which include community education, meaningful engagement of the youth, girls, women and other community members, ensuring women have access to CAC and family planning information and services in the project areas etc. S/he provides technical guidance to staff involved in the implementation of the project activities to ensure that service delivery objectives are met, including training in abortion care and family planning, ensuring the quality of services, avail intended services to target groups that include urban and rural women, adolescent and youth girls, women with disabilities and SGBV survivors. The position will provide leadership and strategic direction to regional team leaders; community engagement advisor, plan and coordinate technical inputs and supervise staff and consultants. This position works closely with the Country Director. S/he will also work closely with all team members in planning, implementing and assessing activities aimed at achieving country program goals/objectives. Specific Responsibilities Project Planning & Management: The SPM provides leadership for planning and effective implementation of the project at the national level. Responsible for integrating and leading activities of the various thematic areas and develop comprehensive annual work plans, work with finance manager to develop budgets, schedules, identifying and monitoring resources to ensure the overall project implementation is on track. Responsible for coordinating the execution of project activities and budget utilization and reporting towards objectives and results. Will work closely with the CD in the case of any needed project realignments or revised strategies. Represent the project team, contribute to the overall country program decisions, compliance/risk mitigation, and participate in business development activities. Service Delivery Results: Work with appropriate staff and consultants, collaborating with government officials and private partners, to ensure that annual work plans are met, including: of women in the different categories received information and services; Design effective and cost-effective training modalities; of providers trained; of sites providing CAC/CC services which includes the introduction and roll out of self-care; of CAC and CC clients served; Availability of equipment and supplies; and Ensure quality of care systems are in place. Work with appropriate staff and consultants to produce and implement required training, community education, and development of IEC and other technical materials as required. Supervision : Supervise the work of staff and consultants under the project and provide them with adequate support and guidance including mentoring, development of annual plans, monitoring of progress and review of performance periodically, and sharing constructive feedback. Documentation : Work with CD and Research, Monitoring and Evaluation (RM&E) unit to develop indicators and reporting systemsto enable collection of required data to monitor and document the process and impact of interventions. Ensure Ipas Global monitoring and tracking systems are in place and implemented at project sites. Work closely with the country RM&E team to ensure accuracy and reporting of data.
