raw_data.title: Senior Project Manager
raw_data.description:
Ipas is a non-profit organization working to improve women’s lives by focusing on improving access to information and services to basic sexual and reproductive health across the globe. Since the year 2000, Ipas Ethiopia has been collaborating with the Ministry of Health (MOH), Regional Health Bureaus (RHBs), Community Based Organizations (CBOs) and various local and international partners to reduce maternal mortality and morbidity resulting from unwanted pregnancy and unsafe abortion.

In light of the need to strengthen our relationship with stakeholders and expedite program implementation, we are planning to hire for the following position:

Job Title: Senior Project Manager

Place of Work: Addis Ababa

Report to: Country Director

Position Type: Full-time

Grade: Expert

Terms of Employment: One year with possibilities for extension

Salary: Negotiable

  1. Position Purpose and Summary of Responsibilities The Senior Project Manager (SPM) develops and implements strategies and work plans related to the project entitled “Reducing unsafe abortion by up to half in Ethiopia” project to ensure that the overall goals and objectives of the project are met. The SPM is responsible for planning and managing the implementation and execution of activities under the project following the agreement entered with the donor and Ministry of Health, which include community education, meaningful engagement of the youth, girls, women and other community members, ensuring women have access to CAC and family planning information and services in the project areas etc. S/he provides technical guidance to staff involved in the implementation of the project activities to ensure that service delivery objectives are met, including training in abortion care and family planning, ensuring the quality of services, avail intended services to target groups that include urban and rural women, adolescent and youth girls, women with disabilities and SGBV survivors. The position will provide leadership and strategic direction to regional team leaders; community engagement advisor, plan and coordinate technical inputs and supervise staff and consultants. This position works closely with the Country Director. S/he will also work closely with all team members in planning, implementing and assessing activities aimed at achieving country program goals/objectives.
  2. Specific Responsibilities

Project Planning & Management:

  • The SPM provides leadership for planning and effective implementation of the project at the national level.
  • Responsible for integrating and leading activities of the various thematic areas and develop comprehensive annual work plans, work with finance manager to develop budgets, schedules, identifying and monitoring resources to ensure the overall project implementation is on track.
  • Responsible for coordinating the execution of project activities and budget utilization and reporting towards objectives and results.
  • Will work closely with the CD in the case of any needed project realignments or revised strategies.
  • Represent the project team, contribute to the overall country program decisions, compliance/risk mitigation, and participate in business development activities.

Work with appropriate staff and consultants, collaborating with government officials and private partners, to ensure that annual work plans are met, including:

      of providers trained;

fields.title: Request for Proposals (RFP) for Development of a Training Curriculum: "Budgeting for Equity: A Practical Guide for Addis Ababa"
fields.description: 1. Background The Center for Budgetary Governance Advocacy (CBGA) is a local civil society organization based in Addis Ababa working on fiscal transparency and gender-responsive budgeting. Under its project “Advancing Gender Equity and Transparency in Budgetary Governance in Addis Ababa,” funded by Christian Aid/EU CSF+, CBGA works with sub-city administrations, sector offices and partner civil society organizations to strengthen gender-responsive and transparent budget practices in Addis Ababa. CBGA has identified a need for a stand-alone, practical training resource that sub-city and woreda finance officers, sector office staff and civil society practitioners can use to apply gender-responsive and equity-focused budgeting in their day-to-day work. CBGA therefore invites proposals from qualified individual consultants or firms to design and develop a training curriculum titled “Budgeting for Equity: A Practical Guide for Addis Ababa.” 2. Objective and Scope of Work Objective: To develop a practical, field-ready training curriculum that builds the capacity of government finance staff, sector office focal persons and civil society practitioners in Addis Ababa to plan, analyze and monitor budgets through a gender-equity lens. The assignment includes: • Review of CBGA’s existing project materials, gender budget scorecard tools, and the relevant Ethiopian budget policy and legal framework (federal and Addis Ababa City Administration) to ground the curriculum in the local context. • Design of the curriculum structure: learning objectives, modules/sessions, sequencing, and estimated time per session, suitable for a short, practitioner-oriented training (not an academic course). • Development of a facilitator’s guide and a participant handbook (the “Practical Guide”), written in plain, accessible language for non-specialist budget officers. • Development of practical tools and job aids - checklists, worksheets, templates and at least two Addis Ababa-based case studies or scenarios - that participants can apply directly in their offices. • Use of a participatory, adult-learning methodology (exercises, group work, worked examples) rather than a lecture-only format. • Production of the final curriculum (facilitator’s guide and participant handbook) in English. • Translation of the training manual (participant handbook) into Amharic and Afaan Oromo, reviewed for accuracy and consistent budgeting/technical terminology. • Production of an audio version of the training manual in Amharic, suitable for participants with limited literacy or as a self-study/refresher aid. • Incorporation of feedback from a review/validation session with CBGA and other stakeholders before finalization. 3. Deliverables and Timeline Deliverable Description 1. Inception Note Brief methodology, proposed curriculum outline and workplan 2. Draft Curriculum Full draft facilitator’s guide, participant handbook and training tools (English), submitted for CBGA review. 3. Validation Session Consultant presents the draft to CBGA (and selected sub-city/sector office representatives) and incorporates feedback. 4. Final Curriculum Package Finalized facilitator’s guide, participant handbook, slide deck and tools/templates, in English, in editable and print-ready formats. 5. Translated Manuals Participant handbook translated into Amharic and Afaan Oromo, reviewed for accuracy and consistent terminology. 6. Audio Version (Amharic) Narrated audio recording(s) of the Amharic training manual, in a standard audio format (e.g., MP3), structured to follow the manual’s sessions. 7. Handover All source files (English, Amharic, Afaan Oromo, and audio), references used, and a short user note on how to adapt the curriculum for future cohorts. Total assignment duration: 4 weeks from contract signing.

fields.title: Refugee Education Transition Advisor
fields.description: GIZ- Internal/External Vacancy Announcement Project office- The Global Programme Refugee Inclusion Accelerator (RISE) Contract duration-31.03.2028 Note: Please note that the position title will be changed to Advisor during the recruitment process Brief Description of the Project The Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH has been working in Ethiopia for more than 50 years on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and other international partners. GIZ supports the Government of Ethiopia in strengthening public institutions and promoting inclusive and sustainable development. The Global Programme Refugee Inclusion Accelerator (RISE) and the planned Joint Project with the UNHCR “ Supporting the Inclusion of Displaced Persons and Host Communities in Ethiopia ” are commissioned under BMZ's Special Initiative on Displaced Persons and Host Countries. Both projects support the Government of Ethiopia in implementing the Makatet Roadmap and advancing the inclusion of refugees into national systems. As part of this commitment, the Government of Ethiopia is leading the gradual transition of refugee schools from humanitarian management into the national education system. This is a complex reform process requiring strengthened institutional capacities, effective coordination among national, regional and international stakeholders, and the development of sustainable systems and approaches to support implementation. The Government is supported in this process through substantial financial support from the World Bank. This position will initially be established under RISE and, subject to commissioning, is intended to transition to the Joint Project with UNHCR to ensure continuity of technical support throughout the education transition process. The Advisor provides technical advisory services to the Ministry of Education while leading the implementation of GIZ's technical support for the education transition, with a particular focus on national coordination and implementation in Benishangul-Gumuz Regional State (BGRS). Main Activities: The Advisor provides technical advisory services to the Ministry of Education and other relevant government institutions and leads the design, coordination and implementation of GIZ's technical assistance for the education transition. The Advisor is responsible for the following tasks: Provide strategic technical advisory to the Ministry of Education, the BGRS-Bureau of Education, the Refugees and Returnees Service (RRS) and other relevant government partners on the implementation of the refugee education transition in line with the Makatet Roadmap, including the strengthening of institutional coordination, governance and implementation arrangements. Support government-led systems development by facilitating the development of institutional frameworks, policy recommendations, operational guidelines and practical tools for integrating refugee education into national planning, budgeting, monitoring, quality assurance and other government systems. Coordinate technical assistance provided through the project, including national and international consultants, and ensure the quality and timely delivery of technical studies, assessments, technical concepts, policy recommendations and other knowledge products supporting government decision-making. Lead institutional readiness assessments and capacity development in BGRS by coordinating school, woreda and institutional assessments, analysing findings together with government partners, and designing and supporting the implementation of capacity development measures, including training programmes, technical workshops, coaching, peer learning and on-the-job advisory support. Lead the development of sustainable qualification pathways for refugee incentive teachers together with the Ministry of Education, teacher education institutions and relevant accreditation authorities, including accredited upgrading programmes, Recognition of Prior Learning approaches and other mechanisms supporting future integration into Ethiopia's public education system. Facilitate coordination and partnership among relevant government institutions, development partners and humanitarian actors by supporting technical working groups and other coordination mechanisms under the Makatet Roadmap and ensuring effective collaboration throughout the education transition process. Ensure quality, learning and cross-cutting integration by mainstreaming gender equality, protection and social cohesion across all technical interventions, documenting lessons learned and good practices, and preparing technical concepts, policy papers, implementation guidelines, briefing notes and reports. Duty travel to BGRS and other refugee hosting areas required

fields.description: የረዳት ግዥ ሰራተኛ ስራ ኃላፊነት፤ የግዥ ሂደትንና አሰራርን በመተግበር መስራት የምትችል፣ አቅራቢዎች የመምረጥና ግዥ በወቅቱ ተግዝቶ እንዲቀርብ ከዋና ግዥ ባለሙያ ጋር በመሆን መስራት የምትችል፣ የግዥ ሂደቶችን ሙሉ በሙሉ በመጠበቅና ህጎችን በማክበር ግዥ መፈጸምና በማገዝ መስራት የምትችል፣ የግዥ ዋጋዎችንና የክፍያ ሁኔታዎችን ከአቅራቢዎች ዋጋዎችን በመውሰድና ግዥ የሚፈጸመዉን ማንኛዉንም ንብረት ጥራትና ዋጋ በማወዳደር ግዥ እንዲገዛ ሲጸድቅ ግዥ የመፈጸምና ለሚመለከተዉ የንብረት ክፍል አንድ በአንድ ቆጥሮ በማስረከብ መስራትና በዚህም የስራ ልምድ ያላት፣ የግዥ ሰነዶችን አደራጅቶ መዝግብ ላይ መዝጎ የመያዝ እና ግዥ የተፈጸመባቸዉን ሰነዶች ለሚመለከተዉ ፋይናንስ ክፍልና ንብረት ክፍል በወቅቱ እንዲወራረድ አድርጎ የመስራት(የስራ ልምድ ያለዉ)፣ የግዥ ስራዉን በእቅድ መስራት የምትችል፣ ከንብረት ፣ ከፋይናንስና ከሌሎች የስራ ክፍሎች ጋራ በመናበብና በመተባበር መስራት የምትችል፣ የግዥ መመሪያና ደንቦችን አዉቃ መስራት የምትችል፣ የግዥ ቀደም ተከተል በመከተል እና በማስፈጸም እለት በእለት ክትትል በማድረግ መስራት የምትችል፣ ግዥ የተጠየቁ ማንኛዉም ቁሳቁስ በተፈለገዉ ቀንና ሰዓት ተገዝቶ እንዲገባ ከሚመለከተዉ ክፍል ጋር በመናበብ በማስፈጸም መስራት የምትችል፣ ፈጣን የሆነች እና በቀላሉ ከአቅራቢዎችና ከባለሙያዎች ጋር መግባባት የምትችል፣ የግዥ ክፍል ስራዎች በእለት ፣ በሳምንትና በወር የተሰሩ ስራዎችንና የስራ ሂደቶችን በማጠቃለል ሪፖርት ሰርታ ማቅረብ የምትችል፣ የስራ ልምድ ፤ በፈርኒቸር ስራዎች ድርጅት ዉስጥ በግዥ ወይም በረዳት ግዥ ከ1 ዓመት በላይ የሰራች፣ መሟላት ያለባቸዉ መስፈርቶች፤ ፈጣን እና በቀላሉ መግባባት የምትችል(የመግባባት ችሎታ ያላት)፣ የግዥ አፈጻጸሞችን እና ሂደቶችን የምታዉቅ፣ ከንብረት ክፍልና ከፋይናንስ ክፍል ጋር ምን ምን የስራ ግንኙነት እዳላቸዉ ጠንቅቃ የምታዉቅ፣ የስራ ልምድ ማቅረብ የምትችል፣ በመጀመሪያ ዲግሪ in Supply Management, Logistics & Supply Chain Management, Business Administration,Accounting Or related field ጥሩ የመረጃ አያያዝ ችሎታ ያላት፣ የኮፒዉተር ችሎታ ያላት(MS Office, Excel & ERP) etc. የመኖሪያ ቦታቸዉ ለጃክሮስ ቅርብ የሆች ቢሆን ይመረጣል፣ የሚሰጠዉን ፈተና ካለፈች በኋላ ዋስ/ተያዥ ማቅረብ የምትችል፣ ደመወዝ ፦ በስምምነት ብዛት ፦ ሁለት(2) ጾታ ፦ ሴት የስራ ሰዓት ፦ ከሰኞ እስከ ቅዳሜ ከ2፡00 እስከ 11፡00 ሰዓት የቅጥር ሁኔታ ፦ ከ60 ቀን በኋላ በቋሚነት

raw_data.title: ረዳት ግዥ ሰራተኛ
raw_data.description:
የረዳት ግዥ ሰራተኛ ስራ ኃላፊነት፤

  • የግዥ ሂደትንና አሰራርን በመተግበር መስራት የምትችል፣

  • አቅራቢዎች የመምረጥና ግዥ በወቅቱ ተግዝቶ እንዲቀርብ ከዋና ግዥ ባለሙያ ጋር በመሆን መስራት የምትችል፣

  • የግዥ ሂደቶችን ሙሉ በሙሉ በመጠበቅና ህጎችን በማክበር ግዥ መፈጸምና በማገዝ መስራት የምትችል፣

  •  የግዥ ዋጋዎችንና የክፍያ ሁኔታዎችን ከአቅራቢዎች ዋጋዎችን በመውሰድና ግዥ የሚፈጸመዉን ማንኛዉንም ንብረት ጥራትና ዋጋ በማወዳደር ግዥ እንዲገዛ ሲጸድቅ ግዥ የመፈጸምና ለሚመለከተዉ የንብረት ክፍል አንድ በአንድ ቆጥሮ በማስረከብ መስራትና በዚህም የስራ ልምድ ያላት፣

  •  የግዥ ሰነዶችን አደራጅቶ መዝግብ ላይ መዝጎ የመያዝ እና ግዥ የተፈጸመባቸዉን ሰነዶች ለሚመለከተዉ ፋይናንስ ክፍልና ንብረት ክፍል በወቅቱ እንዲወራረድ አድርጎ የመስራት(የስራ ልምድ ያለዉ)፣

  •  የግዥ ስራዉን በእቅድ መስራት የምትችል፣

  • ከንብረት ፣ ከፋይናንስና ከሌሎች የስራ ክፍሎች ጋራ በመናበብና በመተባበር መስራት የምትችል፣

  • የግዥ መመሪያና ደንቦችን አዉቃ መስራት የምትችል፣

  •  የግዥ ቀደም ተከተል በመከተል እና በማስፈጸም እለት በእለት ክትትል በማድረግ መስራት የምትችል፣

  •  ግዥ የተጠየቁ ማንኛዉም ቁሳቁስ በተፈለገዉ ቀንና ሰዓት ተገዝቶ እንዲገባ ከሚመለከተዉ ክፍል ጋር በመናበብ በማስፈጸም መስራት የምትችል፣

  •  ፈጣን የሆነች እና በቀላሉ ከአቅራቢዎችና ከባለሙያዎች ጋር መግባባት የምትችል፣

  •  የግዥ ክፍል ስራዎች በእለት ፣ በሳምንትና በወር የተሰሩ ስራዎችንና የስራ ሂደቶችን በማጠቃለል ሪፖርት ሰርታ ማቅረብ የምትችል፣

የስራ ልምድ  ፤

  •  በፈርኒቸር ስራዎች ድርጅት ዉስጥ በግዥ ወይም በረዳት ግዥ ከ1 ዓመት በላይ የሰራች፣

መሟላት ያለባቸዉ መስፈርቶች፤

  •  ፈጣን እና በቀላሉ መግባባት የምትችል(የመግባባት ችሎታ ያላት)፣

  •  የግዥ አፈጻጸሞችን እና ሂደቶችን የምታዉቅ፣

  •  ከንብረት ክፍልና ከፋይናንስ ክፍል ጋር ምን ምን የስራ ግንኙነት እዳላቸዉ ጠንቅቃ የምታዉቅ፣

  •  የስራ ልምድ ማቅረብ የምትችል፣

  •  በመጀመሪያ ዲግሪ in Supply Management, Logistics & Supply Chain Management, Business Administration,Accounting Or related field

  • ጥሩ የመረጃ አያያዝ ችሎታ ያላት፣

  • የኮፒዉተር ችሎታ ያላት(MS Office, Excel & ERP) etc.

  •  የመኖሪያ ቦታቸዉ ለጃክሮስ ቅርብ የሆች ቢሆን ይመረጣል፣

  •  የሚሰጠዉን ፈተና ካለፈች በኋላ ዋስ/ተያዥ ማቅረብ የምትችል፣

  • ደመወዝ፦ በስምምነት

  •  ብዛት፦ ሁለት(2)

  •  ጾታ ፦ ሴት

  •  የስራ ሰዓት፦ ከሰኞ እስከ ቅዳሜ ከ2፡00 እስከ 11፡00 ሰዓት

  •  የቅጥር ሁኔታ፦ ከ60 ቀን በኋላ በቋሚነት

fields.title: Operation Manager
fields.description: About Us Ethio-BioPharma Enterprise (EBPE) is Ethiopia’s state-owned pharmaceutical manufacturing enterprise, established to build the nation’s capacity to manufacture vaccines, essential medicines, diagnostics, medical supplies and other healthcare technologies locally. Operating under EIH, EBPE is developing an integrated pharmaceutical campus at the Kilinto Special Economic Zone in Addis Ababa, co-locating multiple manufacturing units that share infrastructure, talent, and corporate services. Job Summary I. GENERAL POSITION DESCRIPTION Main Purpose of the post The Operations Manager is responsible for leading the design, installation, and testing of all technical and digital systems. This role ensures that the construction of manufacturing plants for Vaccines, Pharmaceuticals, Diagnostics, and Medical Supplies meets all engineering codes and international regulatory standards (EFDA and WHO-GMP). The manager is accountable for making sure all machinery, utility systems (water, air, power, and specialized gases), Building Management Systems (BMS), and IT networks are properly set up, validated, and ready for full-scale production. II. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES / ACCOUNTABILITY A. Engineering, Facility Construction and Utility Installation Lead the review and approval of engineering designs, drawings, P&IDs, equipment layouts, utility layouts, and technical specifications to ensure compliance with project requirements, engineering standards, and WHO-GMP requirements. Manage the planning, installation, and commissioning of mechanical utility systems including HVAC, Water for Injection (WFI), Purified Water (PW), Pure Steam, Clean Compressed Air, Process Gases, Vacuum, Chilled Water, Plant Steam, and associated piping systems. Oversee the construction and installation of process utilities, environmental systems, drainage networks, Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP), fire protection systems, and other building services while coordinating civil, structural, and electrical interfaces. Coordinate and supervise contractors, consultants, and equipment suppliers to ensure construction, equipment installation, and utility works are executed in accordance with approved drawings, specifications, project schedules, quality standards, and contract requirements. Review construction materials, fabrication methods, welding procedures, pressure testing, equipment installation, and utility system testing to ensure compliance with applicable engineering and pharmaceutical standards. Ensure all mechanical, electrical, civil, plumbing, automation, and utility installations comply with Ethiopian regulations, international engineering standards, EFDA requirements, WHO-GMP guidelines, and health, safety, and environmental requirements. B. Automation, Electrical and Information Systems Coordinate the installation and integration of electrical distribution systems, Building Management Systems (BMS), Environmental Monitoring Systems (EMS), automation, PLC/SCADA systems, and IT infrastructure. Oversee the implementation of enterprise IT infrastructure, server rooms, communication networks, ERP integration, and data management systems required to support facility operations. Ensure cybersecurity, data integrity, backup systems, and computerized infrastructure comply with applicable regulatory and operational requirements. C. Equipment Testing and Validation Acceptance Testing: Lead the Factory Acceptance Tests (FAT) at supplier locations and Site Acceptance Tests (SAT) once machinery arrives at the plant to verify they work as ordered. Equipment Qualification: Manage the formal process of Installation Qualification (IQ) and Operational Qualification (OQ) to prove that all machines and utilities are installed and functioning correctly. Calibration Management: Set up a Metrology system to calibrate all measuring instruments (scales, thermometers, pressure gauges, and gas flow meters) to ensure they provide accurate readings traceable to international standards. D. Operational Planning and Staffing Develop engineering SOPs, preventive maintenance strategies, operating manuals, and engineering documentation required for facility operation. Plan spare parts, maintenance tools, engineering consumables, and utility operation requirements to support reliable plant operation. Lead and mentor engineering personnel while coordinating the activities of contractors, consultants, equipment vendors, and cross-functional teams throughout project implementation. III. Authority The Operations Manager is authorized to: 1. Approve or reject technical designs, equipment specifications, and completed installation work. 2.Stop any construction or installation activity that does not meet the specified technical or quality standards. 3.Direct external contractors on-site regarding technical requirements and timelines. 4.Sign off on technical milestones before payments are released to vendors or contractors. 5.Recommend engineering changes and corrective actions to improve project performance, safety, quality, and operational readiness. Effort required Mental Focus: Requires sustained concentration to interpret complex technical blueprints, verify mathematical calculations, and troubleshoot mechanical or software failures. Physical Presence: Requires regular and active presence on construction sites, which involves walking through unfinished structures, climbing ladders for inspections, and standing for long periods during equipment testing. Environment: Work involves exposure to construction site conditions (dust, noise) and eventually working in strictly controlled sterile cleanrooms. Time Demand: Often requires working beyond standard office hours to meet project deadlines or to coordinate with international equipment suppliers in different time zones. The Operations Manager is expected to carry out other related tasks as assigned by pertinent authority Reports to: This positions reports to the CEO Salary: As per the Organization's Scale

  6. Ensure all mechanical, electrical, civil, plumbing, automation, and utility installations comply with Ethiopian regulations, international engineering standards, EFDA requirements, WHO-GMP guidelines, and health, safety, and environmental requirements.

B. Automation, Electrical and Information Systems

  1. Coordinate the installation and integration of electrical distribution systems, Building Management Systems (BMS), Environmental Monitoring Systems (EMS), automation, PLC/SCADA systems, and IT infrastructure.
  2. Oversee the implementation of enterprise IT infrastructure, server rooms, communication networks, ERP integration, and data management systems required to support facility operations.
  3. Ensure cybersecurity, data integrity, backup systems, and computerized infrastructure comply with applicable regulatory and operational requirements.

C. Equipment Testing and Validation

  1. Acceptance Testing: Lead the Factory Acceptance Tests (FAT) at supplier locations and Site Acceptance Tests (SAT) once machinery arrives at the plant to verify they work as ordered.
  2. Equipment Qualification: Manage the formal process of Installation Qualification (IQ) and Operational Qualification (OQ) to prove that all machines and utilities are installed and functioning correctly.
  3. Calibration Management: Set up a Metrology system to calibrate all measuring instruments (scales, thermometers, pressure gauges, and gas flow meters) to ensure they provide accurate readings traceable to international standards.

D. Operational Planning and Staffing

  1. Develop engineering SOPs, preventive maintenance strategies, operating manuals, and engineering documentation required for facility operation.
  2. Plan spare parts, maintenance tools, engineering consumables, and utility operation requirements to support reliable plant operation.
  3. Lead and mentor engineering personnel while coordinating the activities of contractors, consultants, equipment vendors, and cross-functional teams throughout project implementation.

III. Authority

The Operations Manager is authorized to:

1. Approve or reject technical designs, equipment specifications, and completed installation work.

2.Stop any construction or installation activity that does not meet the specified technical or quality standards.

3.Direct external contractors on-site regarding technical requirements and timelines.

4.Sign off on technical milestones before payments are released to vendors or contractors.

5.Recommend engineering changes and corrective actions to improve project performance, safety, quality, and operational readiness.

Effort required

  1. Mental Focus: Requires sustained concentration to interpret complex technical blueprints, verify mathematical calculations, and troubleshoot mechanical or software failures.
  2. Physical Presence: Requires regular and active presence on construction sites, which involves walking through unfinished structures, climbing ladders for inspections, and standing for long periods during equipment testing.
  3. Environment: Work involves exposure to construction site conditions (dust, noise) and eventually working in strictly controlled sterile cleanrooms.
  4. Time Demand: Often requires working beyond standard office hours to meet project deadlines or to coordinate with international equipment suppliers in different time zones.

The Operations Manager is expected to carry out other related tasks as assigned by pertinent authority

Reports to: This positions reports to the CEO

Salary: As per the Organization's Scale

company.name: Hope Enterprise’s University College
company.description:
Hope Enterprises or Hope is a local NGO that was established in 1971 in Addis Ababa to help the needy help themselves through basic needs, education, competence, job and business mediation and value education. As Hope was completing its 32 years of humanitarian service in 2003, it’s then Executive Director, Dr. Minas Hiruy, recommended to the Board the establishment of an outstanding liberal arts university college by submitting a full-fledged proposal. After some discussion, the Board and the General Assembly of Hope accepted the proposal, establishing Hope University College as the first public benefits institution of higher learning in the country on November 25, 2003.  Soon after, the Board adopted a new structure comprising the Ladders of Hope that subsumed the existing and non-college activities of Hope as one division and Hope University College as another division, opening the way for the university college to operate autonomously.
 

Values

The University College believes in goodwill to humankind and to nature and in the concretization of this concern as a step to making the world a community of hope, justice, peace and progress. The University College holds dear the advancement of liberal education as a means of personal and social transformation and regards the provision of education to all as an important public responsibility.

Vision

The vision of the University College is to contribute to the renewal and transformation of society through knowledge and value based education and graduates who can make a difference using what they had gained in the university college.

Mission

The University College, having a mission to provide aspiring leaders the option of pursuing world-class education without leaving their country and cultural setting, shall enable the development of leaders, who being capable of independent work, problem solving, analysis, innovation and reflection, can make a difference in the development of society and in mutually and sustainably supportive relations between man and nature.

Mission Statement

Developing leadership for a world of hope

fields.description: Job Title: Junior Cupping Officer Department: Quality Control & Sensory Laboratory Location: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia Reports To: Senior Cupping Officer / Quality Control Manager Position Summary The Junior Cupping Officer at Mullege Plc plays a vital role in protecting the company's stellar reputation for coffee quality. In this role, you will support the sensory lab team by preparing, testing, and documenting green and roasted coffee samples destined for international markets. This entry-level position demands high physical precision in lab setup, strict adherence to global specialty coffee protocols, and accurate data logging to ensure only premium-grade coffee is cleared for export. Key Responsibilities & Duties 1. Export Sample Processing & Setup Strict Sample Preparation: Receive incoming green coffee lot samples from washing stations, hulling mills, or suppliers, ensuring perfect identification and zero cross-contamination. Roasting & Grinding Calibration: Roast green coffee samples uniformly to exact standard profiles using laboratory sample roasters. Grind coffee precisely according to Specialty Coffee Association (SCA) protocol. Station Preparation: Set up sensory tables daily with strict portion controls, monitored water temperatures (around 93°C–95°C), specialized cupping spoons, and clean testing bowls. 2. Sensory Evaluation & Quality Assistance Sensory Assessment: Participate in daily cupping panels alongside Senior Cupping Officers to assess aroma, flavor notes, acidity, body, and uniformity. Defect Detection: Perform physical inspections on green coffee beans to count primary/secondary defects and check moisture levels before roasting. Export Grading Support: Assist in sorting and cataloging commercial vs. specialty coffee profiles (e.g., Sidamo, Yirgacheffe, Guji, Jimma) to align with client purchase contracts. 3. Data Management & Documentation Laboratory Logging: Enter physical measurements, moisture content readings, and initial cupping scores into Mullege Plc’s internal database or tracking spreadsheets. Traceability Tracking: Maintain flawless records linking sample numbers to their respective warehouse codes or lot numbers to guarantee total traceability from source to container.

Job Title: Junior Cupping Officer

Department: Quality Control & Sensory Laboratory

Location: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia

Reports To: Senior Cupping Officer / Quality Control Manager

Position Summary

The Junior Cupping Officer at Mullege Plc plays a vital role in protecting the company's stellar reputation for coffee quality. In this role, you will support the sensory lab team by preparing, testing, and documenting green and roasted coffee samples destined for international markets. This entry-level position demands high physical precision in lab setup, strict adherence to global specialty coffee protocols, and accurate data logging to ensure only premium-grade coffee is cleared for export.

Key Responsibilities & Duties

1. Export Sample Processing & Setup

  • Strict Sample Preparation: Receive incoming green coffee lot samples from washing stations, hulling mills, or suppliers, ensuring perfect identification and zero cross-contamination.
  • Roasting & Grinding Calibration: Roast green coffee samples uniformly to exact standard profiles using laboratory sample roasters. Grind coffee precisely according to Specialty Coffee Association (SCA) protocol.
  • Station Preparation: Set up sensory tables daily with strict portion controls, monitored water temperatures (around 93°C–95°C), specialized cupping spoons, and clean testing bowls.

2. Sensory Evaluation & Quality Assistance

  • Sensory Assessment: Participate in daily cupping panels alongside Senior Cupping Officers to assess aroma, flavor notes, acidity, body, and uniformity.
  • Defect Detection: Perform physical inspections on green coffee beans to count primary/secondary defects and check moisture levels before roasting.
  • Export Grading Support: Assist in sorting and cataloging commercial vs. specialty coffee profiles (e.g., Sidamo, Yirgacheffe, Guji, Jimma) to align with client purchase contracts.

3. Data Management & Documentation

  • Laboratory Logging: Enter physical measurements, moisture content readings, and initial cupping scores into Mullege Plc’s internal database or tracking spreadsheets.
  • Traceability Tracking: Maintain flawless records linking sample numbers to their respective warehouse codes or lot numbers to guarantee total traceability from source to container.

company.name: Mullege PLC
company.description:
About Us


Mullege PLC is a prominent coffee exporter in Ethiopia, specializing in green Arabica coffee beans. With over three decades of experience, the company has grown from a small supplier to an internationally recognized exporter, serving clients on four continents. They operate two major plants in Addis Ababa and have a substantial annual production capacity and logistics operations. Additionally, Mullege maintains a state-of-the-art warehouse with a capacity to store over 5,000 tons of coffee. 


Our vision


Mullege's vision is to become an internationally recognized exporter of green coffee beans, driven by a strong foundation, innovative ideas, and dedication. Their mission is to provide the most refined coffee to coffee lovers globally through two processing plants in Addis Ababa and pulping stations across Ethiopia. They also aim to be a recognized freight service provider, as evidenced by their national recognition and significant revenue. 


Our success


Mullege's success story highlights its evolution from a small coffee supplier to a major exporter within three generations. Its commitment to quality control, efficient logistics, and a global reach is key to its success. Mullege has a substantial annual production capacity of 22,000 tons of coffee and a state-of-the-art warehouse. It also owns and operates a fleet of trucks for efficient coffee transportation.

company.name: Mullege PLC
company.description:
About Us


Mullege PLC is a prominent coffee exporter in Ethiopia, specializing in green Arabica coffee beans. With over three decades of experience, the company has grown from a small supplier to an internationally recognized exporter, serving clients on four continents. They operate two major plants in Addis Ababa and have a substantial annual production capacity and logistics operations. Additionally, Mullege maintains a state-of-the-art warehouse with a capacity to store over 5,000 tons of coffee. 


Our vision


Mullege's vision is to become an internationally recognized exporter of green coffee beans, driven by a strong foundation, innovative ideas, and dedication. Their mission is to provide the most refined coffee to coffee lovers globally through two processing plants in Addis Ababa and pulping stations across Ethiopia. They also aim to be a recognized freight service provider, as evidenced by their national recognition and significant revenue. 


Our success


Mullege's success story highlights its evolution from a small coffee supplier to a major exporter within three generations. Its commitment to quality control, efficient logistics, and a global reach is key to its success. Mullege has a substantial annual production capacity of 22,000 tons of coffee and a state-of-the-art warehouse. It also owns and operates a fleet of trucks for efficient coffee transportation.

fields.description: Women Empowerment Action (WE-Action) is a feminist women's rights organization that has been operating across various regions in Ethiopia, including Amhara, Oromia, Southern Ethiopia, Central Ethiopia, and Tigray, for the past 30 years. WE-Action has four strategic goals: combating gender inequality, promoting gender-equitable and sustainable livelihoods, ensuring protection and lifesaving support, and achieving organizational excellence. WE-Action is currently seeking a competent GBV Case Management Officer , ensure improved quality of health and psychosocial support for survivors, support development of a functional referral networks in We-Action Dasenech Field Office. Note: - WE-Action has zero tolerance for sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA) and any forms of Gender-Based Violence. I. General duties and responsibilities The GBV Case Officer will work to ensure improved quality of health and psychosocial support for survivors, support development of a functional referral networks that enhance survivors’ ability to receive confidential, safe, and timely services that meets their needs in a timely manner. She will oversee Case management and psychosocial support services provided to survivors of gender-based violence and women and girls in general, implementation of basic psychosocial support activities for women and girls at the outreach sites and local partner support. Program Implementation: Provide direct support and care for adult survivors of GBV and age-appropriate specialized support and care for adolescent, and girl child survivors of GBV, including counselling and case management. Follow GBV guiding principles of respect, confidentiality, and safety/security and non- discrimination while providing services. Ensure proper documentation of reported GBV incidences through utilization of GBV IMS case intake, action, follow up and other case management forms appropriately. Ensure all documentations on reported cases and referrals made are updated, accurate, organized and well maintained by social workers. Work with stakeholders to develop and strengthen referral networks and monitor the implementation of the referral pathway to improve survivors access to confidential, safe GBV services in a timely manner to meet their needs Ensure adherence to GBV guiding principles and the provision of survivor-centered care (respect wishes, decisions of survivors). In consultations with women and girls, develop and support to implement a series of age-appropriate and group emotional and social support activities for women and girls, with an emphasis on meeting the needs of survivors of GBV and strengthening support networks among women and girls. In consultations with GBV officer, develop and implement/ share monthly response plan and GBV key messages/issues based on case trends to disseminate information on services available and referral pathways. Ensure tracking of key program indicators and progress through utilization of the M&E data collection and indicator tracking tools. Actively participate and collaborate with M & E section in the establishment of monitoring & Evaluation system of new and existing projects under coordination. Make regular field visits to projects/programs under coordination for technical support at least one visit per quarter and provide reports Facilitate and implement project mid and end term evaluations to be conducted by government signatories and external consultants. WE-Action has four strategic goals: combating gender inequality, promoting gender-equitable and sustainable livelihoods, ensuring protection and lifesaving support, and achieving organizational excellence. WE-Action is currently seeking a competent GBV Case Management Officer, ensure improved quality of health and psychosocial support for survivors, support development of a functional referral networks in We-Action Dasenech Field Office.

Note: - WE-Action has zero tolerance for sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA) and any forms of Gender-Based Violence.

I.         Description of the position

·       Position: GBV Case Management Officer

·       Duty Station: based in Dasenech Field office, with regularly travels to different sites within the target area.

II.         General duties and responsibilities

The GBV Case Officer will work to ensure improved quality of health and psychosocial support for survivors, support development of a functional referral networks that enhance survivors’ ability to receive confidential, safe, and timely services that meets their needs in a timely manner. She will oversee Case management and psychosocial support services provided to survivors of gender-based violence and women and girls in general, implementation of basic psychosocial support activities for women and girls at the outreach sites and local partner support.

  • Ensure adherence to GBV guiding principles and the provision of survivor-centered care (respect wishes, decisions of survivors).
  • In consultations with women and girls, develop and support to implement a series of age-appropriate and group emotional and social support activities for women and girls, with an emphasis on meeting the needs of survivors of GBV and strengthening support networks among women and girls.

fields.title: (TOR) Audit Service for First-Time IPSAS Adoption
fields.description: ABOUT FIRST CONSULT AFRICA DEVELOPMENT First Consult Africa Development is an economic development organization dedicated to empowering vulnerable communities by designing and implementing sustainable projects across various sectors, including agriculture, manufacturing, and services. Our multidisciplinary teams leverage local expertise to drive enterprise growth, improve access to finance, and foster skill development. With a proven track record, we've successfully created jobs, generated wealth, and attracted investments, ultimately leading to the formation and growth of thriving businesses. BACKGROUND OF THE ASSIGNEMENT First Consult Africa Development is implementing the International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) for the first time. First Consult Africa Development seeks to engage an independent audit and advisory firm to review and provide assurance over the first-time IPSAS adoption process and confirm that the transition complies with applicable IPSAS requirements, the service would also include an audit service for the budget year 2025-26 OBJECTIVE OF THE ASSIGNMENT To provide independent audit and technical assurance on First Consult Africa Development 's first-time IPSAS adoption by reviewing the conversion process, validating IPSAS adjustments, assessing compliance with IPSAS, and identifying areas requiring improvement before issuance of the financial statements and to audit the converted IPSAS records for the budget year 2025-26 SCOPE OF SERVICES • Review the IPSAS conversion methodology and implementation approach. • Assess the opening IPSAS Statement of Financial Position. • Verify conversion adjustments and accounting treatments. • Review IPSAS-compliant accounting policies and disclosures. • Assess compliance of the first IPSAS financial statements with applicable IPSAS. • Issue an audit/assurance report with findings and recommendations. • Audit service for 2025-26 EXPECTED DELIVERABLES The selected firm shall conduct an independent review of the organization’s compliance with IPSAS requirements and audit service for budget year 2025-26. The firm will be responsible for assessing existing practices, identifying gaps, communicating key findings in management, providing practical recommendations for improvement, and submitting timely progress and final reports. The key deliverables shall include: · Inception Report · IPSAS Compliance Review Report · 2025-26 fiscal year audit service · Final Audit Findings Report TIMELINE The assignment is expected to be completed within four (4) weeks from the date of contract signature. The detailed activity schedule and milestones will be agreed during inception and documented in the approved inception report. WORKING ARRANGEMENT AND REPORTING The service provider will be working under a contract with FC Africa Development and shall report to First Consult Africa Development Management and submit an inception report, draft audit findings, and a final assurance report.

fields.description: Junior Cameraman / Videographer Company: Benod Consulting Architects & Engineers Channels: Benod Interiors & Benod Furniture Location: Ayertena, Addis Ababa — On-Site / Field Work About the Role Benod Consulting Architects & Engineers is looking for an efficient and creative Junior Cameraman / Videographer to support the content production of our Benod Interiors and Benod Furniture channels. We are looking for someone with a good visual eye who understands how to capture interesting and useful footage, rather than simply operating a camera. You will work closely with our video editor and creative team to film content at our office, furniture workshop, interior projects, construction sites, and other locations . The role can be structured as either part-time or permanent , depending on the candidate and our production needs, with a monthly payment arrangement . Key Responsibilities Film social media and marketing content for Benod Interiors and Benod Furniture. Accompany the team to interior project sites, construction sites, furniture workshops, and other locations to capture content. Film behind-the-scenes footage, project progress, furniture production, installations, and completed projects. Assist with filming planned content and studio-style productions. Work closely with the video editor to ensure footage is properly captured and suitable for editing. Understand basic framing, composition, lighting, camera movement, and shot selection. Capture both planned shots and spontaneous moments that can be turned into engaging content. Help organize and transfer footage for the editing workflow. Suggest creative shots, angles, and ideas when filming. Be flexible and ready to work in different environments, including offices, workshops, construction sites, and outdoor locations. Required Skills Previous experience in videography, filmmaking, content creation, or a similar role. A good eye for composition, framing, lighting, and interesting visual details . Basic understanding of cameras and video equipment. Ability to capture stable, well-composed footage. Understanding of what makes content engaging for social media. Ability to work efficiently with a video editor and follow a content production workflow. Good communication and teamwork skills. Willingness to travel with the team to different project and workshop locations. Equipment Having your own decent camera or smartphone capable of producing good-quality video is an advantage. For larger or more professional studio productions , additional cameras and equipment may be rented when required. Therefore, applicants do not necessarily need to own a complete professional camera setup. Work Arrangement Permanent or Part-Time Monthly Payment Primarily on-site and field-based Work will take place at our office in Ayertena , as well as project sites, workshops, and other filming locations. Location Preference Our office is located around Ayertena, Addis Ababa . We strongly prefer candidates who live in Ayertena or nearby areas and can easily commute to the office and accompany the team to filming locations. Ideal Candidate The ideal candidate is someone who is efficient, creative, observant, reliable, and comfortable working on the move . You don’t have to be an expert cinematographer, but you should have a strong visual sense, understand how to capture good footage, and be willing to learn and improve with our team. How to Apply Please submit: Updated CV Portfolio or examples of previous video work Links to social media content or videos you have filmed, if available Information about the camera/equipment you currently have access to Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for an interview.

raw_data.title: Junior Cameraman / Videographer
raw_data.description:
Junior Cameraman / Videographer

Company: Benod Consulting Architects & Engineers
Channels: Benod Interiors & Benod Furniture
Location: Ayertena, Addis Ababa — On-Site / Field Work

About the Role

Benod Consulting Architects & Engineers is looking for an efficient and creative Junior Cameraman / Videographer to support the content production of our Benod Interiors and Benod Furniture channels.

We are looking for someone with a good visual eye who understands how to capture interesting and useful footage, rather than simply operating a camera. You will work closely with our video editor and creative team to film content at our office, furniture workshop, interior projects, construction sites, and other locations.

The role can be structured as either part-time or permanent, depending on the candidate and our production needs, with a monthly payment arrangement.

Key Responsibilities

  • Film social media and marketing content for Benod Interiors and Benod Furniture.

  • Accompany the team to interior project sites, construction sites, furniture workshops, and other locations to capture content.

  • Film behind-the-scenes footage, project progress, furniture production, installations, and completed projects.

  • Assist with filming planned content and studio-style productions.

  • Work closely with the video editor to ensure footage is properly captured and suitable for editing.

  • Understand basic framing, composition, lighting, camera movement, and shot selection.

  • Capture both planned shots and spontaneous moments that can be turned into engaging content.

  • Help organize and transfer footage for the editing workflow.

  • Suggest creative shots, angles, and ideas when filming.

  • Be flexible and ready to work in different environments, including offices, workshops, construction sites, and outdoor locations.

Required Skills

  • Previous experience in videography, filmmaking, content creation, or a similar role.

  • A good eye for composition, framing, lighting, and interesting visual details.

  • Basic understanding of cameras and video equipment.

  • Ability to capture stable, well-composed footage.

  • Understanding of what makes content engaging for social media.

  • Ability to work efficiently with a video editor and follow a content production workflow.

  • Good communication and teamwork skills.

  • Willingness to travel with the team to different project and workshop locations.

Equipment

Having your own decent camera or smartphone capable of producing good-quality video is an advantage.

For larger or more professional studio productions, additional cameras and equipment may be rented when required. Therefore, applicants do not necessarily need to own a complete professional camera setup.

Work Arrangement

  • Permanent or Part-Time

  • Monthly Payment

  • Primarily on-site and field-based

  • Work will take place at our office in Ayertena, as well as project sites, workshops, and other filming locations.

Location Preference

Our office is located around Ayertena, Addis Ababa. We strongly prefer candidates who live in Ayertena or nearby areas and can easily commute to the office and accompany the team to filming locations.

Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is someone who is efficient, creative, observant, reliable, and comfortable working on the move. You don’t have to be an expert cinematographer, but you should have a strong visual sense, understand how to capture good footage, and be willing to learn and improve with our team.

How to Apply

Please submit:

  • Updated CV

  • Portfolio or examples of previous video work

  • Links to social media content or videos you have filmed, if available

  • Information about the camera/equipment you currently have access to

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for an interview.

fields.description: Social Enterprise Strategy Consultant Activity Social Enterprise Strategy Development Duration 6 months Duty Station Addis Ababa, with travel to programmer/regional offices as required Reporting To Chief Executive Officer, YADAM Foundation, in coordination with the Senior Management Team Working With Programmed, Finance, MEAL, and the Board Sub-Committee on Sustainability Contract Type Consultancy service agreement (output/deliverable-based) Date August 7/2026 BACKGROUND YADAM Foundation is an Ethiopian non-profit delivering nutrition intervention in partnership with government, donors, and communities. As part of its strategy to strengthen financial sustainability and reduce dependency on restricted donor funding, YADAM has identified social enterprise development — unrestricted, mission-aligned income through fee-based services, social-impact products, or income-generating ventures — as a priority growth area. PURPOSE OF THE ASSIGNMENT YADAM Foundation is seeking an experienced Social Enterprise Strategy Consultant to design a costed and actionable social enterprise strategy and lead its early implementation, diversifying YADAM's income base without compromising its core nutrition mandate. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES • Assess YADAM's existing assets, capabilities, networks, and market opportunities relevant to social enterprise development • Identify and shortlist priority social enterprise concepts, with feasibility and risk screening for each • Design the Social Enterprise Strategy, including business model, governance and financial structuring, 3-year financial projections, and a risk matrix • Facilitate internal validation and approval with the Senior Management Team and the Board • Lead the operational set-up and piloting of at least one priority income-generating venture, including financial controls in coordination with Finance • Build the capacity of designated YADAM staff to sustain the enterprise beyond the consultancy period KEY DELIVERABLES • Inception report and work plan • Diagnostic and market/landscape assessment report • Board-approved Social Enterprise Strategy and implementation plan • Operational tools (costing/pricing framework, business plan template, monitoring indicators) • Final handover report and transition plan

Chief Executive Officer, YADAM Foundation, in coordination with the Senior Management Team

Working With

Programmed, Finance, MEAL, and the Board Sub-Committee on Sustainability

Contract Type

Consultancy service agreement (output/deliverable-based)

Date

August  7/2026

BACKGROUND

YADAM Foundation is an Ethiopian non-profit delivering nutrition intervention in partnership with government, donors, and communities. As part of its strategy to strengthen financial sustainability and reduce dependency on restricted donor funding, YADAM has identified social enterprise development — unrestricted, mission-aligned income through fee-based services, social-impact products, or income-generating ventures — as a priority growth area.

PURPOSE OF THE ASSIGNMENT

YADAM Foundation is seeking an experienced Social Enterprise Strategy Consultant to design a costed and actionable social enterprise strategy and lead its early implementation, diversifying YADAM's income base without compromising its core nutrition mandate.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

•      Assess YADAM's existing assets, capabilities, networks, and market opportunities relevant to social enterprise development

•      Identify and shortlist priority social enterprise concepts, with feasibility and risk screening for each

•      Design the Social Enterprise Strategy, including business model, governance and financial structuring, 3-year financial projections, and a risk matrix

•      Facilitate internal validation and approval with the Senior Management Team and the Board

•      Lead the operational set-up and piloting of at least one priority income-generating venture, including financial controls in coordination with Finance

•      Build the capacity of designated YADAM staff to sustain the enterprise beyond the consultancy period

KEY DELIVERABLES

•      Inception report and work plan

•      Diagnostic and market/landscape assessment report

•      Board-approved Social Enterprise Strategy and implementation plan

•      Operational tools (costing/pricing framework, business plan template, monitoring indicators)

•      Final handover report and transition plan

company.name: Hope Enterprise’s University College
company.description:
Hope Enterprises or Hope is a local NGO that was established in 1971 in Addis Ababa to help the needy help themselves through basic needs, education, competence, job and business mediation and value education. As Hope was completing its 32 years of humanitarian service in 2003, it’s then Executive Director, Dr. Minas Hiruy, recommended to the Board the establishment of an outstanding liberal arts university college by submitting a full-fledged proposal. After some discussion, the Board and the General Assembly of Hope accepted the proposal, establishing Hope University College as the first public benefits institution of higher learning in the country on November 25, 2003.  Soon after, the Board adopted a new structure comprising the Ladders of Hope that subsumed the existing and non-college activities of Hope as one division and Hope University College as another division, opening the way for the university college to operate autonomously.
 

Values

The University College believes in goodwill to humankind and to nature and in the concretization of this concern as a step to making the world a community of hope, justice, peace and progress. The University College holds dear the advancement of liberal education as a means of personal and social transformation and regards the provision of education to all as an important public responsibility.

Vision

The vision of the University College is to contribute to the renewal and transformation of society through knowledge and value based education and graduates who can make a difference using what they had gained in the university college.

Mission

The University College, having a mission to provide aspiring leaders the option of pursuing world-class education without leaving their country and cultural setting, shall enable the development of leaders, who being capable of independent work, problem solving, analysis, innovation and reflection, can make a difference in the development of society and in mutually and sustainably supportive relations between man and nature.

Mission Statement

Developing leadership for a world of hope

company.description:
Who are we ?

The NGO Solidarités International assists populations affected by conflicts and violence, epidemics, natural or climate-related disasters and economic collapse. Our humanitarian teams are committed to helping people whose lives, health and security are threatened, by meeting their most vital needs: food, water, shelter and hygiene. Our mandate is to respond to crises by distributing emergency aid in person and, in parallel, by implementing long-term solutions that enable affected populations to regain sustainable access to water, sanitation, hygiene, diversified livelihoods and safe housing.

Solidarités International is registered in Ethiopia in December 2022 and is aiming at developing emergency programs in true collaboration with the beneficiary communities and local stakeholders.

Our mandate and value

Solidarités International commitment to assist populations affected by the most severe crises dates back to 1980. We always provide aid at the request of the affected population or its representatives, in cooperation with our local partners. Our field teams mainly comprise locally hired staff, to help ensure that the aid provided fits the population’s needs as closely as possible. We are fiercely determined to constantly uphold the humanitarian principles of humanity, independence, impartiality and neutrality. Solidarités International also demonstrates unique technical and social engineering capabilities, which we continue to perfect by building on the innovations and development efforts of our teams and partners.

Find out more about our history explained here.

Why work for us ?

In 2022, our 2,641 staff members worked relentlessly to achieve our collective goal: to provide assistance for people affected by conflicts, violence, epidemics, natural and climate-related disasters and economic collapse in the countries where we work.

As part of its global strategy, Solidarités International is committed to

  • Further develop the professionalism of its human resources;
  • Support and value the diversity of our staff and their experience;
  • Set up conditions that fosters our team’s commitment.

Our teams have always been our NGO’s greatest strength. They share the values that guide our humanitarian action and enable our organization to fulfil its mandate: courage, integrity, professionalism, team spirit and unfailing commitment.

Working conditions

In Solidarités International, we prioritize not only making a meaningful impact in the world but also in your career. Joining our team means:

  • Competitive Compensation: we offer competitive compensation packages firmly rooted in the local job market, ensuring fair compensation.
  • Advanced Social Support: Our benefits include health coverage, maternity and paternity leave and a range of other benefits.
  • Career Advancement: Experience real growth opportunities within our organization.
  • Inclusivity and Fairness: We nurture a culture that values equality, transparency, and the recognition of individual contributions.
  • Transparent HR Policies: Our open HR management policies ensure each decisions’ are justified and communicated to all.
  • Safe Work Environment: Our staff’s security is our prime concern.
  • Zero Tolerance for SEAH: We maintain a strict stance against any type of abuse – all act of exploitation, abuse and/or sexual harassment (SEAH).

In Solidarités International, we're committed to improving the world and providing a fulfilling and evolving career for our dedicated team." You are neither anonymous nor interchangeable: neither is Solidarités International!

Solidarités International is an equitable employer committed to find all forms of discrimination. SI will ever ask for any remuneration to take part in a recruitment process.

Organizational Profile
1.1 General Information

New Millennium Women Empowerment Organization (NMWEO) is an indigenous, non-governmental, non-profit humanitarian organization established in 2007 in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. The organization was previously registered at the Ministry of Justice under registration number 3018 and later registered and licensed by the Federal Charities and Societies Agency as an Ethiopian resident’s charity by the Charities and Societal Proclamation No. 621/2009 by registration No. 0539. NMWEO has been re-registered according to the Civil Society Organizations Proclamation No.113/2019 with registration No. 0539.

Vision 

We envision a country in which women and girls have equal opportunity, claim their rights and free from any violence, and become effective social change agents.

Mission

Our mission is to empower Ethiopian women, girls, and youth in economic, political, and social dimensions, and help them unlock their potential in decision-making through capacity building, advocacy, leadership development, and humanitarian intervention programs.

Core Values and Belief

·       Humanity

·       Gender sensitive

·       Accountability

·       Equity

·       Teamwork and Excellence

·       Partnership and networking

Job Purpose

The Social Worker will support the implementation of community-based protection interventions at woreda and community level. The position will work directly with individuals, families, communities, and community structures to identify protection and social needs, strengthen community participation, facilitate access to appropriate services, and promote safe and inclusive community environments.

The Social Worker will contribute to strengthening community protection mechanisms, prevention of harmful practices, community mobilization, referral and follow-up, community action, and the effective functioning of protection-related services.

The position will apply social work principles, confidentiality, dignity, informed consent, safeguarding, PSEA, gender equality, disability inclusion, child protection, accountability, and Do No Harm throughout all activities.

Key Responsibilities

A.   Community-Based Social Work

  • Establish and maintain constructive relationships with community members and community structures.
  • Identify protection and social concerns affecting individuals, families, and communities.
  • Support communities to identify their own protection priorities and solutions.
  • Promote participation of women, girls, children, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
  • Provide appropriate basic social support within the scope of professional competence.
  • Maintain professional boundaries and confidentiality.

B.   Community Mobilization and Engagement

  • Mobilize and engage communities in project interventions.
  • Support community structures to participate effectively in protection activities.
  • Facilitate community dialogue and awareness activities.
  • Work with community and religious leaders to promote positive attitudes and practices that protect women, girls, and children.
  • Promote community ownership and sustainability of protection interventions.
  • Ensure community engagement is inclusive, conflict-sensitive, and culturally appropriate.

C.   Protection Identification and Referral

  • Identify individuals and groups experiencing or at risk of protection concerns.
  • Provide information on available services and support options.
  • Facilitate safe and appropriate referrals through established referral pathways.
  • Follow up on referrals when appropriate and in accordance with confidentiality and consent requirements.
  • Coordinate with service providers and relevant authorities as required.
  • Immediately report serious protection and safeguarding concerns through established procedures.

D.   Support to Community Protection Mechanisms

  • Support the Protection Officer in strengthening community protection structures.
  • Provide regular follow-up and technical support to community-based protection actors.
  • Support community structures to identify and address protection concerns.
  • Encourage community-based prevention and referral practices.
  • Document community concerns, actions, and feedback and share relevant information with the Protection Officer.

E.   Support to Women and Girls Safe Space

  • Support the safe and effective functioning of the WGSS.
  • Promote safe access and participation of women and girls.
  • Provide information and basic social support within the scope of the role.
  • Support linkages between WGSS users and appropriate specialized services.
  • Promote confidentiality, dignity, safety, accessibility, and respect.
  • Identify operational or protection concerns affecting women and girls and report them to the Protection Officer.

F.    Community Prevention and Social Support

  • Support community initiatives aimed at preventing protection risks and harmful practices.
  • Facilitate discussions that promote positive social norms and protective behaviors.
  • Support communities to develop and implement locally identified protection solutions.
  • Encourage positive family and community support systems.
  • Provide appropriate information and awareness on available protection and social services.

G.  Monitoring, Documentation and Reporting

  • Maintain accurate records of activities and community engagement.
  • Provide regular updates to the Protection Officer.
  • Support collection of project monitoring information and community feedback.
  • Document referrals and follow-up actions in accordance with confidentiality requirements.
  • Contribute to project reports, lessons learned, success stories, and case documentation where appropriate and ethically permissible.
  • Ensure all records are safely stored and protected.

H. Safeguarding and Accountability

  • Comply with NMWEO safeguarding, PSEA, child protection, code of conduct, data protection, and other relevant policies.
  • Maintain confidentiality and protect the privacy and dignity of community members.
  • Promote safe reporting of protection and safeguarding concerns.
  • Ensure that activities are implemented according to Do No Harm principles.
  • Promote accessibility and inclusion of persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups
  •   Inform communities about available feedback and complaint mechanisms.

1.1 General Information

New Millennium Women Empowerment Organization (NMWEO) is an indigenous, non-governmental, non-profit humanitarian organization established in 2007 in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. The organization was previously registered at the Ministry of Justice under registration number 3018 and later registered and licensed by the Federal Charities and Societies Agency as an Ethiopian resident’s charity by the Charities and Societal Proclamation No. 621/2009 by registration No. 0539. NMWEO has been re-registered according to the Civil Society Organizations Proclamation No.113/2019 with registration No. 0539.

Vision 

We envision a country in which women and girls have equal opportunity, claim their rights and free from any violence, and become effective social change agents.

Mission

Our mission is to empower Ethiopian women, girls, and youth in economic, political, and social dimensions, and help them unlock their potential in decision-making through capacity building, advocacy, leadership development, and humanitarian intervention programs.

·       Humanity

·       Gender sensitive

The Protection Officer is responsible for the planning, coordination, implementation, monitoring, and reporting of protection activities at woreda level.   • Strengthen community ownership and participation in protection programming.
  • Support the establishment, capacity, functionality, and sustainability of community-based protection mechanisms.
  • Facilitate meaningful engagement of community leaders, religious leaders, local authorities, women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other relevant groups.
  • Promote community-led identification and prioritization of protection concerns and solutions.
  • Strengthen collaboration between community structures and formal protection and social service systems.
  • Promote locally appropriate prevention and response mechanisms for protection concerns.

C.   Protection Risk Identification and Referral

  • Monitor protection risks and trends within the assigned woreda.
  • Ensure appropriate identification and referral of individuals requiring specialized protection and other essential services.
  • Maintain knowledge of available services and functional referral pathways.
  • Promote safe, confidential, informed, and survivor-/person-centered referral practices.
  • Coordinate with relevant service providers and government structures to strengthen access to services.
  • Ensure urgent protection concerns are appropriately escalated through established mechanisms.

D.   Community Engagement and Prevention

  • Lead community engagement approaches aimed at preventing protection risks and harmful practices.
  • Facilitate dialogue and collaboration among communities, leaders, authorities, and service providers.
  • Promote positive social and behavioral change related to protection, safety, dignity, and rights.
  • Support communities to develop and implement locally owned solutions to identified protection concerns.
  • Ensure community engagement approaches are conflict-sensitive, inclusive, and culturally appropriate.

E.   Women and Girls Safe Space Oversight

  • Provide technical oversight to ensure the existing WGSS is safe, accessible, functional, and responsive to the needs of women and girls.
  • Ensure appropriate linkages between WGSS services and relevant protection, health, psychosocial, legal, and other services.

  • Coordinate with relevant stakeholders to address operational and protection concerns affecting the WGSS.

  • Monitor implementation against project objectives, indicators, targets, and quality standards.
  • Ensure accurate and timely collection and documentation of project information.
  • Work closely with MEAL staff on monitoring, data quality, accountability, feedback, and learning.
  • Prepare regular activity and progress reports for the Project Coordinator.
  • Document lessons learned, good practices, challenges, and recommendations.
  • Ensure protection information is managed securely and confidentially.

G.  Safeguarding, Inclusion and Accountability

  • Ensure compliance with organizational policies and humanitarian protection standards.
  • Promote gender equality, disability inclusion, child safeguarding, and meaningful participation of vulnerable groups.
  • Ensure activities do not expose beneficiaries or communities to additional risks.

  • Support efficient use of project resources at woreda level.
  • Ensure activities are implemented within approved budgets and procedures.
  • Provide timely information on resource requirements and operational gaps.
  • Support proper documentation and accountability for project resources.
