fields.description: Terms of Reference (ToR) To Hire a Service Provider (SP) To Provide Technical Assistance (TA) to the Partner Microfinance Institution (MFI) in the Afar Region Institution: FC Africa Development. Project Title: Economic Recovery for Conflict-Affected Population (ER-CAP) Project Implementation Location: Afar Region – Abala Woreda About FC AFRICA DEVELOPMENT FC Africa Development is an economic development organization dedicated to empowering vulnerable communities by designing and implementing sustainable projects across various sectors, including agriculture, manufacturing, and services. Our multidisciplinary teams leverage local expertise to drive enterprise growth, improve access to finance, and foster skill development. With a proven track record, we've successfully created jobs, generated wealth, and attracted investments, ultimately leading to the formation and growth of thriving businesses. About the ER-CAP Program The Economic Recovery for Conflict-Affected Population Project (ER-CAP) is a five-year project aiming to improve the economic adaptation, protection, and recovery of populations affected by conflict. The program, led by Mercy Corps in collaboration with the Danish Refugee Council (DRC) and FC Africa Development, uses an integrated conflict-sensitive, systems-strengthening, climate-smart, and inclusive approach to enhancing systems that support the economic recovery of communities in three regions: Afar (Abala), Tigray (Mekelle), and Amhara (Woldiya). The program aims to benefit 43,540 individuals, with a specific focus on Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), host communities, and returnee women, youth, and other marginalized groups. The expected outcomes include resilient livelihoods, improved access to financial products and services, and enhanced capacity to mitigate protection risks through access to justice and psychosocial support. As part of this consortium, FC Africa Development primarily focuses on facilitating tailored access to finance to support conflict-affected communities, such as internally displaced persons (IDPs), returnees, and host communities. To ensure effective implementation on the ground, it is crucial to establish and strengthen partnerships with key financial service providers including microfinance institutions (MFIs), savings and credit cooperatives (SACCOs), and banks across all intervention sites. Strengthening the institutional capacity of these financial institutions and providing tailored technical assistance is therefore essential to the program's access-to-finance objectives. Background and Rationale Under the ER-CAP program, FC Africa Development has established a strategic partnership with a Microfinance Institution (MFI) operating in Afar Region to expand access to finance for conflict-affected communities in Abala Woreda. Two years of conflict in Northern Ethiopia significantly disrupted the operations, systems, and institutional capacity of financial service providers operating in the region, including the partner MFI. As ER-CAP moves further into its implementation phase, FC Africa Development, in consultation with the partner MFI, has identified three priority, mutually reinforcing interventions required to restore and strengthen the institutional capacity of the MFI: (i) revision and updating of the MFI's internal manuals and guidelines; (ii) technical support for the implementation of a Core Banking System (CBS); and (iii) loan portfolio management and resource mobilization training for key staff, management, and board members. FC Africa Development seeks to engage a qualified service provider to deliver all three components in an integrated and coordinated manner. This approach is expected to ensure coherence across the interventions, reduce transaction, and enable the service provider to effectively sequence and implement the activities. Objective of the Assignment The overall objective of this assignment is to strengthen the institutional capacity of the partner MFI in Afar Region by updating its internal manuals and guidelines, supporting the effective implementation of its Core Banking System, and building the capacity of its key staff, management, and board members in loan portfolio management and resource mobilization, with an emphasis on Interest-Free Banking principles. Assignment Duration The overall assignment is expected to be completed within four (4) calendar months from the date of contract signing. A detailed, jointly agreed work plan and implementation schedule will be finalized during the inception phase, allowing for reasonable sequencing and, where feasible, parallel implementation of the three components. Scope of Work The service provider will be directly responsible for executing activities split across three highly interconnected components: Components One: Revision and Updating of Internal Manuals and Guidelines The partner MFI's existing operational manuals and guidelines including credit/financing policy, operations, and risk management manuals require review and updating to reflect current National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE) directives, post-conflict operational realities, and enhancing of Interest-Free Banking (IFB) product lines. FC Africa Development seeks a consultancy service with practical experience in microfinance policy and procedure development to review the MFI's existing manuals, identify regulatory and operational gaps, and revise/update the manuals, accordingly, including embedding IFB-compliant procedures and controls. Objective The objective of this component is to review and update the partner MFI's internal manuals and guidelines to ensure they are current, regulatory-compliant, operationally sound, and reflective of the institution's Interest-Free Banking product lines. Specific Objectives: · Conduct a comprehensive desk review of the MFI's existing internal manuals and guidelines (credit/financing policy manual, operations manual, risk management manual, and any existing IFB operational guidelines). · Identify regulatory, operational, and IFB-compliance gaps in the existing manuals against NBE directives, cooperative/microfinance proclamations, and relevant good international practice. · Revise and update the identified manuals, incorporating IFB-compliant procedures, internal controls, governance arrangements, and risk management practices. · Facilitate a validation workshop with the MFI's management and board to review, discuss, and endorse the revised manuals. · Incorporate feedback from the validation workshop and finalize the approved manuals and guidelines, submitted in both hard and soft copy. Deliverables: · Inception report outlining the methodology, detailed work plan, and data collection/review tools for this component. · Manuals gap assessment report summarizing findings from the desk review and stakeholder consultations. · Draft revised manuals and guidelines package, including tracked changes/comments where relevant. · Validation workshop report, including participant feedback and agreed revisions. · Final, approved manuals and guidelines package (hard and soft copy). · Support the MFI in organizing board meeting and approval process of the updated internal manuals. Timeframe Thirty (30) Calendar days. A detailed timeline will be developed during the inception phase. Component Two: Core Banking System (CBS) Implementation Support The partner MFI is implementing a Core Banking System (CBS) to modernize its operations and enhance service delivery to conflict-affected communities in Afar Region. FC Africa Development seeks a consultancy service with practical CBS implementation experience to support the MFI in configuring the system including for Interest-Free Banking product modules validating data migration and building staff capacity through on-site training at the MFI's operations in Semera and Abala Woreda. Objective The objective of this component is to provide hands-on technical assistance to the partner MFI for the effective implementation of its Core Banking System, ensuring the system is properly configured (including for IFB products), data is accurately migrated, and staff in Semera and Abala Woreda are competent to operate it. Specific Objectives · Assess the current status of CBS implementation at the MFI (data migration progress, and IT infrastructure readiness) and identify implementation gaps and risks. · Support the configuration/parameterization of CBS modules relevant to both conventional and Interest-Free Banking products. · Support data cleansing, migration validation, and reconciliation between legacy records and the new CBS. · Develop a CBS user manual/standard operating procedure (SOP) tailored to the MFI's staff and IFB product lines. · Conduct on-site, hands-on CBS training for relevant staff at the MFI's Semera location and its Abala Woreda branch. · Provide post-training, post-go-live troubleshooting and handholding support to consolidate staff competence and system stability. Deliverables: · Inception report and detailed work plan for the CBS implementation support assignment. · CBS implementation status and readiness assessment report. · CBS configuration and IFB-module support report. · CBS user manual/standard operating procedure (SOP). · On-site training reports for Semera and Abala Woreda, including attendance lists and participant feedback. · Final CBS implementation support report, including recommendations for post-go-live stabilization, and a live Core banking system. Timeframe Two Calander months inclusive of on-site training, mentoring and coaching days in Semera and Abala Woreda. A detailed timeline will be developed during the inception phase. Component Three: Loan Portfolio Management and Resource Mobilization Training (Interest-Free Banking Focused) The service provider will assess current portfolio management practices, develop a tailored training manual, and build the capacity of key staff, management, and board members to manage an expanding IFB financing portfolio soundly. It also evaluates existing resource mobilization methods and delivers specialized IFB-compliant training to help the MFI diversify its funding sources, sustain its growth, and effectively expand its outreach into conflict-affected communities. Objective Enhance the knowledge and practical skills of the partner MFI's key staff, management, and board members in effective loan/financing portfolio management, within an Interest-Free Banking framework. It also aims to strengthen their capacity to develop and implement resource mobilization strategies that are compliant with Interest-Free Banking principles. Specific Objectives · Assess the MFI's current loan/financing portfolio management practices, tools, and capacity gaps, including underwriting, appraisal, monitoring, and non-performing financing (NPF) management. · Assess the MFI's current resource mobilization practices, products, and challenges, including its existing deposit base and funding sources. · Develop a tailored, IFB-focused loan/financing portfolio management training manual and materials, covering credit risk fundamentals, sound underwriting and appraisal, monitoring and follow-up, and IFB-specific risk classification and provisioning practices. · Develop an IFB-compliant resource mobilization training manual and materials, covering deposit mobilization approaches and outreach/marketing strategies. · Develop a practical resource mobilization action plan/roadmap tailored to the MFI's operating context in Afar Region. · Deliver structured training to key staff, management, and board members of the MFI on loan portfolio management and resource mobilization. · Conduct pre- and post-training assessments to measure knowledge gained and inform follow-up support needs. Deliverables: · Inception report outlining methodology, work plan, and training approach. · Portfolio management capacity gap assessment report. · Resource mobilization assessment report. · IFB-focused loan/financing portfolio management training manual and PowerPoint materials. · IFB-focused resource mobilization training manual and materials. · Resource mobilization action plan/roadmap for the MFI. · Training delivery report, including attendance, pre/post-assessment results, and participant feedback. Timeframe Thirty (30) calendar days. A detailed timeline will be developed during the inception phase. No Deliverable No of Working Days 1 Inception report 3 2 Portfolio management and resource mobilization capacity gap assessment 8 3 Develop IFB-focused training manuals and materials 12 4 Deliver training to staff, management, and board 4 5 Training report and recommendations 3 Total 30 Note: training-related costs (such as training hall, stationery, refreshment, lunch, transport, and DSA) will be covered by FC Africa. Methodology This assignment will employ a mixed-methods approach, combining desk-based reviews of documents with primary data collection, hands-on technical assistance, and structured training delivery. The service provider is expected to develop and agree a detailed work plan and methodology based on this ToR and discussions with FC Africa's ER-CAP Access to Finance team. · Desk review: review of the MFI's operational manuals, financing/credit policy, by-laws, board minutes, audit reports, CBS documentation, and relevant National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE) directives. · Key informant interviews: Key informant interviews with the MFI's board members (where appropriate), senior management, middle management, and branch staff in Semera and Abala Woreda. · Focus group discussions: Focus group discussions with relevant staff and, where appropriate, community members/clients to inform the resource mobilization and portfolio management components. · Technical assistance and training delivery: Hands-on technical assistance and coaching for manuals revision and CBS configuration, alongside structured, participatory training delivery for the capacity-building components.

·         Validation workshop report, including participant feedback and agreed revisions.

 

·         Final, approved manuals and guidelines package (hard and soft copy).

·         Support the MFI in organizing board meeting and approval process of the updated internal manuals.

 Timeframe

   Thirty (30) Calendar days. A detailed timeline will be developed during the inception phase.

Component Two: Core Banking System (CBS) Implementation Support

The partner MFI is implementing a Core Banking System (CBS) to modernize its operations and enhance service delivery to conflict-affected communities in Afar Region. FC Africa Development seeks a consultancy service with practical CBS implementation experience to support the MFI in configuring the system including for Interest-Free Banking product modules validating data migration and building staff capacity through on-site training at the MFI's operations in Semera and Abala Woreda.

Objective

The objective of this component is to provide hands-on technical assistance to the partner MFI for the effective implementation of its Core Banking System, ensuring the system is properly configured (including for IFB products), data is accurately migrated, and staff in Semera and Abala Woreda are competent to operate it.

   Specific Objectives

·         Assess the current status of CBS implementation at the MFI (data migration progress, and IT infrastructure readiness) and identify implementation gaps and risks.

·         Support the configuration/parameterization of CBS modules relevant to both conventional and Interest-Free Banking products.

·         Support data cleansing, migration validation, and reconciliation between legacy records and the new CBS.

·         Develop a CBS user manual/standard operating procedure (SOP) tailored to the MFI's staff and IFB product lines.

·         Conduct on-site, hands-on CBS training for relevant staff at the MFI's Semera location and its Abala Woreda branch.

·         Provide post-training, post-go-live troubleshooting and handholding support to consolidate staff competence and system stability.

 

 Deliverables:

·         Inception report and detailed work plan for the CBS implementation support assignment.

·         CBS implementation status and readiness assessment report.

·         CBS configuration and IFB-module support report.

·         CBS user manual/standard operating procedure (SOP).

·         On-site training reports for Semera and Abala Woreda, including attendance lists and participant feedback.

·         Final CBS implementation support report, including recommendations for post-go-live stabilization, and a live Core banking system.

Timeframe

Two Calander months inclusive of on-site training, mentoring and coaching days in Semera and Abala Woreda. A detailed timeline will be developed during the inception phase.

Component Three: Loan Portfolio Management and Resource Mobilization Training (Interest-Free Banking Focused)

The service provider will assess current portfolio management practices, develop a tailored training manual, and build the capacity of key staff, management, and board members to manage an expanding IFB financing portfolio soundly. It also evaluates existing resource mobilization methods and delivers specialized IFB-compliant training to help the MFI diversify its funding sources, sustain its growth, and effectively expand its outreach into conflict-affected communities.

Objective

Enhance the knowledge and practical skills of the partner MFI's key staff, management, and board members in effective loan/financing portfolio management, within an Interest-Free Banking framework. It also aims to strengthen their capacity to develop and implement resource mobilization strategies that are compliant with Interest-Free Banking principles.

    Specific Objectives

·         Assess the MFI's current loan/financing portfolio management practices, tools, and capacity gaps, including underwriting, appraisal, monitoring, and non-performing financing (NPF) management.

·         Assess the MFI's current resource mobilization practices, products, and challenges, including its existing deposit base and funding sources.

·      Develop a tailored, IFB-focused loan/financing portfolio management training manual and materials, covering credit risk fundamentals, sound underwriting and appraisal, monitoring and follow-up, and IFB-specific risk classification and provisioning practices.

·         Develop an IFB-compliant resource mobilization training manual and materials, covering deposit mobilization approaches and outreach/marketing strategies.

·         Develop a practical resource mobilization action plan/roadmap tailored to the MFI's operating context in Afar Region.

·         Deliver structured training to key staff, management, and board members of the MFI on loan portfolio management and resource mobilization.

·         Conduct pre- and post-training assessments to measure knowledge gained and inform follow-up support needs.

Deliverables:

·         Inception report outlining methodology, work plan, and training approach.

·         Portfolio management capacity gap assessment report.

·         Resource mobilization assessment report.

·         IFB-focused loan/financing portfolio management training manual and PowerPoint materials.

·         IFB-focused resource mobilization training manual and materials.

·         Resource mobilization action plan/roadmap for the MFI.

·         Training delivery report, including attendance, pre/post-assessment results, and participant feedback.

Timeframe

   Thirty (30) calendar days. A detailed timeline will be developed during the inception phase.

Methodology

This assignment will employ a mixed-methods approach, combining desk-based reviews of documents with primary data collection, hands-on technical assistance, and structured training delivery. The service provider is expected to develop and agree a detailed work plan and methodology based on this ToR and discussions with FC Africa's ER-CAP Access to Finance team.

·         Desk review: review of the MFI's operational manuals, financing/credit policy, by-laws, board minutes, audit reports, CBS documentation, and relevant National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE) directives.

·         Key informant interviews: Key informant interviews with the MFI's board members (where appropriate), senior management, middle management, and branch staff in Semera and Abala Woreda.

·         Focus group discussions: Focus group discussions with relevant staff and, where appropriate, community members/clients to inform the resource mobilization and portfolio management components.

company.description:
About the company

As the largest producer and exporter of coffee in Ethiopia, Kerchanshe Trading has a proud history of providing quality coffees to the local and international markets. Founded on the principles of bringing fairness and transparency to the coffee value chain while satisfying customer demand, Kerchanshe is also a company with heart and vision.

Kerchanshe specializes in coffees sourced from Yirgacheffe, Lekempti, Gimbi, Djimma, and Sidamo, names that epitomise fine Arabica coffee. Since its inception 15 years ago, Kerchanshe has established a track record of fair trading and excellent customer service, and now employs over 1,250 permanent staff and 10,000 seasonal staff. Directly and indirectly, it impacts the livelihoods of over 1 million coffee growers throughout the southern and south-western coffee-cultivating regions of Ethiopia.

The passion for fine coffee is coupled with consistent reinvestment not only in improved infrastructure, technology and processes, but Kerchanshe also invests 10% of its annual profits into social responsibility programs such as building schools and providing clean water to the communities it serves

OUR VISION

To be the leader in innovation and quality among coffee producers and exporters while caring for the environment.

OUR MISSION

We are committed to providing the finest high-quality coffee beans to our customers worldwide while forging mutually beneficial relationships with the community and the environment that we live in.

QUALITY POLICY

At Kerchanshe we are highly conscious of the fact that the quality of our beans is what sets us apart.

 

Our Mission

"We are driven to deliver unparalleled quality coffee beans to discerning customers worldwide, fostering enduring relationships with both our communities and the natural world."

Our Vision

"To pioneer innovation and excellence within the global coffee industry while nurturing a profound respect for environmental preservation."

Our Values

Ethical Integrity: We steadfastly adhere to the highest ethical standards in all our dealings, prioritizing integrity and accountability.

Sustainable Practices: We embrace sustainable methodologies that seamlessly integrate with the environment, ensuring responsible stewardship of our resources.

Customer-Centric Excellence: Our unwavering commitment to consistency, integrity, and excellence ensures unparalleled service and satisfaction for our customers.

Empowered Workforce: We empower and champion our diverse workforce, fostering a culture of collaboration, innovation, and continuous growth.

Community Enrichment: We are deeply committed to giving back to our communities through meaningful engagement and impactful initiatives, embodying our ethos of corporate citizenship.

Why work for us

Embark on a fulfilling journey with Kerchanshe Group, where you'll discover more than just a job. Join us for stimulating career opportunities, personalized work schedules that accommodate your lifestyle, a vibrant and inclusive culture that promotes collaboration and innovation, and comprehensive compensation and benefits packages designed to enhance your overall satisfaction and well-being.

In addition to these offerings, you'll have access to ongoing professional development and training programs to further hone your skills and expand your expertise. Furthermore, at Kerchanshe, we prioritize work-life balance, providing resources and support to help you thrive both personally and professionally.

Join our community at Kerchanshe Group, where your individuality is celebrated, your growth is nurtured, and your contributions make a meaningful impact. Together, let's build a brighter future for ourselves and our communities.

Team Benefits

At Kerchanshe Group, we prioritize the welfare and satisfaction of our employees by providing a suite of professional benefits tailored to enhance their work experience. Our comprehensive offerings include:

  • Subsidized canteen services at both headquarters and coffee washing stations/farms
  • Dedicated employee transportation services
  • Annual employee recognition program, celebrating outstanding contributions
  • Provision of vehicles with fuel for executive management
  • These benefits underscore our commitment to cultivating a supportive and rewarding environment, where employee well-being and professional growth are paramount.

fields.title: Protection Officer (Maternity Cover)
fields.description: Medical Teams Calling Daring to love like Jesus, we boldly break barriers to health and restore wholeness in a hurting world. Medical Teams International holds strict child and vulnerable adult safeguarding principles and a zero-tolerance policy for misconduct related to sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse in the workplace and other places where the organization’s activities are rendered. Parallel to technical competence, recruitment & selection, hiring decisions will give due emphasis to assessing candidates' eligibility thorough background checks, police clearance, and professional reference check processes. JOB SUMMARY Protection Officer Response contributes to the calling of Medical Teams by implementing response activities which include case management, psychosocial support, safe space activity, and another related project. The position holder will train and supervise social workers and community activists in Refugee camps & host Communities to prevent and respond to GBV issues. This includes providing ongoing training and mentorship for community workers, and community activists, developing a weekly, monthly, and quarterly work plan, and utilizing monitoring and evaluation systems to ensure high-quality services, smooth communication, collaboration, and coordination among partners from the protection, health, legal, and psychosocial sectors committed to reducing the incidence of violence against women. ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES Prepare and develop weekly and monthly work plans for GBV-related prevention activities, ensuring alignment with the overall program objectives. Implement GBV prevention and response activities, including fieldwork and community-based programs, ensuring that activities are in line with GBV IASC guidelines and best practices. Process and maintain accurate case documentation, including case histories, assessments, interventions, and progress reports, ensuring all information complies with confidentiality standards. Apply protection principles such as confidentiality, safety, and non-discrimination in all program activities, ensuring that GBV survivors are treated with respect and dignity. Prepare outreach materials and awareness campaigns tailored to local communities, ensuring that the information is relevant and culturally appropriate. Implement community-based interventions in partnership with relevant stakeholders such as women and children’s affairs, teachers, medical providers, and law enforcement. Process referrals to appropriate service providers for GBV survivors, ensuring that their needs are met, and all required documentation is provided. Apply the necessary legal frameworks to all protection activities, ensuring that the rights of survivors are upheld in accordance with national laws and international standards. Prepare regular reports, including weekly updates, case progress reports, and activity summaries for submission to the Protection Manager and field coordinator. Implement and support the delivery of capacity-building initiatives for community workers and partners, ensuring effective coordination in response to GBV incidents. Process requests for protection of supplies and services, ensuring adherence to the logistical and financial policies of the organization. Apply best practices in the integration of GBV response activities into health, education, and legal services to ensure holistic support for survivors. Prepare documentation and reports for submission to relevant authorities as required, ensuring that the information complies with legal standards and confidentiality of policies. Implement any other duties assigned by the Protection Manager or senior leadership to support the effective delivery of the GBV program. Support the integration of accountability practices into program activities by following established procedures during planning, implementation, monitoring, and reporting. Help ensure that accountability is reflected in day-to-day tasks, team interactions, and when working with partners or communities. Support safeguarding of program participants and employees through promoting an environment of awareness and upholding the code of conduct provisions of Medical Teams Protection from Sexual Exploitation & Abuse, Child & Vulnerable Adult protection, and harassment-free workplace policies. Incumbents will remain alert and responsive to any child and adult safeguarding risks, acquire relevant knowledge and skills which will enable you to promote strong safeguarding practices, understand the child and adult safeguarding policy and procedures, and conduct yourself in a manner consistent with the Safeguarding. Other Duties Maintain a clean and safe working environment, disposing of waste and sharps appropriately. Other duties as assigned Utilize volunteers when appropriate.

fields.title: Social media & community manager
fields.description: RAMA Technologies PLC is producing a children’s educational animation series teaching young children in Amharic. We are looking for a creative, responsible Social Media & Community Manager to build and run the series’ public presence and its community of parents, teachers, and young viewers. Key Responsibilities • Develop and execute the social media strategy across YouTube, TikTok, Facebook, Instagram, and Telegram. • Plan, write, and publish engaging Amharic and English content for parents and families; maintain a consistent, warm, child-safe brand voice. • Work with the animation team to turn each episode into clips, shorts, teasers, and stills; manage the publishing calendar. • Build and moderate the community: respond to parents’ questions and comments, enforce child-safe moderation standards, and grow relationships with schools, parenting groups, and local influencers. • Track analytics (reach, watch time, growth, engagement), report monthly, and adjust strategy based on results. • Use AI-assisted tools for drafting, scheduling, and repurposing content — with human review before anything is published. Requirements • Excellent written Amharic and English; a natural, warm communication style suitable for a children’s and family audience. • 2+ years managing social media accounts for a brand, media outlet, or creator (portfolio of accounts/content required). • Solid grasp of YouTube, TikTok, Facebook, Instagram, and Telegram formats, trends, and analytics. • Basic video editing for short-form content (e.g., CapCut, Premiere, or similar). • Sound judgment for child-appropriate content and community safety; experience with children’s, family, or education content is a strong advantage. • Familiarity with AI content tools and scheduling platforms is an advantage. Compensation Competitive salary based on experience, plus performance-based variable pay linked to agreed KPIs (channel growth, engagement, publishing consistency).

fields.description: Hill Bottom Properties is seeking a highly organised and compliance-minded Admin Supervisor to manage the full administrative backbone of our company. QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE • Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Public Administration, Law, or related field • Minimum 4 years' experience in an administrative or regulatory compliance role in Ethiopia • Direct experience dealing with Ethiopian government agencies — Addis Ababa City Administration, ERCA, Ministry of Labour, Land Authority, or equivalent strongly preferred • Demonstrated experience managing permit and licence renewals in an Ethiopian business context • Experience managing document management systems — physical and digital archiving • Proficiency with Odoo or equivalent document management and business system preferred • Fluent Amharic (written and spoken) — essential for all government interactions. Professional English required for internal documentation • Strong supervisory experience — ability to manage and direct a small team KEY COMPETENCIES ✓ Regulatory compliance management ✓ Permit & licence tracking ✓ Government agency liaison ✓ Document management & archiving ✓ Team supervision ✓ Attention to detail ✓ Deadline management ✓ Correspondence management ✓ Odoo / systems proficiency ✓ Fluent Amharic & English ✓ Proactive problem-solving ✓ Professional integrity

​የመንገድ መመሪያን መከተል፡ የተመደበውን የማስታወቂያ ሳይክል በተወሰኑ መንገዶችና በተቀመጠው የጊዜ ሰሌዳ መሰረት ማሽከርከር።
​ሙያዊ ስነ-ምግባር፡ ሁልጊዜም ንጹህ እና ፕሮፌሽናል የሆነ ስነ-ምግባርን መላበስ።
​የንብረት እንክብካቤ፡ ብስክሌቱ እና የተገጠመለት ቢልቦርድ ሁልጊዜ ንጹህ እና ደህንነታቸው የተጠበቀ መሆናቸውን ማረጋገጥ።
​ሪፖርት ማድረግ፡ በስራ ሰዓት የሚያጋጥሙ ማንኛውንም ችግሮች፣ ብልሽቶች ወይም ክስተቶች ለሚመለከተው አካል ወዲያውኑ ማሳወቅ።
​የመሳሪያዎች አያያዝ፡ የዕለቱን ስራ እንደጨረሱ ብስክሌቱን እና ሌሎች መሳሪያዎችን በጥንቃቄ መመለስ።

We combine deep knowledge of how care and supply chains operate, human-centred product design, data engineering and responsible artificial intelligence. Our work helps health workers, managers and public institutions turn fragmented data into timely decisions—so essential medicines, vaccines and services are available where and when people need them. Our philosophy We believe useful innovation is not novelty for its own sake. It is the disciplined work of understanding a real problem, challenging assumptions, building and testing a better response, measuring what changes, and strengthening the institutions that must sustain the result. Technology is valuable only when it improves a decision, a workflow or an outcome in the real operating environment. · Start with reality: design around the health workers, workloads, incentives, infrastructure and constraints that actually exist—not an imported ideal workflow. · Build with people, not for them: government counterparts and frontline users are co-designers, decision-makers and eventual owners, not passive recipients. · Strengthen the system, not a standalone application: connect workflows, data, institutions and incentives so information can lead to action across every level. · Push boundaries responsibly: make ambitious but testable bets, protect safety and privacy, and change direction quickly when evidence contradicts the original idea. · Make capability local and durable: transfer knowledge, product ownership and operational responsibility so progress continues without permanent dependence on an external project team. · Be honest about impact: distinguish deployment from adoption and activity from results; make claims specific, measurable and open to verification. What this means for candidates Opian is looking for accomplished specialists who are also builders. Candidates should bring exceptional depth in their discipline, intellectual courage, practical judgment and the humility to learn from users and evidence. We value people who can move from ambiguity to a testable approach, from a workshop to an operating routine, and from a promising pilot to an institutionally owned system. Government Partnership and Institutionalization Lead Role purpose Own the end-to-end product strategy and translate real supply-chain and service-delivery problems into prioritized, testable and sustainable digital capabilities. The Product Director will ensure that ForLab+ strengthens existing transactional and national systems rather than becoming a parallel reporting platform. Key responsibilities · Define the product vision, operating model, outcomes, roadmap and release priorities in partnership with government and users. · Lead discovery with health facilities, woreda teams, regional managers, supply hubs and national programs to document actual decisions, workflows and constraints. · Convert workflows into clear user stories, acceptance criteria, data requirements and measurable product outcomes. · Prioritize capabilities that improve source transaction capture, inventory accuracy, traceability, replenishment and closed-loop issue resolution. · Maintain alignment between ForLab+, authoritative registries, existing logistics systems, service-delivery systems and national analytics platforms. · Balance user value, policy requirements, interoperability dependencies, technical feasibility, cost and transition readiness. · Lead usability testing, pilot feedback loops, backlog refinement, release acceptance and product performance reviews. · Define adoption and usage measures, including active use, workflow completion, data quality, latency and action closure. · Build government product-management capacity and transfer the roadmap, backlog and release-governance processes. raw_data.title: Product Director / Product Owner
raw_data.description:
About Opian

Opian is an Ethiopian health-technology and innovation company building decision infrastructure for stronger health systems. We combine deep knowledge of how care and supply chains operate, human-centred product design, data engineering and responsible artificial intelligence. Our work helps health workers, managers and public institutions turn fragmented data into timely decisions—so essential medicines, vaccines and services are available where and when people need them.

Our philosophy

We believe useful innovation is not novelty for its own sake. It is the disciplined work of understanding a real problem, challenging assumptions, building and testing a better response, measuring what changes, and strengthening the institutions that must sustain the result. Technology is valuable only when it improves a decision, a workflow or an outcome in the real operating environment.

· Start with reality: design around the health workers, workloads, incentives, infrastructure and constraints that actually exist—not an imported ideal workflow.

· Build with people, not for them: government counterparts and frontline users are co-designers, decision-makers and eventual owners, not passive recipients.

· Strengthen the system, not a standalone application: connect workflows, data, institutions and incentives so information can lead to action across every level.

· Push boundaries responsibly: make ambitious but testable bets, protect safety and privacy, and change direction quickly when evidence contradicts the original idea.

· Make capability local and durable: transfer knowledge, product ownership and operational responsibility so progress continues without permanent dependence on an external project team.

· Be honest about impact: distinguish deployment from adoption and activity from results; make claims specific, measurable and open to verification.

What this means for candidates

Opian is looking for accomplished specialists who are also builders. Candidates should bring exceptional depth in their discipline, intellectual courage, practical judgment and the humility to learn from users and evidence. We value people who can move from ambiguity to a testable approach, from a workshop to an operating routine, and from a promising pilot to an institutionally owned system. The standard is simple: show not only what you know, but what you personally built, changed, tested, learned and left stronger.

· Work across public health, supply chain, policy, product, technology and field implementation boundaries.

· Turn expertise into usable products, processes, decisions and measurable improvements—not reports alone.

· Operate with urgency while preserving quality, public trust, data protection, service continuity and government ownership.

Government Partnership and Institutionalization Lead

Role purpose

Own the end-to-end product strategy and translate real supply-chain and service-delivery problems into prioritized, testable and sustainable digital capabilities. The Product Director will ensure that ForLab+ strengthens existing transactional and national systems rather than becoming a parallel reporting platform.

Key responsibilities

· Define the product vision, operating model, outcomes, roadmap and release priorities in partnership with government and users.

· Lead discovery with health facilities, woreda teams, regional managers, supply hubs and national programs to document actual decisions, workflows and constraints.

· Convert workflows into clear user stories, acceptance criteria, data requirements and measurable product outcomes.

· Prioritize capabilities that improve source transaction capture, inventory accuracy, traceability, replenishment and closed-loop issue resolution.

· Maintain alignment between ForLab+, authoritative registries, existing logistics systems, service-delivery systems and national analytics platforms.

· Balance user value, policy requirements, interoperability dependencies, technical feasibility, cost and transition readiness.

· Lead usability testing, pilot feedback loops, backlog refinement, release acceptance and product performance reviews.

· Define adoption and usage measures, including active use, workflow completion, data quality, latency and action closure.

· Build government product-management capacity and transfer the roadmap, backlog and release-governance processes.

Expected results

· A stakeholder-approved product strategy and phased roadmap tied to operational outcomes.

· Validated workflows and requirements covering vaccines and RMNCH commodities at relevant supply-chain levels.

· Usable, offline-capable product releases accepted by representative end users.

· A government-owned product backlog, release process and performance-monitoring approach.

company.name: Transsion Manufacturing PLC
company.description:
TRANSSION MANUFACTURING PLC.

Background

Transsion Holdings is a manufacturer of mobile phones based in Shenzhen, China. It was the largest smartphone manufacturer by sales in Africa in 2017, and also sells mobile phones in South Asia. Its brands include phone brands, Itel and Infinix after-sales service brand Carlcare and accessories brand Oraimo. It manufactures phones in China, Pakistan, Ethiopia, and Bangladesh and recently at India.

Transsion Holdings Pvt. Ltd was founded as Transsion Technology in Hong Kong in 2006, with a focus on the development, manufacturing, sales, and services of mobile communication products. Transsion entered the African market with its Tecno and Itel brands, and started focusing on the African market in July 2008, initially with feature phones Transsion released its first smartphone in 2014.Transsion set up its Nigerian subsidiary in June 2008, and had subsidiaries in seven countries in Africa by October that year. Transsion set up a manufacturing plant in Ethiopia in 2011. Transsion entered the Indian market in 2016. The market share of Transsion's smartphone brands in Africa combined surpassed that of Samsung in 2017, making Transsion the largest manufacturer of smartphones for the African market in the fourth quarter of 2017.Transsion was also the largest manufacturer of mobile phones in Africa in the first half of 2017.Transsion's 2018 attempt at a reverse takeover failed. In October 2018, Transsion Holdings started producing smartphones in their new manufacturing plant in Bangladesh.Transsion Holdings became a public listed company in September 2019 by listing on the STAR Market section of the Shanghai Stock Exchange.

Operations

Transsion sells mobile phones in Africa and South Asia. It operates mobile phone brands Tecno, Itel, and Infinix, as well as after-sales support service Carlcare and accessories brand Oraimo. Spice Digital, an Indian phone brand, was acquired in 2017. Transsion manufactures its phones in China, Ethiopia, Bangladesh, India, and Pakistan. Transsion was the first non-African mobile phone company to set up an after-sales support network in Africa.Transsion's success in the African market has been attributed to tailoring its phones' features to the needs of the African market. Transsion's phones offer a featurethat calibrates camera exposures for darker skin tones, allowing face details to be retained. Transsion developed phones with dual SIM functionality, which were well received because African users commonly used more than one SIM card at a time save money. Transsion released phones with long battery life, which are suited to low electrification rates in Africa and the propensity of blackouts. The phones included support for multiple African languages, and Tecno was the first major mobile phone brand in Ethiopia to include support for an Amharic keyboard. Transsion heavily advertises its mobile phone brands in Africa.

Vision

To become the most popular provider of smart devices and mobile services for

consumers in global emerging markets

Mission

To improve the lives of as many people as possible through technology and

innovation

CORE VALUES

·      Customer

Customers are both the starting point and the end point for all work of TRANSSIONers

·      Respect

Respect defines how we treat each other and our differences.

·      Openness

Staying open connects us to the future and its possibilities.

·      Innovation

Innovation is essential to achieving breakthroughs on different levels, both

personal and organizational.

·      Sharing

Sharing invites every “I” to become “we”.

·      Bottom line

We always show compassion, even if it puts us at a disadvantage.

company.description:
About the company

Marie Stopes International (MSI) is one of the largest international Sexual Reproductive Health (SRH) and Family Planning (FP) organizations in the world. We are a results oriented social enterprise that develop efficient, effective and sustainable SRH/FP programmes around the world.

Marie Stopes International Ethiopia (MSIE), a partner of MSI, is currently undertaking a dramatic scale-up of health service delivery for low income women and couples in Ethiopia. This includes expanding services in clinics and rural outreach programs into new regions of Ethiopia and creating social franchising networks of private quality service providers.  MSIE announces information about job vacancies widely and encourages applications from all sectors of the community.  MSIE considers all applicants based on their abilities and will ensure no group is disadvantaged on the basis of disability, gender, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race (which includes colour, nationality and ethnic or national origins), religion or belief, economic or social class, sex, HIV/AIDs status and political affiliation.

MSIE also implements a Safeguarding Policy to safeguard and protect the rights of staff, children, young people and vulnerable sections of the community and to this end, successful candidates will need to sign MSIE’s ‘code of conduct’ and undergo a background check. The Safeguarding Policy includes an adult Safeguarding, dignity at work place, child safeguarding, human trafficking and anti-slavery, sexual harassment, equality and diversity.  MSIE applies zero tolerance approach for the violation such policies. 

MSIE is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to hiring and retaining female employees. The organization has flexible policies including: travel policy for pregnant and lactating women, flexible work hour for non-clinic staff without reducing the total working hour. Women employees have access to on-job mentorship which aim to create gender-sensitive and inclusive work environment. As such, qualified women are encouraged to apply 

 

Our Mission

Ensuring the Individual’s Right to Children by Choice not Chance.

Vision
To become a sustainable nationwide provider of high quality, integrated reproductive health/family planning services.

Our Values

1 Mission driven
With unwavering commitment, we exist to empower women and men to have children by choice not chance.

2 Client centred
We are dedicated to our clients and work tirelessly to deliver high-quality, high-impact services that meet their individual needs.

3 Accountable
We are accountable for our actions and focus on results, ensuring long term sustainability and increasing the impact of the Partnership.

4 Courageous
We recruit and nurture talented, passionate and brave people who have the courage to push boundaries, make tough decisions and challenge others in line with our mission.
 

Why work for us

MSI works in 37 countries around the world to help women and girls to have children by choice, not chance.

For an individual woman or girl, being able to choose when she has children means having the power to take control of her future.
It can mean having the ability to finish her education, pursue a career, look after the children she already has and ensure she remains healthy. MSI was founded in 1976 to provide the contraception and safe abortion services that give women and girls a choice. Since then, choice has been at the heart of everything that we do and our mission remains clear: to help women and girls to have children by choice, not chance.

MSI is a global organisation with 11,000 team members working in 37 countries to deliver our mission. Starting from one single clinic in London, our organisation has grown from one clinic in central London to become one of the world’s largest providers of high quality, affordable contraception and safe abortion services.
Over the last 40 years, we have touched the lives of more than 120 million women and girls, giving them the power to take control of their futures. But we know that there is much more to do, today there are over 230 million women who want to use contraception but can't and that number continues to grow.

company.name: Transsion Manufacturing PLC
company.description:
TRANSSION MANUFACTURING PLC.

Background

Transsion Holdings is a manufacturer of mobile phones based in Shenzhen, China. It was the largest smartphone manufacturer by sales in Africa in 2017, and also sells mobile phones in South Asia. Its brands include phone brands, Itel and Infinix after-sales service brand Carlcare and accessories brand Oraimo. It manufactures phones in China, Pakistan, Ethiopia, and Bangladesh and recently at India.

Transsion Holdings Pvt. Ltd was founded as Transsion Technology in Hong Kong in 2006, with a focus on the development, manufacturing, sales, and services of mobile communication products. Transsion entered the African market with its Tecno and Itel brands, and started focusing on the African market in July 2008, initially with feature phones Transsion released its first smartphone in 2014.Transsion set up its Nigerian subsidiary in June 2008, and had subsidiaries in seven countries in Africa by October that year. Transsion set up a manufacturing plant in Ethiopia in 2011. Transsion entered the Indian market in 2016. The market share of Transsion's smartphone brands in Africa combined surpassed that of Samsung in 2017, making Transsion the largest manufacturer of smartphones for the African market in the fourth quarter of 2017.Transsion was also the largest manufacturer of mobile phones in Africa in the first half of 2017.Transsion's 2018 attempt at a reverse takeover failed. In October 2018, Transsion Holdings started producing smartphones in their new manufacturing plant in Bangladesh.Transsion Holdings became a public listed company in September 2019 by listing on the STAR Market section of the Shanghai Stock Exchange.

Operations

Transsion sells mobile phones in Africa and South Asia. It operates mobile phone brands Tecno, Itel, and Infinix, as well as after-sales support service Carlcare and accessories brand Oraimo. Spice Digital, an Indian phone brand, was acquired in 2017. Transsion manufactures its phones in China, Ethiopia, Bangladesh, India, and Pakistan. Transsion was the first non-African mobile phone company to set up an after-sales support network in Africa.Transsion's success in the African market has been attributed to tailoring its phones' features to the needs of the African market. Transsion's phones offer a featurethat calibrates camera exposures for darker skin tones, allowing face details to be retained. Transsion developed phones with dual SIM functionality, which were well received because African users commonly used more than one SIM card at a time save money. Transsion released phones with long battery life, which are suited to low electrification rates in Africa and the propensity of blackouts. The phones included support for multiple African languages, and Tecno was the first major mobile phone brand in Ethiopia to include support for an Amharic keyboard. Transsion heavily advertises its mobile phone brands in Africa.

Vision

To become the most popular provider of smart devices and mobile services for

consumers in global emerging markets

Mission

To improve the lives of as many people as possible through technology and

innovation

CORE VALUES

·      Customer

Customers are both the starting point and the end point for all work of TRANSSIONers

·      Respect

Respect defines how we treat each other and our differences.

·      Openness

Staying open connects us to the future and its possibilities.

·      Innovation

Innovation is essential to achieving breakthroughs on different levels, both

personal and organizational.

·      Sharing

Sharing invites every “I” to become “we”.

·      Bottom line

We always show compassion, even if it puts us at a disadvantage.

The organization was previously registered at the Ministry of Justice under registration number 3018 and later registered and licensed by the Federal Charities and Societies Agency as an Ethiopian resident’s charity by the Charities and Societal Proclamation No. 621/2009 by registration No. 0539. NMWEO has been re-registered according to the Civil Society Organizations Proclamation No.113/2019 with registration No. 0539. Vision We envision a country in which women and girls have equal opportunity, claim their rights and free from any violence, and become effective social change agents. Mission Our mission is to empower Ethiopian women, girls, and youth in economic, political, and social dimensions, and help them unlock their potential in decision-making through capacity building, advocacy, leadership development, and humanitarian intervention programs. Core Values and Belief · Humanity · Gender sensitive · Accountability · Equity · Teamwork and Excellence · Partnership and networking Job Purpose The Protection Officer is responsible for the planning, coordination, implementation, monitoring, and reporting of protection activities at woreda level. The Officer will lead the implementation of community-based protection interventions, strengthen community protection committees, facilitate consultations on child and early marriage, support the implementation of community action plans, and oversee the rehabilitation and functioning of the existing Women and Girls Safe Space (WGSS), where applicable. The Protection Officer will work closely with the Social Worker, community structures, religious leaders, local authorities, and relevant service providers to ensure that protection activities are inclusive, community-led, safe, accountable, and consistent with protection, safeguarding, PSEA, child protection, gender, disability inclusion, and Do No Harm principles. Maintain effective coordination with relevant government offices, community structures, religious leaders, and other stakeholders. Community-Based Protection and Stakeholder Engagement Strengthen community ownership and participation in protection programming. Support the establishment, capacity, functionality, and sustainability of community-based protection mechanisms. Facilitate meaningful engagement of community leaders, religious leaders, local authorities, women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other relevant groups. Promote community-led identification and prioritization of protection concerns and solutions. Strengthen collaboration between community structures and formal protection and social service systems. Ensure appropriate identification and referral of individuals requiring specialized protection and other essential services. Maintain knowledge of available services and functional referral pathways. Promote safe, confidential, informed, and survivor-/person-centered referral practices. Coordinate with relevant service providers and government structures to strengthen access to services. Ensure urgent protection concerns are appropriately escalated through established mechanisms. D. Community Engagement and Prevention Lead community engagement approaches aimed at preventing protection risks and harmful practices. Facilitate dialogue and collaboration among communities, leaders, authorities, and service providers. Promote positive social and behavioral change related to protection, safety, dignity, and rights. Ensure community engagement approaches are conflict-sensitive, inclusive, and culturally appropriate. E. Women and Girls Safe Space Oversight Provide technical oversight to ensure the existing WGSS is safe, accessible, functional, and responsive to the needs of women and girls. Ensure appropriate linkages between WGSS services and relevant protection, health, psychosocial, legal, and other services. Monitor the quality and accessibility of services provided through the WGSS. Promote confidentiality, dignity, safety, and informed choice for women and girls accessing services. Coordinate with relevant stakeholders to address operational and protection concerns affecting the WGSS. F. Monitoring, Quality Assurance and Reporting Monitor implementation against project objectives, indicators, targets, and quality standards. Ensure accurate and timely collection and documentation of project information. Work closely with MEAL staff on monitoring, data quality, accountability, feedback, and learning. Prepare regular activity and progress reports for the Project Coordinator. Document lessons learned, good practices, challenges, and recommendations. Ensure protection information is managed securely and confidentially. G. Safeguarding, Inclusion and Accountability Ensure compliance with organizational policies and humanitarian protection standards. Promote gender equality, disability inclusion, child safeguarding, and meaningful participation of vulnerable groups. Ensure activities do not expose beneficiaries or communities to additional risks. Promote awareness and use of feedback, complaint, and reporting mechanisms. Maintain professional boundaries and confidentiality. Immediately report safeguarding, PSEA, and serious protection concerns through established organizational procedures. H. Financial and Resource Management Support efficient use of project resources at woreda level. Ensure activities are implemented within approved budgets and procedures. Provide timely information on resource requirements and operational gaps. Support proper documentation and accountability for project resources.

fields.title: Chief Nursing Officer (CNO)
fields.description: LANDMARK GENERAL HOSPITAL JOB DESCRIPTION – CHIEF NURSING OFFICER (CNO) Position Title: Chief Nursing Officer (CNO) Department: Nursing Services Reports To: Chief Executive Officer (CEO) / Deputy Chief Executive Officer (DCEO) 4. Supervises Nursing Department Heads/ Head Nurses Staff Nurses and Midwives Supervisors Nursing Educators Other nursing personnel as assigned 5. Position Purpose The Chief Nursing Officer is responsible for the overall leadership, management, coordination, supervision, and continuous improvement of nursing services at Landmark General Hospital. The CNO ensures that nursing care is safe, ethical, evidence-based, patient-centered, efficient, and compliant with applicable Ethiopian laws, professional requirements, hospital policies, WHO Patient Safety Friendly Hospital Framework (PSFHF) standards, and applicable hospital accreditation standards. The CNO provides strategic nursing leadership and ensures that nursing services contribute to the hospital's quality, patient safety, accreditation, clinical governance, and continuous improvement objectives. 6. Key Duties and Responsibilities Nursing Leadership and Governance Provide strategic and operational leadership for all nursing and midwifery services. Develop, implement, review, and monitor nursing policies, procedures, protocols, guidelines, and standards. Establish clear nursing reporting lines, accountability, delegation, and scope of practice. Conduct regular nursing management rounds and monitor nursing performance across all clinical units. Ensure adequate nursing staffing, appropriate skill mix, duty schedules, and effective utilization of nursing resources. Participate in hospital executive management and multidisciplinary committees as required. Promote professional nursing practice, ethical conduct, accountability, teamwork, and effective communication. B. WHO-PSFHF / Patient Safety Responsibilities The CNO shall serve as a key nursing leader for implementation and monitoring of the WHO Patient Safety Friendly Hospital Framework (PSFHF). Responsibilities include: 1. Ensure nursing services comply with applicable PSFHF requirements. 2. Promote a strong patient-safety culture throughout nursing services. 3. Ensure safe, evidence-based nursing practices are consistently implemented. 4. Monitor nursing compliance with patient identification, medication safety, infection prevention, falls prevention, pressure injury prevention, safe handover, documentation, and other patient-safety practices. Ensure nursing staff understand and follow patient-safety policies and procedures. Participate in identification, reporting, investigation, analysis, and prevention of adverse events, near misses, incidents, and sentinel events. Ensure nursing-related patient-safety indicators are monitored and improved. Participate in patient-safety and quality-improvement committees. Promote patient and family involvement in care and patient-safety improvement. Ensure nursing staff receive appropriate patient-safety education and continuing professional development. Maintain appropriate evidence and records demonstrating nursing compliance with PSFHF requirements. WHO's PSFHF specifically addresses leadership and management, patient and public involvement, safe evidence-based clinical practices, safe environments, and lifelong learning; these areas should therefore be reflected in the CNO's accountability. C. Accreditation and Quality Improvement The CNO shall be a key responsible person for ensuring nursing readiness for and compliance with hospital accreditation requirements. Responsibilities include: Ensure nursing services comply with applicable national and international accreditation standards adopted by Landmark General Hospital. Participate in hospital accreditation planning, implementation, internal assessment, corrective action, and follow-up activities. Coordinate with the Quality and Safety Department to identify nursing-related accreditation gaps. Develop and implement corrective and preventive action plans for identified nursing deficiencies. Ensure nursing departments maintain required accreditation documents, records, reports, checklists, indicators, and evidence. Prepare nursing departments for accreditation surveys and assessment visits. Participate in mock surveys, tracer activities, audits, interviews, and document reviews. Ensure findings from accreditation assessments are communicated to relevant nursing staff. Monitor implementation of accreditation corrective actions and report progress to hospital management. Promote continuous quality improvement rather than compliance only during accreditation periods. Ensure nursing quality indicators are regularly collected, analyzed, reported, and used for improvement. D. Nursing Quality and Performance Monitoring Establish and monitor nursing quality indicators and key performance indicators. Monitor patient outcomes and nursing-sensitive indicators. Conduct or facilitate regular nursing audits. Review nursing documentation and patient-care records. Monitor compliance with nursing standards, protocols, and clinical guidelines. Identify trends, risks, and performance gaps and initiate improvement actions. Present nursing quality and performance reports to hospital management. Develop quality-improvement projects based on identified nursing and patient-safety problems. Nursing Management Rounds Establish a structured nursing management-round schedule. Conduct regular rounds with nursing heads and supervisors. Assess: Patient safety Emergency preparedness Staff availability and attendance Nursing documentation Patient identification Medication administration practices Infection prevention and control Cleanliness and environmental safety Waste segregation Equipment availability Dressing-code compliance Instrument processing Patient satisfaction and complaints Document findings and assign responsible persons and deadlines for corrective actions. Follow up implementation of identified actions. This is particularly relevant to Ethiopian hospital accreditation requirements, which include nursing management rounds led by nursing leadership and assessment of areas such as emergency preparedness, staff attendance, cleanliness, waste segregation, and instrument processing. Infection Prevention and Control Ensure nursing compliance with infection prevention and control policies. Promote hand hygiene and appropriate PPE use. Monitor standard and transmission-based precautions. Collaborate with IPC staff on infection prevention activities. Ensure appropriate nursing practices for waste segregation, sharps disposal, isolation, sterilization/instrument processing, and environmental safety. Participate in healthcare-associated infection prevention and surveillance activities. Staff Development and Competency Identify nursing training and competency-development needs. Develop annual nursing education and training plans. Ensure orientation and competency assessment for newly hired nurses. Promote continuing professional development. Ensure nurses maintain valid professional licenses and required credentials. Support competency assessment, clinical supervision, mentorship, and coaching. Monitor compliance with mandatory hospital training requirements. Clinical Practice and Patient-Centered Care Ensure evidence-based nursing care is provided. Promote respect for patient rights, dignity, privacy, confidentiality, and informed participation. Ensure appropriate nursing assessment, care planning, implementation, evaluation, and documentation. Promote effective communication and safe clinical handover. Ensure timely escalation of deteriorating patients. Promote multidisciplinary collaboration. Monitor patient and family satisfaction with nursing services. Risk Management and Incident Management 1. Identify nursing-related clinical and operational risks. 2. Ensure timely reporting and escalation of incidents. 3. Participate in root-cause analysis and other incident-review processes. 4. Implement corrective and preventive actions. 5. Monitor recurring incidents and develop strategies to prevent recurrence. 6. Ensure lessons learned from incidents are communicated to nursing staff. J. Staffing and Resource Management 1. Develop nursing staffing plans according to patient volume, acuity, and service requirements. 2. Ensure appropriate nurse-to-patient allocation. 3. Monitor overtime, absenteeism, turnover, and staffing shortages. 4. Participate in recruitment and selection of nursing personnel. 5. Recommend staffing adjustments based on service needs. 6. Ensure effective use and maintenance of nursing equipment and supplies. 7. Collaborate with Finance, HR, Procurement, and other departments regarding nursing resource requirements. K. Documentation and Reporting 1. Ensure accurate, complete, timely, and confidential nursing documentation. 2. Review nursing reports and clinical records. 3. Submit regular nursing performance reports to hospital management. 4. Maintain accreditation and PSFHF-related nursing evidence. 5. Ensure nursing records are available and organized for internal and external assessment. 6. Ensure nursing data are used for quality improvement and management decisions. 7. Scope of Authority The CNO has authority to:  Direct and supervise nursing services.  Assign and reassign nursing personnel according to service needs.  Recommend recruitment, promotion, disciplinary action, and termination in accordance with hospital policy.  Stop or escalate unsafe nursing practices.  Require corrective action for nursing non-compliance.  Recommend changes to nursing policies, staffing, resources, and workflows.  Initiate nursing quality-improvement activities.  Escalate serious patient-safety and accreditation risks to executive management. 8. Decision-Making Authority The CNO may make operational decisions within the approved nursing structure and hospital policies and shall escalate decisions involving significant financial, legal, clinical, staffing, or patient-safety risks to the appropriate executive authority. 9. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) The CNO shall be evaluated using measurable indicators including: 1. Nursing compliance with PSFHF requirements. 2. Nursing accreditation compliance rate. 3. Completion rate of nursing corrective-action plans. 4. Nursing documentation compliance. 5. Medication-administration error rate. 6. Patient falls rate. 7. Pressure injury rate. 8. Nursing-related adverse-event rate. 9. Patient satisfaction with nursing services. 10. Nursing staff turnover rate. 11. Nursing absenteeism rate. 12. Staff competency-assessment completion rate. 13. Mandatory training completion rate. 14. Infection-prevention compliance. 15. Hand-hygiene compliance. 16. Nursing audit completion rate. 17. Nursing management-round completion rate. 18. Timeliness of incident reporting and follow-up. 19. Compliance with professional licensing requirements. 20. Improvement in nursing-sensitive patient outcomes. 10. Required Training The CNO should have training/competency in:  WHO Patient Safety Friendly Hospital Framework (PSFHF)  Patient safety  Hospital accreditation standards  Quality improvement  Clinical governance  Risk management  Infection prevention and control  Incident reporting and investigation  Root-cause analysis  Nursing leadership and management  Clinical audit  Patient rights and ethics  Emergency preparedness  Occupational health and safety  Leadership and communication  Healthcare data management and quality indicators 11. Required Skills  Strategic nursing leadership  Clinical leadership  Patient-safety management  Accreditation-readiness management  Quality-improvement skills  Clinical audit skills  Risk assessment and management  Problem-solving and decision-making  Staff supervision and performance management  Conflict resolution  Communication and interpersonal skills  Data analysis and report writing  Training and mentoring  Team-building and multidisciplinary collaboration  Policy and SOP development 12. Working Relationships The CNO shall work closely with:  CEO  DCEO  CMO  COO  Quality and Safety Department  HR Department  IPC Department  Medical Staff  Pharmacy  Laboratory  Facility and Engineering  Finance  Procurement  Hospital Administration  Education Department  Patients and families  External regulatory and accreditation bodies
