The CNO provides strategic nursing leadership and ensures that nursing services contribute to the hospital's quality, patient safety, accreditation, clinical governance, and continuous improvement objectives.

6. Key Duties and Responsibilities

Nursing Leadership and Governance

  • Provide strategic and operational leadership for all nursing and midwifery services.
  • Develop, implement, review, and monitor nursing policies, procedures, protocols, guidelines, and standards.
  • Establish clear nursing reporting lines, accountability, delegation, and scope of practice.
  • Conduct regular nursing management rounds and monitor nursing performance across all

clinical units.

  • Ensure adequate nursing staffing, appropriate skill mix, duty schedules, and effective utilization of nursing resources.
  • Participate in hospital executive management and multidisciplinary committees as required.
  • Promote professional nursing practice, ethical conduct, accountability, teamwork, and effective communication.

B. WHO-PSFHF / Patient Safety Responsibilities

The CNO shall serve as a key nursing leader for implementation and monitoring of the WHO Patient Safety Friendly Hospital Framework (PSFHF).

Responsibilities include:

  • 1. Ensure nursing services comply with applicable PSFHF requirements.
  • 2. Promote a strong patient-safety culture throughout nursing services.
  • 3. Ensure safe, evidence-based nursing practices are consistently implemented.
  • 4. Monitor nursing compliance with patient identification, medication safety, infection prevention, falls prevention, pressure injury prevention, safe handover, documentation, and other patient-safety practices.
  • Ensure nursing staff understand and follow patient-safety policies and procedures.
  • Participate in identification, reporting, investigation, analysis, and prevention of adverse events, near misses, incidents, and sentinel events.
  • Ensure nursing-related patient-safety indicators are monitored and improved.
  • Participate in patient-safety and quality-improvement committees.
  • Promote patient and family involvement in care and patient-safety improvement.
  • Ensure nursing staff receive appropriate patient-safety education and continuing professional development.
  • Maintain appropriate evidence and records demonstrating nursing compliance with PSFHF requirements. WHO's PSFHF specifically addresses leadership and management, patient and public involvement, safe evidence-based clinical practices, safe environments, and lifelong learning; these areas should therefore be reflected in the CNO's accountability.

C. Accreditation and Quality Improvement

The CNO shall be a key responsible person for ensuring nursing readiness for and compliance with hospital accreditation requirements. Responsibilities include:

  • Ensure nursing services comply with applicable national and international accreditation standards adopted by Landmark General Hospital.
  • Participate in hospital accreditation planning, implementation, internal assessment, corrective action, and follow-up activities.
  • Coordinate with the Quality and Safety Department to identify nursing-related accreditation gaps.
  • Develop and implement corrective and preventive action plans for identified nursing deficiencies.
  • Ensure nursing departments maintain required accreditation documents, records, reports, checklists, indicators, and evidence.
  • Prepare nursing departments for accreditation surveys and assessment visits.
  • Participate in mock surveys, tracer activities, audits, interviews, and document reviews.
  • Ensure findings from accreditation assessments are communicated to relevant nursing staff.
  • Monitor implementation of accreditation corrective actions and report progress to hospital management.
  • Promote continuous quality improvement rather than compliance only during accreditation periods.
  • Ensure nursing quality indicators are regularly collected, analyzed, reported, and used for improvement.

D. Nursing Quality and Performance Monitoring

  • Establish and monitor nursing quality indicators and key performance indicators.
  • Monitor patient outcomes and nursing-sensitive indicators.
  • Conduct or facilitate regular nursing audits.
  • Review nursing documentation and patient-care records.
  • Monitor compliance with nursing standards, protocols, and clinical guidelines.
  • Identify trends, risks, and performance gaps and initiate improvement actions.
  • Present nursing quality and performance reports to hospital management.
  • Develop quality-improvement projects based on identified nursing and patient-safety

problems.

Nursing Management Rounds

  • Establish a structured nursing management-round schedule.
  • Conduct regular rounds with nursing heads and supervisors.

Assess:

  • Patient safety
  • Emergency preparedness
  • Staff availability and attendance
  • Nursing documentation
  • Patient identification
  • Medication administration practices
  • Infection prevention and control
  • Cleanliness and environmental safety
  • Waste segregation
  • Equipment availability
  • Dressing-code compliance
  • Instrument processing
  • Patient satisfaction and complaints

Document findings and assign responsible persons and deadlines for corrective actions.

Follow up implementation of identified actions.

This is particularly relevant to Ethiopian hospital accreditation requirements, which include nursing management rounds led by nursing leadership and assessment of areas such as emergency preparedness, staff attendance, cleanliness, waste segregation, and instrument processing.

Infection Prevention and Control

  • Ensure nursing compliance with infection prevention and control policies.
  • Promote hand hygiene and appropriate PPE use.
  • Monitor standard and transmission-based precautions.
  • Collaborate with IPC staff on infection prevention activities.
  • Ensure appropriate nursing practices for waste segregation, sharps disposal, isolation, sterilization/instrument processing, and environmental safety.
  • Participate in healthcare-associated infection prevention and surveillance activities.

Staff Development and Competency

  • Identify nursing training and competency-development needs.
  • Develop annual nursing education and training plans.
  • Ensure orientation and competency assessment for newly hired nurses.
  • Promote continuing professional development.
  • Ensure nurses maintain valid professional licenses and required credentials.
  • Support competency assessment, clinical supervision, mentorship, and coaching.
  • Monitor compliance with mandatory hospital training requirements.

Clinical Practice and Patient-Centered Care

  • Ensure evidence-based nursing care is provided.
  • Promote respect for patient rights, dignity, privacy, confidentiality, and informed participation.
  • Ensure appropriate nursing assessment, care planning, implementation, evaluation, and documentation.
  • Promote effective communication and safe clinical handover.
  • Ensure timely escalation of deteriorating patients.
  • Promote multidisciplinary collaboration.
  • Monitor patient and family satisfaction with nursing services.

Risk Management and Incident Management

1. Identify nursing-related clinical and operational risks.

2. Ensure timely reporting and escalation of incidents.

3. Participate in root-cause analysis and other incident-review processes.

4. Implement corrective and preventive actions.

5. Monitor recurring incidents and develop strategies to prevent recurrence.

6. Ensure lessons learned from incidents are communicated to nursing staff.

J. Staffing and Resource Management

1. Develop nursing staffing plans according to patient volume, acuity, and service

requirements.

2. Ensure appropriate nurse-to-patient allocation.

3. Monitor overtime, absenteeism, turnover, and staffing shortages.

4. Participate in recruitment and selection of nursing personnel.

5. Recommend staffing adjustments based on service needs.

6. Ensure effective use and maintenance of nursing equipment and supplies.

7. Collaborate with Finance, HR, Procurement, and other departments regarding nursing resource requirements.

K. Documentation and Reporting

1. Ensure accurate, complete, timely, and confidential nursing documentation.

2. Review nursing reports and clinical records.

3. Submit regular nursing performance reports to hospital management.

4. Maintain accreditation and PSFHF-related nursing evidence.

5. Ensure nursing records are available and organized for internal and external assessment.

6. Ensure nursing data are used for quality improvement and management decisions.

7. Scope of Authority

The CNO has authority to:

 Direct and supervise nursing services.

 Assign and reassign nursing personnel according to service needs.

 Recommend recruitment, promotion, disciplinary action, and termination in accordance

with hospital policy.

 Stop or escalate unsafe nursing practices.

 Require corrective action for nursing non-compliance.

 Recommend changes to nursing policies, staffing, resources, and workflows.

 Initiate nursing quality-improvement activities.

 Escalate serious patient-safety and accreditation risks to executive management.

8. Decision-Making Authority

The CNO may make operational decisions within the approved nursing structure and hospital policies and shall escalate decisions involving significant financial, legal, clinical, staffing, or patient-safety risks to the appropriate executive authority.

9. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

The CNO shall be evaluated using measurable indicators including:

1. Nursing compliance with PSFHF requirements.

2. Nursing accreditation compliance rate.

3. Completion rate of nursing corrective-action plans.

4. Nursing documentation compliance.

5. Medication-administration error rate.

6. Patient falls rate.

7. Pressure injury rate.

8. Nursing-related adverse-event rate.

9. Patient satisfaction with nursing services.

10. Nursing staff turnover rate.

11. Nursing absenteeism rate.

12. Staff competency-assessment completion rate.

13. Mandatory training completion rate.

14. Infection-prevention compliance.

15. Hand-hygiene compliance.

16. Nursing audit completion rate.

17. Nursing management-round completion rate.

18. Timeliness of incident reporting and follow-up.

19. Compliance with professional licensing requirements.

20. Improvement in nursing-sensitive patient outcomes.

10. Required Training

The CNO should have training/competency in:

 WHO Patient Safety Friendly Hospital Framework (PSFHF)

 Patient safety

 Hospital accreditation standards

 Quality improvement

 Clinical governance

 Risk management

 Infection prevention and control

 Incident reporting and investigation

 Root-cause analysis

 Nursing leadership and management

 Clinical audit

 Patient rights and ethics

 Emergency preparedness

 Occupational health and safety

 Leadership and communication

 Healthcare data management and quality indicators

11. Required Skills

 Strategic nursing leadership

 Clinical leadership

 Patient-safety management

 Accreditation-readiness management

 Quality-improvement skills

 Clinical audit skills

 Risk assessment and management

 Problem-solving and decision-making

 Staff supervision and performance management

 Conflict resolution

 Communication and interpersonal skills

 Data analysis and report writing

 Training and mentoring

 Team-building and multidisciplinary collaboration

 Policy and SOP development

12. Working Relationships

The CNO shall work closely with:

 CEO

 DCEO

 CMO

 COO

 Quality and Safety Department

 HR Department

 IPC Department

 Medical Staff

 Pharmacy

 Laboratory

 Facility and Engineering

 Finance

 Procurement

 Hospital Administration

 Education Department

 Patients and families

 External regulatory and accreditation bodies

raw_data.title: Project Director
raw_data.description:
About Opian

Opian is an Ethiopian health-technology and innovation company building decision infrastructure for stronger health systems. We combine deep knowledge of how care and supply chains operate, human-centred product design, data engineering and responsible artificial intelligence. Our work helps health workers, managers and public institutions turn fragmented data into timely decisions—so essential medicines, vaccines and services are available where and when people need them.


Our philosophy

We believe useful innovation is not novelty for its own sake. It is the disciplined work of understanding a real problem, challenging assumptions, building and testing a better response, measuring what changes, and strengthening the institutions that must sustain the result. Technology is valuable only when it improves a decision, a workflow or an outcome in the real operating environment.

· Start with reality: design around the health workers, workloads, incentives, infrastructure and constraints that actually exist—not an imported ideal workflow.

· Build with people, not for them: government counterparts and frontline users are co-designers, decision-makers and eventual owners, not passive recipients.

· Strengthen the system, not a standalone application: connect workflows, data, institutions and incentives so information can lead to action across every level.

· Push boundaries responsibly: make ambitious but testable bets, protect safety and privacy, and change direction quickly when evidence contradicts the original idea.

· Make capability local and durable: transfer knowledge, product ownership and operational responsibility so progress continues without permanent dependence on an external project team.

· Be honest about impact: distinguish deployment from adoption and activity from results; make claims specific, measurable and open to verification.

What this means for candidates

Opian is looking for accomplished specialists who are also builders. Candidates should bring exceptional depth in their discipline, intellectual courage, practical judgment and the humility to learn from users and evidence. We value people who can move from ambiguity to a testable approach, from a workshop to an operating routine, and from a promising pilot to an institutionally owned system. The standard is simple: show not only what you know, but what you personally built, changed, tested, learned and left stronger.

· Work across public health, supply chain, policy, product, technology and field implementation boundaries.

· Turn expertise into usable products, processes, decisions and measurable improvements—not reports alone.

· Operate with urgency while preserving quality, public trust, data protection, service continuity and government ownership.


Role purpose

Provide overall strategic, technical and fiduciary leadership for a national digital supply-chain transformation program focused on improving last-mile visibility and availability of vaccines and RMNCH commodities. The Project Director will be accountable for results, government co-leadership, partner alignment, delivery quality, risk management and the progressive transfer of operational responsibilities to Ethiopian institutions.

Key responsibilities

· Provide overall leadership and maintain a single, outcome-oriented program strategy across assessment, architecture, product development, pilot implementation, governance, evaluation and transition.

· Serve as the principal senior representative to the Ministry of Health, program lead executive offices, EPSS, EPHI, EFDA, regional health bureaus, universities and implementation partners.

· Establish decision rights, escalation mechanisms, steering arrangements and performance-management routines that keep government counterparts in substantive leadership roles.

· Approve annual and quarterly plans, budgets, staffing, subaward scopes, major technical decisions and corrective actions.

· Ensure that product and integration choices align with national digital-health architecture, authoritative registries and existing transactional systems.

· Hold workstream leads accountable for measurable improvements in data quality, system use, stock visibility, decision latency and commodity-management performance.

· Anticipate political, institutional, technical, financial and operational risks and ensure timely mitigation and transparent communication.

· Lead sustainability, institutionalization and handover planning from the first year, including ownership, recurrent costs, hosting, source-code custody and support arrangements.

· Ensure compliance with applicable organizational policies, safeguarding, information security, privacy and ethical requirements.

Expected results

· A government-endorsed program governance and delivery model with clear decision rights and accountability.

· Integrated workplans and budgets delivered on schedule with material risks actively managed.

· A credible pilot that demonstrates routine use and operational value, not only system deployment.

· An agreed scale-up and transition pathway with progressively reduced dependence on external implementation support.

Job Summary

The Finance Manager is responsible for the strategic planning, coordination, and control of all financial resources, accounting operations, and treasury management for Ethio-BioPharma Enterprise.

The Manager ensures that the enterprise’s financial activities are conducted in strict compliance with the Public Enterprises Proclamation, Ethiopian Tax Laws, and International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS). The role focuses on maintaining financial integrity, optimizing liquidity, ensuring accurate budgetary control, and providing timely financial advice to the CEO and the Board to support sustainable growth and operational efficiency

A. Strategic Financial Management and Policy

1. Initiates and designs improvements to the enterprise’s financial policies, manuals, and internal control systems to safeguard assets.

2. Ensures the enterprise’s transition and continuous adherence to IFRS for all financial reporting.

3. Formulates long-term financial strategies and investment plans in line with the enterprise’s expansion goals.

B.     Budgeting and Performance Control

Leads the preparation of the annual consolidated budget and monitors departmental spending

1. Analyzes financial variances and provides strategic recommendations to management to address budget overruns or revenue shortfalls.

2. Coordinates with the Ethiopian investment holdings (EIH) regarding financial performance targets and dividends.

C.     Financial Reporting and Auditing

1.  Oversees the preparation of accurate and timely monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements.

2.  Serves as the primary liaison for the Office of the Federal Auditor General (OFAG) or external auditors to ensure smooth annual audit processes.

3.  Ensures that all audit findings and management letters are addressed and corrective measures are implemented promptly.

D.      Treasury, Cash, and Tax Management

1.  Manages the enterprise's liquidity to ensure sufficient funds for operations, projects, and debt servicing.

2.  Maintains strong relationships with the Commercial Bank of Ethiopia (CBE) and other financial institutions.

3.  Ensures timely and accurate declaration and payment of all taxes (VAT, Withholding Tax, Business Income Tax, and Employee Income Tax) as per Ethiopian Ministry of Revenues regulations.

E.     Internal Controls and Risk Management

1. Establishes and maintains a robust internal control environment to prevent fraud, waste, and financial mismanagement.

2. Supervises the payroll process to ensure accuracy, compliance with pension regulations, and timely disbursement.

3. Conducts financial risk assessments related to currency fluctuations (especially for imported pharmaceutical inputs) and market trends.

fields.title: Government Partnership and Institutionalization Lead
fields.description: About Opian Opian is an Ethiopian health-technology and innovation company building decision infrastructure for stronger health systems. We combine deep knowledge of how care and supply chains operate, human-centred product design, data engineering and responsible artificial intelligence. Our work helps health workers, managers and public institutions turn fragmented data into timely decisions—so essential medicines, vaccines and services are available where and when people need them. Our philosophy We believe useful innovation is not novelty for its own sake. It is the disciplined work of understanding a real problem, challenging assumptions, building and testing a better response, measuring what changes, and strengthening the institutions that must sustain the result. Technology is valuable only when it improves a decision, a workflow or an outcome in the real operating environment. · Start with reality: design around the health workers, workloads, incentives, infrastructure and constraints that actually exist—not an imported ideal workflow. · Build with people, not for them: government counterparts and frontline users are co-designers, decision-makers and eventual owners, not passive recipients. · Strengthen the system, not a standalone application: connect workflows, data, institutions and incentives so information can lead to action across every level. · Push boundaries responsibly: make ambitious but testable bets, protect safety and privacy, and change direction quickly when evidence contradicts the original idea. · Make capability local and durable: transfer knowledge, product ownership and operational responsibility so progress continues without permanent dependence on an external project team. · Be honest about impact: distinguish deployment from adoption and activity from results; make claims specific, measurable and open to verification. What this means for candidates Opian is looking for accomplished specialists who are also builders. Candidates should bring exceptional depth in their discipline, intellectual courage, practical judgment and the humility to learn from users and evidence. We value people who can move from ambiguity to a testable approach, from a workshop to an operating routine, and from a promising pilot to an institutionally owned system. The standard is simple: show not only what you know, but what you personally built, changed, tested, learned and left stronger. · Work across public health, supply chain, policy, product, technology and field implementation boundaries. · Turn expertise into usable products, processes, decisions and measurable improvements—not reports alone. · Operate with urgency while preserving quality, public trust, data protection, service continuity and government ownership. Government Partnership and Institutionalization Lead Role purpose Build and sustain the government co-leadership, governance, accountability and institutional arrangements required for the program to operate within Ethiopia’s health system and continue beyond external implementation support. Key responsibilities · Develop and maintain a stakeholder and political-economy map covering national agencies, lead executive offices, programs, regional authorities and implementation partners. · Establish and facilitate steering, technical working group and operational review mechanisms with documented mandates and decision rights. · Coordinate with the Ministry of Health, EPI, RMNCH, digital-health and planning functions, EPSS, EPHI, EFDA and regional health bureaus. · Translate technical proposals into institutionally feasible roles, policies, SOPs, accountability mechanisms and approval pathways. · Embed government counterparts in assessment, product prioritization, architecture, implementation, evaluation and transition decisions. · Lead capacity-transfer plans covering product ownership, system administration, data governance, support, supervision and performance management. · Track institutional commitments, policy decisions, unresolved ownership issues and readiness for transfer. · Coordinate sustainability and recurrent-cost planning with relevant institutions and development partners. · Identify duplication, mandate conflicts and partner dependencies and facilitate resolution through agreed governance channels. Expected results · Functional governance bodies with documented decisions and consistent participation. · Clear institutional ownership of systems, data, integrations, support and performance-review processes. · Approved SOPs, accountability arrangements and transition milestones. · Government counterparts able to perform progressively larger shares of operational functions.

· Operate with urgency while preserving quality, public trust, data protection, service continuity and government ownership.

Government Partnership and Institutionalization Lead


Role purpose

Build and sustain the government co-leadership, governance, accountability and institutional arrangements required for the program to operate within Ethiopia’s health system and continue beyond external implementation support.

Key responsibilities

· Develop and maintain a stakeholder and political-economy map covering national agencies, lead executive offices, programs, regional authorities and implementation partners.

· Establish and facilitate steering, technical working group and operational review mechanisms with documented mandates and decision rights.

· Coordinate with the Ministry of Health, EPI, RMNCH, digital-health and planning functions, EPSS, EPHI, EFDA and regional health bureaus.

· Translate technical proposals into institutionally feasible roles, policies, SOPs, accountability mechanisms and approval pathways.

· Embed government counterparts in assessment, product prioritization, architecture, implementation, evaluation and transition decisions.

· Lead capacity-transfer plans covering product ownership, system administration, data governance, support, supervision and performance management.

· Track institutional commitments, policy decisions, unresolved ownership issues and readiness for transfer.

· Coordinate sustainability and recurrent-cost planning with relevant institutions and development partners.

· Identify duplication, mandate conflicts and partner dependencies and facilitate resolution through agreed governance channels.

Expected results

· Functional governance bodies with documented decisions and consistent participation.

· Clear institutional ownership of systems, data, integrations, support and performance-review processes.

· Approved SOPs, accountability arrangements and transition milestones.

· Government counterparts able to perform progressively larger shares of operational functions.

Working directly with the Ethiopia Multi-Property Commercial Manager, hotel leadership teams, and cluster revenue management, this role is accountable for generating demand, executing proactive sales campaigns, and hitting volume targets across rooms, meetings, and events. The role has clear accountability for building a robust sales pipeline, maximizing account penetration, and fostering a strong commercial culture. ASSET SCOPE This role will look after the Ethiopia portfolio of hotels managed by The First Group Hospitality. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Commercial Strategy and Leadership · Develop, lead, and execute the corporate and group sales strategy ensuring alignment with ownership objectives, brand standards, annual budgets, and hotel business plans. · Serve as the primary point of contact for key local and international corporate accounts, travel management companies (TMCs), NGOs, and government entities, maximizing revenue through strategic negotiation and preferred partnerships. · Ensure that inclusive standard accommodation amenities, specifically zero-cost gym and shuttle services, are prominently highlighted in all corporate RFPs, group proposals, and client site inspections to maximize booking conversions. · Actively prospect new business leads, manage the sales pipeline using CRM platforms, and conduct regular client presentations and site visits to convert business. · Collaborate with marketing and revenue teams to align sales efforts with direct booking strategies, supporting channel mix optimization and reducing dependency on high-commission third-party channels. RevPAR, Total Revenue and Market Share Growth · Drive RevPAR, ADR, occupancy, market share, and total revenue growth across the portfolio through proactive B2B corporate account management, volume contract negotiations, and targeted local sales initiatives. · Generate revenue and capture growth opportunities across rooms, food and beverage, meetings and events, and corporate groups by aggressively prospecting new business leads and converting pipeline opportunities · Identify demand gaps, market trends, and shifting customer behaviors by closely monitoring competitor set activities, local city-wide events, and key corporate accounts to shift market share away from competitors. · Ensure all commercial and sales decisions balance volume growth with profitability metrics, optimizing the business mix to minimize high-commission third-party costs and elevate account long-term value. · Partner closely with revenue management teams to optimize group pricing strategies, corporate rate structures, and inventory controls to secure high-yield corporate accounts and maximize revenue during peak demand periods. Business Planning, Reporting and Analysis · Contribute actively to annual commercial business planning, sales budgeting, forecasting, and corporate rate setting. · Prepare clear sales activity reports, account production summaries, and pipeline presentations for senior management and stakeholders. · Use data from the hotel property management system (PMS), CRM, and business intelligence tools to track progress against corporate targets, loyalty member enrollment, and lead conversion rates. · Track progress against sales action plans, corporate account production, direct booking targets, corporate loyalty member acquisition, and group/MICE pipeline conversion rates. Operational and Stakeholder Alignment · Work closely with hotel operations teams to ensure contracted corporate agreements, group arrival requirements, and special event requests are fully aligned with the actual guest experience, service delivery, and operations. · Partner with food and beverage leaders to conceptualize, package, and sell high-yield corporate catering, banquet events, and social gatherings that maximize space utilization and grow total revenue. Ensure sales proposals and corporate collateral clearly communicate inclusive standard amenities, specifically highlighting zero-cost gym and shuttle services, to maximize package and contract. · Maintain strong, collaborative relationships with asset management and brand representatives to ensure strategic property alignment and the long-term commercial success of the sales accounts. Key Performance Indicators · Proactive sales-led contribution toward overall hotel RevPAR, ADR, occupancy, and market share index performance. · Delivery of targeted revenue and room night production across corporate, MICE, and group segments against sales budget and forecast goals. · Sales-led generation efficiency, negotiation turnaround time, corporate contract renewal rates, and pipeline conversion metrics. · Effectiveness in supporting channel mix optimization, driving corporate loyalty sign-ups, and improving direct account management cost-efficiency. · Accuracy in sales production forecasting, contract pricing compliance, and the speed of corrective action taken on underperforming accounts. · Maintain corporate room nights and MICE revenue in line with the target budget Maintain pipeline conversion rates in line with established targets

JOB SUMMARY

The Sales Manager is responsible for driving revenue, securing group and transient business, and managing key corporate, MICE (Meetings, Incentives, Conferences, and Exhibitions), and government accounts for the three Ethiopian cluster hotels. Working directly with the Ethiopia Multi-Property Commercial Manager, hotel leadership teams, and cluster revenue management, this role is accountable for generating demand, executing proactive sales campaigns, and hitting volume targets across rooms, meetings, and events. The role has clear accountability for building a robust sales pipeline, maximizing account penetration, and fostering a strong commercial culture.

 

ASSET SCOPE

This role will look after the Ethiopia portfolio of hotels managed by The First Group Hospitality.

  KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Commercial Strategy and Leadership

·         Develop, lead, and execute the corporate and group sales strategy ensuring alignment with ownership objectives, brand standards, annual budgets, and hotel business plans.

·         Serve as the primary point of contact for key local and international corporate accounts, travel management companies (TMCs), NGOs, and government entities, maximizing revenue through strategic negotiation and preferred partnerships.

·         Ensure that inclusive standard accommodation amenities, specifically zero-cost gym and shuttle services, are prominently highlighted in all corporate RFPs, group proposals, and client site inspections to maximize booking conversions.

·         Actively prospect new business leads, manage the sales pipeline using CRM platforms, and conduct regular client presentations and site visits to convert business.

·         Collaborate with marketing and revenue teams to align sales efforts with direct booking strategies, supporting channel mix optimization and reducing dependency on high-commission third-party channels.

RevPAR, Total Revenue and Market Share Growth

·         Drive RevPAR, ADR, occupancy, market share, and total revenue growth across the portfolio through proactive B2B corporate account management, volume contract negotiations, and targeted local sales initiatives.

·         Generate revenue and capture growth opportunities across rooms, food and beverage, meetings and events, and corporate groups by aggressively prospecting new business leads and converting pipeline opportunities

·         Identify demand gaps, market trends, and shifting customer behaviors by closely monitoring competitor set activities, local city-wide events, and key corporate accounts to shift market share away from competitors.

·         Ensure all commercial and sales decisions balance volume growth with profitability metrics, optimizing the business mix to minimize high-commission third-party costs and elevate account long-term value.

·         Partner closely with revenue management teams to optimize group pricing strategies, corporate rate structures, and inventory controls to secure high-yield corporate accounts and maximize revenue during peak demand periods.

Team Management and Performance   

·         Escalate commercial risks, account production shortfalls, and resource needs clearly to the Multi-Property Commercial Manager and senior leadership team.

·         Ensure strong communication and cohesive commercial coordination between sales, marketing, PR, revenue, reservations, events, and hotel operations teams.

·         Lead sales executives, coordinators, and corporate segments with clearly defined account targets, daily reporting routines, and strict accountability for revenue-generating activities

·         Direct sales executives, coordinators, and segment specialists with clearly defined revenue goals, account portfolios, and strict accountability for daily proactive sales activities (e.g., cold calls, site inspections, and client meetings)

·         Set clear individual and team KPIs (including account conversion rates, call volume, and revenue targets), monitor performance metrics regularly, and implement timely corrective actions or performance improvement plans where necessary

Above-Property and Shared-Service Collaboration

·         Build strong and productive relationships with above-property and shared-service sales, distribution, and loyalty teams to ensure property-level priorities are supported and actioned.

·         Translate above-property sales and loyalty initiatives into local property-level account production, ensuring the cluster hotels receive maximum focus from global corporate channels.

Business Planning, Reporting and Analysis

·          Contribute actively to annual commercial business planning, sales budgeting, forecasting, and corporate rate setting.

·          Prepare clear sales activity reports, account production summaries, and pipeline presentations for senior management and stakeholders.

·         Use data from the hotel property management system (PMS), CRM, and business intelligence tools to track progress against corporate targets, loyalty member enrollment, and lead conversion rates.

·         Track progress against sales action plans, corporate account production, direct booking targets, corporate loyalty member acquisition, and group/MICE pipeline conversion rates.

 

Operational and Stakeholder Alignment

·         Work closely with hotel operations teams to ensure contracted corporate agreements, group arrival requirements, and special event requests are fully aligned with the actual guest experience, service delivery, and operations.

·         Partner with food and beverage leaders to conceptualize, package, and sell high-yield corporate catering, banquet events, and social gatherings that maximize space utilization and grow total revenue. Ensure sales proposals and corporate collateral clearly communicate inclusive standard amenities, specifically highlighting zero-cost gym and shuttle services, to maximize package and contract.

·         Maintain strong, collaborative relationships with asset management and brand representatives to ensure strategic property alignment and the long-term commercial success of the sales accounts.

 Key Performance Indicators

·         Proactive sales-led contribution toward overall hotel RevPAR, ADR, occupancy, and market share index performance.

·         Delivery of targeted revenue and room night production across corporate, MICE, and group segments against sales budget and forecast goals.

·         Sales-led generation efficiency, negotiation turnaround time, corporate contract renewal rates, and pipeline conversion metrics.

·         Effectiveness in supporting channel mix optimization, driving corporate loyalty sign-ups, and improving direct account management cost-efficiency.

·         Accuracy in sales production forecasting, contract pricing compliance, and the speed of corrective action taken on underperforming accounts.

Sabahar is an Ethiopian company that produces uniquely designed, hand made cotton and silk textiles. In addition to scarves and shawls, we make table linens, cushions, throws and towels. Our products are entirely hand made in Ethiopia from natural fibers.

Kathy Marshall, a Canadian by birth but a twenty-year veteran of Ethiopia, founded Sabahar in 2004 and still works as its General Manager. The organization was previously registered at the Ministry of Justice under registration number 3018 and later registered and licensed by the Federal Charities and Societies Agency as an Ethiopian resident’s charity by the Charities and Societal Proclamation No. 621/2009 by registration No. 0539. NMWEO has been re-registered according to the Civil Society Organizations Proclamation No.113/2019 with registration No. 0539. Vision We envision a country in which women and girls have equal opportunity, claim their rights and free from any violence, and become effective social change agents. Mission Our mission is to empower Ethiopian women, girls, and youth in economic, political, and social dimensions, and help them unlock their potential in decision-making through capacity building, advocacy, leadership development, and humanitarian intervention programs. Core Values and Belief · Humanity · Gender sensitive · Accountability · Equity · Teamwork and Excellence · Partnership and networking Job Purpose The Social Worker will support the implementation of community-based protection interventions at woreda and community level. The position will work directly with individuals, families, communities, and community structures to identify protection and social needs, strengthen community participation, facilitate access to appropriate services, and promote safe and inclusive community environments. The Social Worker will contribute to strengthening community protection mechanisms, prevention of harmful practices, community mobilization, referral and follow-up, community action, and the effective functioning of protection-related services. The position will apply social work principles, confidentiality, dignity, informed consent, safeguarding, PSEA, gender equality, disability inclusion, child protection, accountability, and Do No Harm throughout all activities. Key Responsibilities A. Community-Based Social Work Establish and maintain constructive relationships with community members and community structures. Identify protection and social concerns affecting individuals, families, and communities. Support communities to identify their own protection priorities and solutions. Promote participation of women, girls, children, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups. Provide appropriate basic social support within the scope of professional competence. Maintain professional boundaries and confidentiality. B. Community Mobilization and Engagement Mobilize and engage communities in project interventions. Support community structures to participate effectively in protection activities. Facilitate community dialogue and awareness activities. Work with community and religious leaders to promote positive attitudes and practices that protect women, girls, and children. Promote community ownership and sustainability of protection interventions. Ensure community engagement is inclusive, conflict-sensitive, and culturally appropriate. C. Protection Identification and Referral Identify individuals and groups experiencing or at risk of protection concerns. Provide information on available services and support options. Facilitate safe and appropriate referrals through established referral pathways. Follow up on referrals when appropriate and in accordance with confidentiality and consent requirements. Coordinate with service providers and relevant authorities as required. Immediately report serious protection and safeguarding concerns through established procedures. D. Support to Community Protection Mechanisms Support the Protection Officer in strengthening community protection structures. Provide regular follow-up and technical support to community-based protection actors. Support community structures to identify and address protection concerns. Encourage community-based prevention and referral practices. Document community concerns, actions, and feedback and share relevant information with the Protection Officer. E. Support to Women and Girls Safe Space Support the safe and effective functioning of the WGSS. Promote safe access and participation of women and girls. Provide information and basic social support within the scope of the role. Support linkages between WGSS users and appropriate specialized services. Promote confidentiality, dignity, safety, accessibility, and respect. Identify operational or protection concerns affecting women and girls and report them to the Protection Officer. F. Community Prevention and Social Support Support community initiatives aimed at preventing protection risks and harmful practices. Facilitate discussions that promote positive social norms and protective behaviors. Support communities to develop and implement locally identified protection solutions. Encourage positive family and community support systems. Provide appropriate information and awareness on available protection and social services. G. Monitoring, Documentation and Reporting Maintain accurate records of activities and community engagement. Provide regular updates to the Protection Officer. Support collection of project monitoring information and community feedback. Document referrals and follow-up actions in accordance with confidentiality requirements. Contribute to project reports, lessons learned, success stories, and case documentation where appropriate and ethically permissible. Ensure all records are safely stored and protected. H. Safeguarding and Accountability Comply with NMWEO safeguarding, PSEA, child protection, code of conduct, data protection, and other relevant policies. Maintain confidentiality and protect the privacy and dignity of community members. Promote safe reporting of protection and safeguarding concerns. Ensure that activities are implemented according to Do No Harm principles. Promote accessibility and inclusion of persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups Inform communities about available feedback and complaint mechanisms.

fields.title: Senior Accountant
fields.description: Job Opening: Senior Accountant – Miawa Water Distribution Location: Ethiopia, Oromia Region, Sheger City, Ashewa Mada Job Type: Full-Time Department: Finance & Accounting Reports To: Finance Manager Company Briefing Miawa Purified Natural Water, a key brand under Miawa Group, is positioned as an affordable, pure, and accessible beverage brand built on quality and strong market visibility. Serving diverse market segments—including retail, HORECA (hotels, restaurants, and cafes), and institutions—our product portfolio spans 0.33L, 0.5L, 1L, and 2L bottle sizes. The distribution arm of Miawa Group operates a robust hybrid distribution model, combining independent sub-agents and a direct delivery van fleet to secure wide market coverage. Miawa Group maintains strict operational standards, relying on systematic financial and sales performance reporting to drive brand consistency and sustainable commercial growth. Job Summary We are seeking an analytical, highly organized, and proactive Senior Accountant to oversee the financial operations of our Miawa Water distribution company. In this role, you will be responsible for general ledger management, route sales reconciliations, inventory accounting across all bottle sizes, expense tracking, and financial reporting. The ideal candidate possesses strong experience in FMCG or beverage distribution, comfortable handling high-volume daily transactions across direct delivery fleets and sub-agent networks while maintaining strict internal controls and tax compliance. Key Responsibilities Financial Reporting & General Ledger: Prepare accurate monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements for the distribution business in compliance with local accounting standards and Miawa Group reporting guidelines. Route & Channel Sales Reconciliation: Perform daily and weekly reconciliations of cash, credit, and digital transactions from direct delivery van fleets and sub-agent sales channels. Inventory & Cost Accounting: Oversee inventory accounting for all SKU sizes (0.33L, 0.5L, 1L, and 2L), reconcile physical stock counts against ledger records, track product breakages/losses, and calculate cost of goods sold (COGS). Operational Expense & Budget Tracking: Monitor operational expenses—including fleet maintenance, fuel, driver allowances, and marketing promotional tools—against approved budgets and maintain systematic performance reports. Month-End & Year-End Close: Lead month-end close procedures, revenue recognition, accruals, bank reconciliations, and variance analysis to present clear financial insights to management. Taxation & Regulatory Compliance: Ensure full compliance with all tax regulations (VAT, Withholding Tax, Payroll Tax, and Corporate Income Tax), ensuring timely calculations, filings, and payments. Audit Preparation & Internal Controls: Serve as the primary point of contact for internal and external auditors, maintaining complete audit trails and enforcing internal financial controls over cash collection and credit terms.

The distribution arm of Miawa Group operates a robust hybrid distribution model, combining independent sub-agents and a direct delivery van fleet to secure wide market coverage. Miawa Group maintains strict operational standards, relying on systematic financial and sales performance reporting to drive brand consistency and sustainable commercial growth.

Job Summary

We are seeking an analytical, highly organized, and proactive Senior Accountant to oversee the financial operations of our Miawa Water distribution company. In this role, you will be responsible for general ledger management, route sales reconciliations, inventory accounting across all bottle sizes, expense tracking, and financial reporting. The ideal candidate possesses strong experience in FMCG or beverage distribution, comfortable handling high-volume daily transactions across direct delivery fleets and sub-agent networks while maintaining strict internal controls and tax compliance.

Key Responsibilities

  • Financial Reporting & General Ledger: Prepare accurate monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements for the distribution business in compliance with local accounting standards and Miawa Group reporting guidelines.
  • Route & Channel Sales Reconciliation: Perform daily and weekly reconciliations of cash, credit, and digital transactions from direct delivery van fleets and sub-agent sales channels.
  • Inventory & Cost Accounting: Oversee inventory accounting for all SKU sizes (0.33L, 0.5L, 1L, and 2L), reconcile physical stock counts against ledger records, track product breakages/losses, and calculate cost of goods sold (COGS).
  • Operational Expense & Budget Tracking: Monitor operational expenses—including fleet maintenance, fuel, driver allowances, and marketing promotional tools—against approved budgets and maintain systematic performance reports.
  • Month-End & Year-End Close: Lead month-end close procedures, revenue recognition, accruals, bank reconciliations, and variance analysis to present clear financial insights to management.
  • Taxation & Regulatory Compliance: Ensure full compliance with all tax regulations (VAT, Withholding Tax, Payroll Tax, and Corporate Income Tax), ensuring timely calculations, filings, and payments.
  • Audit Preparation & Internal Controls: Serve as the primary point of contact for internal and external auditors, maintaining complete audit trails and enforcing internal financial controls over cash collection and credit terms.

Duty Station: One of the following intervention woredas: Mai(t)sebri, Dima, Sheraro, Tahtay-Adyabo, Irob, Gulo-Mekeda, Sanja, Dabat, and Debark

Number of Positions: 9 (one per intervention woreda)

Duration: 12 months

Report To: Project Coordinator

Organization: New Millennium Women Empowerment Organization (NMWEO)

Organizational Profile
1.1 General Information

New Millennium Women Empowerment Organization (NMWEO) is an indigenous, non-governmental, non-profit humanitarian organization established in 2007 in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. The organization was previously registered at the Ministry of Justice under registration number 3018 and later registered and licensed by the Federal Charities and Societies Agency as an Ethiopian resident’s charity by the Charities and Societal Proclamation No. 621/2009 by registration No. 0539. NMWEO has been re-registered according to the Civil Society Organizations Proclamation No.113/2019 with registration No. 0539.

Vision 

We envision a country in which women and girls have equal opportunity, claim their rights and free from any violence, and become effective social change agents.

Mission

Our mission is to empower Ethiopian women, girls, and youth in economic, political, and social dimensions, and help them unlock their potential in decision-making through capacity building, advocacy, leadership development, and humanitarian intervention programs.

Core Values and Belief

·       Humanity

·       Gender sensitive

·       Accountability

·       Equity

·       Teamwork and Excellence

·       Partnership and networking

Job Purpose

The Protection Officer is responsible for the planning, coordination, implementation, monitoring, and reporting of protection activities at woreda level. The Officer will lead the implementation of community-based protection interventions, strengthen community protection committees, facilitate consultations on child and early marriage, support the implementation of community action plans, and oversee the rehabilitation and functioning of the existing Women and Girls Safe Space (WGSS), where applicable.

The Protection Officer will work closely with the Social Worker, community structures, religious leaders, local authorities, and relevant service providers to ensure that protection activities are inclusive, community-led, safe, accountable, and consistent with protection, safeguarding, PSEA, child protection, gender, disability inclusion, and Do No Harm principles.

Key Responsibilities

A.   Protection Programme Coordination

  • Lead the day-to-day implementation of protection activities in the assigned woreda.
  • Translate project plans and objectives into practical woreda-level implementation plans.
  • Ensure activities are implemented according to approved plans, budgets, quality standards, and timelines.
  • Coordinate closely with the Project Coordinator on progress, priorities, challenges, and required actions.
  • Provide technical supervision and guidance to the Social Worker.
  • Maintain effective coordination with relevant government offices, community structures, religious leaders, and other stakeholders.
  • Represent the project in relevant woreda-level coordination forums and meetings.
  • Identify protection risks, operational challenges, and emerging needs and recommend appropriate responses.

B.   Community-Based Protection and Stakeholder Engagement

  • Strengthen community ownership and participation in protection programming.
  • Support the establishment, capacity, functionality, and sustainability of community-based protection mechanisms.
  • Facilitate meaningful engagement of community leaders, religious leaders, local authorities, women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other relevant groups.
  • Promote community-led identification and prioritization of protection concerns and solutions.
  • Strengthen collaboration between community structures and formal protection and social service systems.
  • Promote locally appropriate prevention and response mechanisms for protection concerns.

C.   Protection Risk Identification and Referral

  • Monitor protection risks and trends within the assigned woreda.
  • Ensure appropriate identification and referral of individuals requiring specialized protection and other essential services.
  • Maintain knowledge of available services and functional referral pathways.
  • Promote safe, confidential, informed, and survivor-/person-centered referral practices.
  • Coordinate with relevant service providers and government structures to strengthen access to services.
  • Ensure urgent protection concerns are appropriately escalated through established mechanisms.

D.   Community Engagement and Prevention

  • Lead community engagement approaches aimed at preventing protection risks and harmful practices.
  • Facilitate dialogue and collaboration among communities, leaders, authorities, and service providers.
  • Promote positive social and behavioral change related to protection, safety, dignity, and rights.
  • Support communities to develop and implement locally owned solutions to identified protection concerns.
  • Ensure community engagement approaches are conflict-sensitive, inclusive, and culturally appropriate.

E.   Women and Girls Safe Space Oversight

  • Provide technical oversight to ensure the existing WGSS is safe, accessible, functional, and responsive to the needs of women and girls.
  • Ensure appropriate linkages between WGSS services and relevant protection, health, psychosocial, legal, and other services.
  • Monitor the quality and accessibility of services provided through the WGSS.
  • Promote confidentiality, dignity, safety, and informed choice for women and girls accessing services.
  • Coordinate with relevant stakeholders to address operational and protection concerns affecting the WGSS.

F.    Monitoring, Quality Assurance and Reporting

  • Monitor implementation against project objectives, indicators, targets, and quality standards.
  • Ensure accurate and timely collection and documentation of project information.
  • Work closely with MEAL staff on monitoring, data quality, accountability, feedback, and learning.
  • Prepare regular activity and progress reports for the Project Coordinator.
  • Document lessons learned, good practices, challenges, and recommendations.
  • Ensure protection information is managed securely and confidentially.

G.  Safeguarding, Inclusion and Accountability

  • Ensure compliance with organizational policies and humanitarian protection standards.
  • Promote gender equality, disability inclusion, child safeguarding, and meaningful participation of vulnerable groups.
  • Ensure activities do not expose beneficiaries or communities to additional risks.
  • Promote awareness and use of feedback, complaint, and reporting mechanisms.
  • Maintain professional boundaries and confidentiality.
  • Immediately report safeguarding, PSEA, and serious protection concerns through established organizational procedures.

H.  Financial and Resource Management

  • Support efficient use of project resources at woreda level.
  • Ensure activities are implemented within approved budgets and procedures.
  • Provide timely information on resource requirements and operational gaps.
  • Support proper documentation and accountability for project resources.

company.description:
About the Lutheran World Federation (LWF)

We are a global communion of churches in the Lutheran tradition, living and working together for a just, peaceful, and reconciled world. LWF World Service is the humanitarian and development arm of the Lutheran World Federation. We are a widely recognized, international, faith-based organization working in over 20 countries. We seek to bring people of all backgrounds together in the common quest for justice, peace, and reconciliation in an increasingly complex and fragmented world.

Lutheran World Federation (LWF) in Ethiopia  

LWF World Service Ethiopia is a registered foreign charity, which has been operating in Ethiopia since 1973 implementing various development and humanitarian projects in different parts of Ethiopia. LWF World Service Ethiopia works closely with the Ethiopian Evangelical Church Mekane Yesus (EECMY), the Ethiopian Government, UN organizations and other funding partners. Its thematic areas include the promotion of food security and sustainable livelihood, sustainable natural resources management, emergency preparedness, response and rehabilitation, and capacity building. 

A commitment to the human rights of every individual, regardless of their status, guides our work, actions, and operations. We are particularly known for our timely, compassionate, and professional humanitarian work, and our field presence in hard-to-reach areas. Our work is people-centered and community-based. Above all, we work with the most vulnerable, and in order to claim and uphold their rights, we engage proactively with local government and community structures.

LWF Safeguarding Commitment

LWF World Service is committed to creating and maintaining a safe organization where people we come in contact with are protected from harm and abuse. Harm and abuse may include but are not limited to physical, psychological, and sexual violence and abuse, financial and material abuse, all forms of modern slavery, and all forms of maltreatment and exploitation.

Medical Teams International holds strict child and vulnerable adult safeguarding principles and a zero-tolerance policy for misconduct related to sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse in the workplace and other places where the organization’s activities are rendered. Parallel to technical competence, recruitment & selection, hiring decisions will give due emphasis to assessing candidates' eligibility thorough background checks, police clearance, and professional reference check processes. JOB SUMMARY Medical Officer contributes to the calling of Medical Teams International by providing quality consultation & health care services for internally displaced people, refugees and host community.The Medical Officer is responsible for delivering high-quality medical care, providing consultations, and supporting patients throughout their treatment journey. This role includes clinical assessments, diagnosis, treatment planning, patient education, and coordinating with multidisciplinary teams to ensure optimal patient outcomes. ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES Medical / Technical Provide consultations with diagnosis and treatment of illnesses based on the guidelines in Ethiopia and focusing initially on IMCI (Integrated Management of Childhood Illnesses) Support the treatment of co-infections in children diagnosed with severe acute malnutrition and referred to an appropriate outpatient treatment program. Provide appropriate referrals to the medical doctor or to the relevant referral sites in a timely fashion without delays Prescribe medications and instruct patients on correct usage based on guidelines Ensure medical supplies are available and support the projection of needs Provide patient education and instruct on prevention methods for illness, proper nutrition, and hygiene Compile weekly and monthly reports required by the Ministry of Health as well as UNHCR and provide to the clinic in-charge. Follow EPI routine/campaigns sessions at clinic and catchment Follow infection, prevention, and control protocols through maintaining good hand hygiene and appropriately using personal protective equipment Support the integration of accountability practices into program activities by following established procedures during planning, implementation, monitoring, and reporting. raw_data.title: Medical Officer
raw_data.description:
Medical Teams Calling   

Daring to love like Jesus, we boldly break barriers to health and restore wholeness in a hurting world.   

Medical Teams International holds strict child and vulnerable adult safeguarding principles and a zero-tolerance policy for misconduct related to sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse in the workplace and other places where the organization’s activities are rendered. Parallel to technical competence, recruitment & selection, hiring decisions will give due emphasis to assessing candidates' eligibility thorough background checks, police clearance, and professional reference check processes.  

JOB SUMMARY

Medical Officer contributes to the calling of Medical Teams International by providing quality consultation & health care services for internally displaced people, refugees and host community.The Medical Officer is responsible for delivering high-quality medical care, providing consultations, and supporting patients throughout their treatment journey. This role includes clinical assessments, diagnosis, treatment planning, patient education, and coordinating with multidisciplinary teams to ensure optimal patient outcomes. 

 ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES  

 Medical / Technical  

  • Provide consultations with diagnosis and treatment of illnesses based on the guidelines in Ethiopia and focusing initially on IMCI (Integrated Management of Childhood Illnesses)  
  • Support the treatment of co-infections in children diagnosed with severe acute malnutrition and referred to an appropriate outpatient treatment program.   
  • Provide appropriate referrals to the medical doctor or to the relevant referral sites in a timely fashion without delays  
  • Prescribe medications and instruct patients on correct usage based on guidelines  
  • Ensure medical supplies are available and support the projection of needs  
  • Provide patient education and instruct on prevention methods for illness, proper nutrition, and hygiene  
  • Compile weekly and monthly reports required by the Ministry of Health as well as UNHCR and provide to the clinic in-charge.  
  • Follow EPI routine/campaigns sessions at clinic and catchment  
  • Follow infection, prevention, and control protocols through maintaining good hand hygiene and appropriately using personal protective equipment  
  • Support the integration of accountability practices into program activities by following established procedures during planning, implementation, monitoring, and reporting. Help ensure that accountability is reflected in day-to-day tasks, team interactions, and when working with partners or communities. 
  • Support safeguarding of program participants and employees through promoting an environment of awareness and upholding the code of conduct provisions of Medical Teams Protection from Sexual Exploitation & Abuse, Child & Vulnerable Adult protection, and harassment-free workplace policies. Incumbents will remain alert and responsive to any child and adult safeguarding risks, acquire relevant knowledge and skills which will enable you to promote strong safeguarding practices, understand the child and adult safeguarding policy and procedures, and conduct yourself in a manner consistent with the Safeguarding. 

Quality Management  

  • Ensure all patients are treated based on the Guidelines of the Ministry of Health and the IMCI guidelines. 
  • Ensure rational use of drugs such that only those essential for treatment are prescribed. Do not overprescribe.  
  • Provide compassionate and respectful care to all patients who present to the clinic.  
  • Support other staff and colleagues to maintain good infection control practices to prevent spread of illnesses within the clinic and among the staff.

Operating under EIH, EBPE is developing an integrated pharmaceutical campus at the Kilinto Special Economic Zone in Addis Ababa, co-locating multiple manufacturing units that share infrastructure,talent, and corporate services. Job Summary I. The role ensures that all phases—design, construction, commissioning, qualification, validation, technology transfer, and operational readiness comply with EFDA, WHO PQ, and international GMP standards. The officer develops robust, risk-based quality systems tailored to vaccine, diagnostics and pharmaceutical manufacturing, and works closely with engineers, architects, contractors, and regulators to ensure construction activities meet regulatory and industry requirements. Key responsibilities include quality oversight of construction, inspections, documentation review, vendor and equipment qualification, and leadership of URS, FAT/SAT, commissioning, and validation activities. The role also manages non-conformities and drives corrective and preventive actions. The officer ensures the facility is built and prepared to operate as a modern, fully compliant, state-of-the-art vaccine manufacturing plant. II. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES / ACCOUNTABILITY A. Work closely with internal staff, international consultants, EPC contractors, and regulatory bodies. raw_data.description:
About Us

Ethio-BioPharma Enterprise (EBPE) is Ethiopia’s state-owned pharmaceutical manufacturing enterprise, established to build the nation’s capacity to manufacture vaccines, essential medicines, diagnostics, medical supplies and other healthcare technologies locally. Operating under EIH, EBPE is developing an integrated pharmaceutical campus at the Kilinto Special Economic Zone in Addis Ababa, co-locating multiple manufacturing units that share infrastructure,talent, and corporate services.

Job Summary

I. GENERAL POSITION DESCRIPTION

Main Purpose of the post

The Quality Assurance officer will provide strategic and operational leadership and expert oversight to establish and implement a comprehensive QA system for Ethio-biopharma Enterprise’s vaccine, Pharmaceutical & diagnostics manufacturing projects. The role ensures that all phases—design, construction, commissioning, qualification, validation, technology transfer, and operational readiness comply with EFDA, WHO PQ, and international GMP standards.

The officer develops robust, risk-based quality systems tailored to vaccine, diagnostics and pharmaceutical manufacturing, and works closely with engineers, architects, contractors, and regulators to ensure construction activities meet regulatory and industry requirements. Key responsibilities include quality oversight of construction, inspections, documentation review, vendor and equipment qualification, and leadership of URS, FAT/SAT, commissioning, and validation activities. The role also manages non-conformities and drives corrective and preventive actions.

The officer ensures the facility is built and prepared to operate as a modern, fully compliant, state-of-the-art vaccine manufacturing plant.

II. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES / ACCOUNTABILITY

A. Leadership

  1. Develop and implement the Quality Strategy aligned with Ethio-biopharma’s mission, regulatory expectations, and global best practices.
  2. Provide quality leadership across the enterprise and serve as the primary officer to the CEO on all quality and compliance matters.
  3. Establish and lead the Quality Management System (QMS) from the project phase through full-scale manufacturing.
  4. Ensure quality policies, governance structures, and performance indicators are well-defined and implemented.
  5. Work closely with internal staff, international consultants, EPC contractors, and regulatory bodies.
  6. Ensure GMP principles are observed in preparing architectural layouts, engineering designs, workflows, and contamination control strategies.
  7. Oversee detailed design reviews for compliance for Regulatory compliance
  8. Provide QA leadership during process design, method development, and validation planning.
  9. Plan, coordinate and monitor the Quality Assurance activities of the enterprise

B. Establishment of the QA System (Project to Manufacturing Phase)

  1. Leads the establishment of a phased QMS roadmap covering: Project Phase (non-GMP but quality-governed), Pre-Operational Phase, GMP Readiness Phase, and Commercial Manufacturing Phase.
  2. Leads the design and stepwise implementation of a phase-appropriate Quality Management System (QMS) that evolves from project stage requirements to full cGMP-compliant commercial manufacturing systems.
  3. Prepares all QMS documents including document control, change management, management review, deviation handling, CAPA, supplier qualification, and risk management.
  4. Develops quality oversight mechanisms for technology transfer partners, contractors, including EPC contractors, and consultants.
  5. Establishes systems to ensure compliance during procurement of equipment, utilities, and raw materials.
  6. Ensures construction activities support smooth transition into qualification, validation, and GMP operations.

C. Regulatory Compliance & Inspection Readiness

  1. Ensures full compliance with national (EFDA) and international standards (GMP, WHO, EMA where applicable).
  2. Leads preparation for regulatory inspections, external audits, and prequalification (e.g., WHO PQ) processes.
  3. Serves as the primary point of contact with regulatory authorities on quality matters.
  4. Maintains up-to-date awareness of evolving regulations and guide the organization in implementing changes.
  5. In collaboration with the RA officer for GMP & Regulatory Affairs, supports preparation and submission of facility licensing applications and product registration dossiers.
  6. Supports EFDA, WHO PQ, and other international regulatory inspections and ensure inspection readiness.
  7. Ensure that GMP principles and QA requirements are embedded into architectural layouts, engineering designs, workflows, personnel/material flows, and contamination control strategies.
  8. Lead QA integration into planning and design activities, working closely with internal staff, international consultants, EPC contractors, regulatory bodies, and other partners.

D. Validation, Qualification & Technology Transfer Oversight

  1. Oversees qualification of equipment, utilities, and cleanrooms.
  2. Participates in the preparation and QA review of User Requirement Specifications (URS) for equipment, systems, and facility components.
  3. Participates in Factory Acceptance Test (FAT), Site Acceptance Test (SAT), and related inspections from a QA and compliance perspective.
  4. Provides QA oversight during equipment installation, utility commissioning, and environmental system implementation.
  5. Oversees quality considerations during facility design, construction, commissioning, and qualification (DQ, IQ, OQ, and PQ).
  6. Approves validation master plans, validation protocols and ensure lifecycle validation of processes, cleaning, and analytical methods.
  7. Provides QA oversight of technology transfer activities with international partners.
  8. Ensures data integrity principles (ALCOA+, GAMP 5) are embedded in computerized systems and laboratory operations.
  9. Ensure technical transfer documents, protocols, and processes meet global GMP standards.
  10. Review and approve technology transfer plans, analytical method transfer protocols, and comparability assessments.
  11. Ensure quality, documentation, and data integrity expectations are met during transfers from technology transfer partners.
  12. Ensure readiness of facility, equipment, materials, and staff for receiving technology.
  13. Participate in and approve technology transfer quality requirements.

E. Quality Governance & Documentation

  1. Establishes and maintain the Document Management System.
  2. Approves all quality-critical SOPs, policies, protocols, and reports.
  3. Develops quality governance frameworks, including Quality manual and Management Reviews.
  4. Prepares quality reports for the CEO and Board as required.

F. Building & Leading the Quality Assurance Team

  1. Defines QA organizational structure and staffing plan appropriate for each project phase.
  2. Recruit, train, mentor, and evaluate QA personnel to build a high-performing quality culture.
  3. Promotes a strong culture of compliance, continuous improvement, and ethical conduct across the enterprise.

G. Project execution Quality Oversight

  1. Review design documents, construction drawings, specifications, and change orders for ultimate quality compliance.
  2. Ensure implementation alignment with regulatory requirements (EFDA, WHO PQ, and GMP).
  3. Provide QA oversight during material selection, equipment procurement, installation, and commissioning.
  4. Verify that critical materials (e.g., cleanroom panels, flooring, stainless steel piping, etc.) meet standards and compliant, traceable, and suitable for later qualification and validation.
  5. Work closely with consultants, engineering, contractors, procurement, and regulatory teams.
  6. Prepare and support inspections and audits during and after construction.
  7. Ensure accurate, complete, and controlled documentation for all project/construction activities.

H. Training, Auditing, and Technical Leadership

  1. Provide capacity-building initiatives by training internal staff, engineers, and operational teams on QA principles, GMP standards, contamination control, validation and regulatory expectations.
  2. Lead Core Quality Assurance operations like Self inspection/Internal audit, Annual product review, Out of Specification/Out of trend activities, and the like
  3. Conduct internal QA audits, gap assessments, deviation investigations, and CAPA management to drive continuous compliance improvement.
  4. Provides QA and regulatory input on technology transfer, process design, documentation systems, and operational readiness.
  5. Conduct periodic training on GMP, data integrity, and quality systems.

I. Operational Quality Oversight

  1. Oversee batch review, release procedures, and product disposition systems.
  2. Ensure Quality Risk Management (ICH Q9) is integrated into all operations.
  3. Build and oversee Good Documentation Practices (GDP) across the enterprise.
  4. Establish systems for complaints handling, product recall, and market surveillance.
  5. Ensure control of materials, supplier qualification, and vendor audits.

J. Continuous Improvement

  1. Lead continuous improvement initiatives using QRM, and other appropriate quality management tools.
  2. Analyze quality metrics and trends to drive preventive actions.
  3. Implement digitalization initiatives for QMS automation and data integrity strengthening.

K. Reporting and Planning

  1. Prepare weekly, monthly, quarterly, and annual QA work plans and performance reports for the CEO.
  2. Report on QA system establishment progress, validation and qualification status, risk assessments, internal audit, annual product review, regulatory compliance, etc..
  3. Provide strategic recommendations on quality risks and mitigation measures.

L. Authority

  1. Authorized for technical document approval, issuance and archive
  2. Approve/reject materials & products; batch release/rejection
  3. Approve SOPs, test methods, protocols, investigations, monitoring programs, and quality related project documents
  4. Approve training programs, operator qualifications
  5. Authorized for Line clearance, contamination control, process oversight
  6. Authorized to evaluate and address contractor/vendor non-compliance and recommend corrective preventive actions
  7. Approve quality related deliverables of consultants
  8. Authorized to approve, Validation Master Plans (VMPs), validation, qualification, and vendor-qualification.
  9. Block or quarantine any material or product that does not meet specifications.
  10. Suspend production activities during deviations, contamination risks, or facility failures.
  11. Stop any operation that poses a quality, GMP, safety, or data integrity risk.
  12. Approve URS (User Requirement Specifications) for all GMP critical systems/equipment.
  13. Authorize changes through the Change Control procedure.
  14. Authorize document issuance and archival.
  15. Approve final deviation, CAPA, OOS, OOT investigations.

M. Effort required

  1. Requires continuous analytical judgment, regulatory decision-making, and mental concentration.
  2. Involves periodic on-site inspections, facility walkthroughs, FAT/SAT witnessing, and construction oversight.
  3. Requires strong leadership in a multidisciplinary, fast-paced project environment.

The Quality Assurance and Regulatory Affair Officer is expected to carry out other related tasks as assigned by pertinent authority

Reports to: This positions reports to the CEO

Salary: As per the Organization's Scale

About the company

Teklehaimanot General Hospital is a patient-centered private hospital in the center of Addis Ababa that provides trusted multi-disciplinary medical services.
