Through decades of unwavering endeavor to be a patient-centered private hospital, TGH is proud to offer over 70 General, specialty, subspecialty, and supportive services with 402 dedicated staff, of which 329 are full-time employees and 73 are part-time and contractual employees equipped with a culture of medical teamwork. Its credit program serves over 100 companies, Local and international companies, sharing in the grandeur of full hospitality that builds lasting patient-to-care provider relationships. For seven consecutive years, TGH has been ranked “Green Level” general hospital.

Our Mission

Our Vision

Our Values

“To nurture all human beings principled in honesty through compassion with the utmost respect”
TGH, with a strong commitment to nurturing all human beings, upholds the principles of honesty, compassion, and utmost respect. Through its unwavering dedication to providing exceptional healthcare services, The Hospital strives to become a trusted institution, a place where patients find solace, comfort, and the promise of a brighter future.
At Teklehaimanot General Hospital the core value of “nurturing all human beings’’ resonates throughout every aspect of the organization. From the moment patients step through the doors, they are greeted with warmth and empathy. The hospital's dedicated team of healthcare and Customer service professionals understands the critical importance of treating patients not just as medical cases, but as individuals deserving of kindness, compassion, and personalized attention. Every patient is regarded as a unique story, and the hospital's mission is to provide holistic care that addresses both physical and emotional well-being.
“Honesty” is the bedrock upon which Teklehaimanot General Hospital stands. Transparent communication, ethical practices, and integrity are the guiding principles that shape every interaction within the hospital. Patients and their families can trust that they will receive accurate information about their conditions, treatment options, and the overall care process. The hospital's commitment to honesty ensures that patients are empowered to make informed decisions and actively participate in their healthcare journey.
“Compassion” is the lifeblood that flows through the veins of Teklehaimanot General Hospital. The hospital's healthcare professionals are not only highly skilled and knowledgeable but also deeply empathetic and understanding. They recognize that patients may be experiencing fear, pain, or uncertainty and go above and beyond to provide comfort and support. Whether it's holding a hand, offering a listening ear, or providing words of encouragement, the hospital's staff is devoted to fostering an environment that promotes healing and emotional well-being.
Above all, Teklehaimanot General Hospital treats every individual with “utmost respect”. Regardless of age, gender, socioeconomic status, or background, every patient is valued and treated with dignity. The hospital's commitment to respect extends to its commitment to cultural sensitivity and inclusivity. The diverse needs and beliefs of patients are honored, and efforts are made to create an environment that is welcoming and accommodating to all.

Why work for us

Choosing to work for Teklehaimanot General Hospital means joining a healthcare institution that values its employees, patients, and the community at large. We provide an environment that fosters professional growth, collaboration, and innovation, while emphasizing the importance of delivering exceptional patient care. With our commitment to excellence, cutting-edge facilities, and a supportive work culture, Teklehaimanot General Hospital offers a fulfilling and rewarding career path for healthcare professionals seeking to make a difference.  The following facts highlight the numerous benefits and opportunities that await prospective candidates who choose TGH.

We foster a collaborative and supportive work environment that encourages teamwork, communication, and professional growth. Our hospital values the contributions of each employee and believes in a culture of respect, inclusivity, and continuous learning. You will have the chance to work alongside skilled professionals from diverse backgrounds, creating a stimulating and enriching atmosphere that allows for personal and career development.
3. Opportunities for Professional Development:
We believe in investing in our employees' growth and development. Teklehaimanot General Hospital offers a range of opportunities for professional advancement, including ongoing training programs, workshops, conferences, and mentorship initiatives. Teklehaimanot General Hospital upholds the highest standards of integrity, ensuring that our employees work in an environment built on trust, honesty, and accountability. Repair & Maintenance Engineer_ Electrical

Position Title: Repair and Maintenance Engineer

Reports to: Senior Repair & Maintenance Supervisor

About EcoMobby:

EcoMobby Spare Parts is a trailblazer in Ethiopia's automotive industry, proudly standing as the nation's first dedicated spare parts shop for electric mobility vehicles (EMVs). Established in March, 2024, we are committed to supporting the burgeoning EV ecosystem and ensuring a seamless ownership experience for our customers. It’s currently looking to expand its team with exceptional talent that will ensure premium service to its customers.

Purpose of the position

The Repair and Maintenance Engineer will diagnose, repair, and maintain electrical systems of e-bikes to ensure safety, reliability, and high-quality service. Support uptime, reduce repeat failures, and maintain accurate repair documentation.

1. Core Responsibilities

A. Electrical Diagnostics & Repair

  • Diagnose and repair charger faults such as unstable voltage, no output, overheating, and abnormal noise using appropriate electrical testing tools.

  • Test ECU and control systems for power supply, communication, and signal issues; replace faulty units and verify system functionality after installation.

  • Inspect wiring harnesses and connectors for damage, loose terminals, short circuits, or corrosion; perform continuity testing where required.

  • Repair or replace defective components including connectors, wiring sections, and basic PCB elements.

  • Interpret wiring diagrams and schematics to systematically troubleshoot faults.

  • Perform post-repair functional testing to ensure safe and reliable operation before bike release.

B. Preventive Maintenance

  • Conduct routine electrical inspections as per maintenance schedule.

  • Identify and report early signs of electrical failure to prevent breakdowns and downtime..

C. Root Cause & Quality Control

  • Conduct basic root cause analysis for recurring electrical faults and document findings.

  • Escalate complex or unresolved issues to the supervisor in a timely manner.

  • Verify that all repaired bikes meet safety and functional standards before release.

D. Documentation

  • Ensure all repair activities are properly documented in the job card system and master log.

  • Escalate recurring or repeated faults for further investigation.

E. Team & Workplace Support

  • Work closely with cross-functional teams to resolve technical issues efficiently.

  • Provide guidance to junior technicians as required.

  • Uphold 5S and workplace safety standards at all times.

2. Performance Expectations

  • Complete at least 95% of repairs within the agreed time.

  • Keep repeat repair cases below 5%.

  • Ensure all repair records are accurate and completed daily.

  • Follow all safety rules at all times.

Required Skills

  • 2+ years of Experience in electrical diagnostics and repair (e-bike or similar systems is advantageous).

  • Ability to read wiring diagrams.

  • Skilled in using multimeter and electrical tools.

  • Basic soldering and PCB repair knowledge.

  • Strong problem-solving and attention to detail.

  • Workshop environment with exposure to tools, machinery, and occasional outdoor testing.

Duty Station: One of the following intervention woredas: Mai(t)sebri, Dima, Sheraro, Tahtay-Adyabo, Irob, Gulo-Mekeda, Sanja, Dabat, and Debark

Number of Positions: 9 (one per intervention woreda)

  • Duration: 12 months

Report To: Protection Officer

Organization: New Millennium Women Empowerment Organization (NMWEO)

Organizational Profile
1.1 General Information

New Millennium Women Empowerment Organization (NMWEO) is an indigenous, non-governmental, non-profit humanitarian organization established in 2007 in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. The organization was previously registered at the Ministry of Justice under registration number 3018 and later registered and licensed by the Federal Charities and Societies Agency as an Ethiopian resident’s charity by the Charities and Societal Proclamation No. 621/2009 by registration No. 0539. NMWEO has been re-registered according to the Civil Society Organizations Proclamation No.113/2019 with registration No. 0539.

Vision 

We envision a country in which women and girls have equal opportunity, claim their rights and free from any violence, and become effective social change agents.

Mission

Our mission is to empower Ethiopian women, girls, and youth in economic, political, and social dimensions, and help them unlock their potential in decision-making through capacity building, advocacy, leadership development, and humanitarian intervention programs.

Core Values and Belief

·       Humanity

·       Gender sensitive

·       Accountability

·       Equity

·       Teamwork and Excellence

·       Partnership and networking

Job Purpose

The Social Worker will support the implementation of community-based protection interventions at woreda and community level. The position will work directly with individuals, families, communities, and community structures to identify protection and social needs, strengthen community participation, facilitate access to appropriate services, and promote safe and inclusive community environments.

The Social Worker will contribute to strengthening community protection mechanisms, prevention of harmful practices, community mobilization, referral and follow-up, community action, and the effective functioning of protection-related services.

The position will apply social work principles, confidentiality, dignity, informed consent, safeguarding, PSEA, gender equality, disability inclusion, child protection, accountability, and Do No Harm throughout all activities.

Key Responsibilities

A.   Community-Based Social Work

  • Establish and maintain constructive relationships with community members and community structures.
  • Identify protection and social concerns affecting individuals, families, and communities.
  • Support communities to identify their own protection priorities and solutions.
  • Promote participation of women, girls, children, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
  • Provide appropriate basic social support within the scope of professional competence.
  • Maintain professional boundaries and confidentiality.

B.   Community Mobilization and Engagement

  • Mobilize and engage communities in project interventions.
  • Support community structures to participate effectively in protection activities.
  • Facilitate community dialogue and awareness activities.
  • Work with community and religious leaders to promote positive attitudes and practices that protect women, girls, and children.
  • Promote community ownership and sustainability of protection interventions.
  • Ensure community engagement is inclusive, conflict-sensitive, and culturally appropriate.

C.   Protection Identification and Referral

  • Identify individuals and groups experiencing or at risk of protection concerns.
  • Provide information on available services and support options.
  • Facilitate safe and appropriate referrals through established referral pathways.
  • Follow up on referrals when appropriate and in accordance with confidentiality and consent requirements.
  • Coordinate with service providers and relevant authorities as required.
  • Immediately report serious protection and safeguarding concerns through established procedures.

D.   Support to Community Protection Mechanisms

  • Support the Protection Officer in strengthening community protection structures.
  • Provide regular follow-up and technical support to community-based protection actors.
  • Support community structures to identify and address protection concerns.
  • Encourage community-based prevention and referral practices.
  • Document community concerns, actions, and feedback and share relevant information with the Protection Officer.

E.   Support to Women and Girls Safe Space

  • Support the safe and effective functioning of the WGSS.
  • Promote safe access and participation of women and girls.
  • Provide information and basic social support within the scope of the role.
  • Support linkages between WGSS users and appropriate specialized services.
  • Promote confidentiality, dignity, safety, accessibility, and respect.
  • Identify operational or protection concerns affecting women and girls and report them to the Protection Officer.

F.    Community Prevention and Social Support

  • Support community initiatives aimed at preventing protection risks and harmful practices.
  • Facilitate discussions that promote positive social norms and protective behaviors.
  • Support communities to develop and implement locally identified protection solutions.
  • Encourage positive family and community support systems.
  • Provide appropriate information and awareness on available protection and social services.

G.  Monitoring, Documentation and Reporting

  • Maintain accurate records of activities and community engagement.
  • Provide regular updates to the Protection Officer.
  • Support collection of project monitoring information and community feedback.
  • Document referrals and follow-up actions in accordance with confidentiality requirements.
  • Contribute to project reports, lessons learned, success stories, and case documentation where appropriate and ethically permissible.
  • Ensure all records are safely stored and protected.

H. Safeguarding and Accountability

  • Comply with NMWEO safeguarding, PSEA, child protection, code of conduct, data protection, and other relevant policies.
  • Maintain confidentiality and protect the privacy and dignity of community members.
  • Promote safe reporting of protection and safeguarding concerns.
  • Ensure that activities are implemented according to Do No Harm principles.
  • Promote accessibility and inclusion of persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups
  •   Inform communities about available feedback and complaint mechanisms.

fields.title: Project Accountant
fields.description: Main Duties & Responsibilities of the Position Holder: He/She shall: Ensure that the overall Supervision of the project Financial Activities are properly performed and follows up that the daily routines are carried out smoothly. Assist the Team Leader in all aspects of administrative actions. See to it that adequate stock of supplies are requested on time and maintained in accordance with the policy of LWF. Operate and maintain the project’s Accounts according to LWF-ET procedures. Participate in the preparation of annual/ Working Budget of the project jointly with the program staff. Prepare monthly Fund Request together with the program staff based on the planned activity for the period. Make sure that the monthly fund request is for the activities planned for that period only. Make sure that the finance part of the Quarterly Monitoring Report (QMR) of the project tally the Narrative part of the report Collect the monthly financial report of the project from head office finance every month and should discuss with the concerned project staff Code all disbursements & receipts according to LWF/ET procedure. Make sure that all disbursements are summarized according to the cost centers and account codes. Ensure that LWF Procurement Procedures are followed and relevant financial documents, such as purchase requisitions, proforma invoice, purchase order, and Goods receiving Notes are properly raised. Prepares and checks Financial Statements before they are sent to the Head Office every month and to reach Head Office before five days of the next month. It includes cash count balance. Prepare monthly bank reconciliation statements. Supervise the Store Keepers and see to it that the purchase storing and issuing of goods are processed strictly in accordance with LWF procedures. Make sure that all project Fixed Assets are registered properly in accordance with LWF procedures. Control and Assist the Secretary/Cashier in all financial matters. Prepare monthly Payroll/ Pay Sheet for Casual workers if any, based on the approved attendance and other relevant documents in consultation with the Team Leader . Together with the Team Leader , He is Answerable for all Purchases and Disbursements in regard to budgetary provisions and stipulations. Make sure that all necessary and appropriate taxes like 2% or 30% With Hold tax (WHT), Income taxes, pension contributions are deducted and paid to the concerned offices of government on time. Make sure that all disbursements are in accordance with LWF financial procedures. Make sure that all disbursements are not out of the Budget Allocated for each line items As a responsible head for accounts and personnel administration of the project, he makes surprise cash count & staff supervision, and reports to the Team Leader . Where the Accountant is not convinced about certain payments or payment procedures authorized by the Team Leader , he should explain his/her concerns. But if still there is disagreement, the accountant should refer to the Finance Manager at head office for advice. Follow procedure as outlined in LWF World Service Ethiopia Staff Rules, Collective Agreement and other Operation Manuals; Perform any other duties as assigned to him by the Team Leader or his designate. This Job Description may be revised by the LWF/WS- Ethiopia at any time as it deems necessary

company.description:
About the Lutheran World Federation (LWF)

We are a global communion of churches in the Lutheran tradition, living and working together for a just, peaceful, and reconciled world. LWF World Service is the humanitarian and development arm of the Lutheran World Federation. We are a widely recognized, international, faith-based organization working in over 20 countries. We seek to bring people of all backgrounds together in the common quest for justice, peace, and reconciliation in an increasingly complex and fragmented world.

Lutheran World Federation (LWF) in Ethiopia  

LWF World Service Ethiopia is a registered foreign charity, which has been operating in Ethiopia since 1973 implementing various development and humanitarian projects in different parts of Ethiopia. LWF World Service Ethiopia works closely with the Ethiopian Evangelical Church Mekane Yesus (EECMY), the Ethiopian Government, UN organizations and other funding partners. Its thematic areas include the promotion of food security and sustainable livelihood, sustainable natural resources management, emergency preparedness, response and rehabilitation, and capacity building. 

A commitment to the human rights of every individual, regardless of their status, guides our work, actions, and operations. We are particularly known for our timely, compassionate, and professional humanitarian work, and our field presence in hard-to-reach areas. Our work is people-centered and community-based. Above all, we work with the most vulnerable, and in order to claim and uphold their rights, we engage proactively with local government and community structures.

LWF Safeguarding Commitment

LWF World Service is committed to creating and maintaining a safe organization where people we come in contact with are protected from harm and abuse. Harm and abuse may include but are not limited to physical, psychological, and sexual violence and abuse, financial and material abuse, all forms of modern slavery, and all forms of maltreatment and exploitation.

company.description:
About the company

Coca-Cola was first bottled in Ethiopia’s capital, Addis Ababa, in 1959 by the Ethiopian Bottling Share Company, which later opened a second branch in Dire Dawa in 1965.

The two plants were nationalized in 1975 and ran as public companies until 1996 when they were bought by Ethiopian entrepreneurs through privatization. Just prior to this, in 1995, Coca-Cola Sabco bought shares in the business and, in 1999, signed joint venture agreement with Ethiopian owners. With its leadership working hand in hand with employees, the business has seen significant growth over the years. Processes and functions have improved, resulting in considerable sales increases. On July 02, 2016, SABMiller plc, The Coca-Cola Company and Gutsche Family Investments (controlling 80% of Coca-Cola South African Bottling Company (Sabco) officilay merged and created Africa’s largest Coca-Cola bottler - Coca-Cola Beverages Africa (CCBA)

With the aim of increasing its foot prints across the nation, a new plant was commissioned in 2016 at Bahir Dar having state-of-the-art production facility.

East Africa Bottling Share Company as a Coca Cola Franchise Bottler in Ethiopia under Coca-Cola Beverages Africa (CCBA) has three production plants in Addis Ababa, Dire Dawa and Bahir Dar with an aggressive expansion plan throughout the country, hence bringing the total number of employees to more than 1,800.


Our Vision

To Refresh Africa and Create Shared Value


Our Mission

• to be the Leading and Most admired Company in Africa


Refresh Africa every day and make our continent a better place for all 

Our Values

➢   We have a passion for the coca-cola business and for the brand

➢   We think and act like “owners” at all times

➢   We work and win in teams across the business

➢   Accountability is clear and personal

➢   We hare humble but confident in all we do

➢   Safety, quality, the environment, and our communities are integral to our working lives All of this we do it with the highest integrity

Why work for us

Why join us?

  • We always act with the belief of Growing our people, "grows the busi­ ness". Our people will always be our competitive advantage. Become part of a large community where employees get a chance to network and build connections.
  • We empower our people to learn a new skill on the job through self-direction. Work with many talented and experienced people who are able to guide employees' career development.
  • Our leaders possess ample expertise in the Industry making them ideal Mentors & Coaches. As we are made up of small teams, employees will get unique opportunities to learn a variety of skills.
  • Our Genetic make-up highly values teamwork, positive attitude, effective communication, diversity, innovative mindset, agility, and continuous learning.
  • We engage in executing our social responsibility where we operate making sure we play our part in alleviating social challenges with respect to community education, women entrepreneurship, environmental protection - This is the basis for a brighter future, built on a hand up, not a handout.
  • Work for a brand that is well-known internationally and instantly recognizable. Our brand has been a leading brand for over 130 years and still continues to grow because We are not constrained by traditional thinking but prefer to "think like a consumer" and take risks.

Team Benefits

company.name: Marie Stopes International Ethiopia
company.description:
About the company

Marie Stopes International (MSI) is one of the largest international Sexual Reproductive Health (SRH) and Family Planning (FP) organizations in the world. We are a results oriented social enterprise that develop efficient, effective and sustainable SRH/FP programmes around the world.

Marie Stopes International Ethiopia (MSIE), a partner of MSI, is currently undertaking a dramatic scale-up of health service delivery for low income women and couples in Ethiopia. This includes expanding services in clinics and rural outreach programs into new regions of Ethiopia and creating social franchising networks of private quality service providers.  MSIE announces information about job vacancies widely and encourages applications from all sectors of the community.  MSIE considers all applicants based on their abilities and will ensure no group is disadvantaged on the basis of disability, gender, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race (which includes colour, nationality and ethnic or national origins), religion or belief, economic or social class, sex, HIV/AIDs status and political affiliation.

MSIE also implements a Safeguarding Policy to safeguard and protect the rights of staff, children, young people and vulnerable sections of the community and to this end, successful candidates will need to sign MSIE’s ‘code of conduct’ and undergo a background check. The Safeguarding Policy includes an adult Safeguarding, dignity at work place, child safeguarding, human trafficking and anti-slavery, sexual harassment, equality and diversity.  MSIE applies zero tolerance approach for the violation such policies. 

MSIE is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to hiring and retaining female employees. The organization has flexible policies including: travel policy for pregnant and lactating women, flexible work hour for non-clinic staff without reducing the total working hour. Women employees have access to on-job mentorship which aim to create gender-sensitive and inclusive work environment. As such, qualified women are encouraged to apply 

 

Our Mission

Ensuring the Individual’s Right to Children by Choice not Chance.

Vision
To become a sustainable nationwide provider of high quality, integrated reproductive health/family planning services.

Our Values

1 Mission driven
With unwavering commitment, we exist to empower women and men to have children by choice not chance.

2 Client centred
We are dedicated to our clients and work tirelessly to deliver high-quality, high-impact services that meet their individual needs.

3 Accountable
We are accountable for our actions and focus on results, ensuring long term sustainability and increasing the impact of the Partnership.

4 Courageous
We recruit and nurture talented, passionate and brave people who have the courage to push boundaries, make tough decisions and challenge others in line with our mission.
 

Why work for us

MSI works in 37 countries around the world to help women and girls to have children by choice, not chance.

For an individual woman or girl, being able to choose when she has children means having the power to take control of her future.
It can mean having the ability to finish her education, pursue a career, look after the children she already has and ensure she remains healthy. MSI was founded in 1976 to provide the contraception and safe abortion services that give women and girls a choice. Since then, choice has been at the heart of everything that we do and our mission remains clear: to help women and girls to have children by choice, not chance.

MSI is a global organisation with 11,000 team members working in 37 countries to deliver our mission. Starting from one single clinic in London, our organisation has grown from one clinic in central London to become one of the world’s largest providers of high quality, affordable contraception and safe abortion services.
Over the last 40 years, we have touched the lives of more than 120 million women and girls, giving them the power to take control of their futures. But we know that there is much more to do, today there are over 230 million women who want to use contraception but can't and that number continues to grow.

fields.title: Mechanic
fields.description: Position Title: Mechanic Job Purpose To perform preventive, corrective, and breakdown maintenance of mechanical machinery and equipment to ensure reliable, safe, and efficient operation of production facilities. The position is responsible for inspection, troubleshooting, repair, adjustment, installation, and maintenance of mechanical systems while minimizing equipment downtime and supporting continuous production. Key Duties and Responsibilities Carry out preventive, corrective, and breakdown maintenance of production and utility equipment. Inspect mechanical equipment regularly to identify wear, defects, abnormal conditions, and potential failures. Diagnose mechanical faults and determine appropriate repair and maintenance requirements. Repair, replace, adjust, and align mechanical components such as bearings, shafts, gears, chains, sprockets, belts, pulleys, couplings, valves, pumps, and other machine parts. Perform mechanical maintenance on production-line equipment, conveyors, fillers, packers, compressors, pumps, mixers, and other associated machinery as applicable. Conduct machine dismantling, assembly, alignment, adjustment, and installation activities safely and correctly. Perform lubrication of machinery and equipment according to approved lubrication schedules and procedures. Monitor equipment operating conditions and identify unusual vibration, noise, temperature, leakage, or other signs of mechanical failure. Respond promptly to equipment breakdowns and carry out corrective actions to restore production safely and efficiently. Support maintenance activities during machine changeovers, installation, commissioning, and modification of equipment. Work closely with electrical, instrumentation, production, and other maintenance personnel to resolve equipment-related problems. Participate in planned preventive maintenance activities and ensure maintenance tasks are completed according to the maintenance schedule. Use appropriate hand tools, power tools, measuring instruments, and maintenance equipment safely and correctly. Conduct basic measurements and inspections to verify equipment alignment, clearances, dimensions, and operating conditions. Ensure that repaired equipment is properly tested and safe for operation before handing it over to the production team. Maintain accurate records of breakdowns, maintenance activities, spare parts used, equipment condition, and repair history. Report equipment defects, spare-part requirements, safety hazards, and other maintenance issues to the immediate supervisor. Maintain and properly use maintenance tools, equipment, and workshop facilities. Ensure proper housekeeping and 5S standards in the workshop and maintenance work areas. Follow lockout/tagout (LOTO), permit-to-work, machine isolation, and other applicable safety procedures before undertaking maintenance work. Ensure compliance with occupational health and safety, environmental, quality, food safety, GMP, and company requirements. Participate in root-cause analysis of repeated equipment failures and recommend corrective and preventive actions. Contribute to reducing machine downtime, maintenance costs, equipment failures, and production losses. Participate in continuous improvement activities to improve equipment reliability, availability, and overall equipment effectiveness (OEE). Perform other related duties assigned by the immediate supervisor.

About the company

Teklehaimanot General Hospital is a patient-centered private hospital in the center of Addis Ababa that provides trusted multi-disciplinary medical services. With a focus on quality and customer care, it has a distinctive, compassionate, and honest approach to serving the need of all patients. Devised with experienced and compassionate medical staff, TGH is a health coach and medical partner to cater to all medical care needs. “An earnest deed is worth more than silver and gold” so fairness in price, quality, and flexibility creates a shelter for hope and recovery.
Through decades of unwavering endeavor to be a patient-centered private hospital, TGH is proud to offer over 70 General, specialty, subspecialty, and supportive services with 402 dedicated staff, of which 329 are full-time employees and 73 are part-time and contractual employees equipped with a culture of medical teamwork. Its credit program serves over 100 companies, Local and international companies, sharing in the grandeur of full hospitality that builds lasting patient-to-care provider relationships. For seven consecutive years, TGH has been ranked “Green Level” general hospital.

Our Mission

  • To be among the premium and most preferred healthcare providers in East Africa

Our Vision

  • To provide quality health care services at a reasonable price 

Our Values

“To nurture all human beings principled in honesty through compassion with the utmost respect”
TGH, with a strong commitment to nurturing all human beings, upholds the principles of honesty, compassion, and utmost respect. Through its unwavering dedication to providing exceptional healthcare services, The Hospital strives to become a trusted institution, a place where patients find solace, comfort, and the promise of a brighter future.
At Teklehaimanot General Hospital the core value of “nurturing all human beings’’ resonates throughout every aspect of the organization. From the moment patients step through the doors, they are greeted with warmth and empathy. The hospital's dedicated team of healthcare and Customer service professionals understands the critical importance of treating patients not just as medical cases, but as individuals deserving of kindness, compassion, and personalized attention. Every patient is regarded as a unique story, and the hospital's mission is to provide holistic care that addresses both physical and emotional well-being.
“Honesty” is the bedrock upon which Teklehaimanot General Hospital stands. Transparent communication, ethical practices, and integrity are the guiding principles that shape every interaction within the hospital. Patients and their families can trust that they will receive accurate information about their conditions, treatment options, and the overall care process. The hospital's commitment to honesty ensures that patients are empowered to make informed decisions and actively participate in their healthcare journey.
“Compassion” is the lifeblood that flows through the veins of Teklehaimanot General Hospital. The hospital's healthcare professionals are not only highly skilled and knowledgeable but also deeply empathetic and understanding. They recognize that patients may be experiencing fear, pain, or uncertainty and go above and beyond to provide comfort and support. Whether it's holding a hand, offering a listening ear, or providing words of encouragement, the hospital's staff is devoted to fostering an environment that promotes healing and emotional well-being.
Above all, Teklehaimanot General Hospital treats every individual with “utmost respect”. Regardless of age, gender, socioeconomic status, or background, every patient is valued and treated with dignity. The hospital's commitment to respect extends to its commitment to cultural sensitivity and inclusivity. The diverse needs and beliefs of patients are honored, and efforts are made to create an environment that is welcoming and accommodating to all.

Why work for us

Choosing to work for Teklehaimanot General Hospital means joining a healthcare institution that values its employees, patients, and the community at large. We provide an environment that fosters professional growth, collaboration, and innovation, while emphasizing the importance of delivering exceptional patient care. With our commitment to excellence, cutting-edge facilities, and a supportive work culture, Teklehaimanot General Hospital offers a fulfilling and rewarding career path for healthcare professionals seeking to make a difference.  The following facts highlight the numerous benefits and opportunities that await prospective candidates who choose TGH.
1. Commitment to Patient Care:
At Teklehaimanot General Hospital, our primary focus is on delivering high-quality patient care. Our employees are driven by a shared mission to make a positive impact on the lives of individuals and their families. By working with us, you will have the opportunity to contribute to the well-being of the community and play a crucial role in saving lives and improving health outcomes.
2. Collaborative and Supportive Work Environment:
We foster a collaborative and supportive work environment that encourages teamwork, communication, and professional growth. Our hospital values the contributions of each employee and believes in a culture of respect, inclusivity, and continuous learning. You will have the chance to work alongside skilled professionals from diverse backgrounds, creating a stimulating and enriching atmosphere that allows for personal and career development.
3. Opportunities for Professional Development:
We believe in investing in our employees' growth and development. Teklehaimanot General Hospital offers a range of opportunities for professional advancement, including ongoing training programs, workshops, conferences, and mentorship initiatives. We encourage our employees to expand their knowledge and skills, fostering a culture of continuous professional development that supports career progression within the organization.
4. Competitive Compensation and Benefits:
We understand the importance of recognizing and rewarding our employees' hard work and dedication. Teklehaimanot General Hospital offers competitive compensation packages that are commensurate with industry standards, ensuring that employees feel valued and motivated. Additionally, we strictly adhere to privilege package that are stated on Ethiopian labor law.
5. Ethical and Transparent Practices:
As an organization, we prioritize ethical conduct and maintain transparency in our operations. Teklehaimanot General Hospital upholds the highest standards of integrity, ensuring that our employees work in an environment built on trust, honesty, and accountability. We are committed to maintaining a positive reputation and upholding the trust placed in us by our patients and the community.

Team Benefits

Teklehaimanot General Hospital has implemented a comprehensive range of employee benefits aimed at promoting employee well-being and job satisfaction. This write-up will explore the various employer benefits offered by Teklehaimanot General Hospital:

The organization was previously registered at the Ministry of Justice under registration number 3018 and later registered and licensed by the Federal Charities and Societies Agency as an Ethiopian resident’s charity by the Charities and Societal Proclamation No. 621/2009 by registration No. 0539. NMWEO has been re-registered according to the Civil Society Organizations Proclamation No.113/2019 with registration No. 0539. Vision We envision a country in which women and girls have equal opportunity, claim their rights and free from any violence, and become effective social change agents. Mission Our mission is to empower Ethiopian women, girls, and youth in economic, political, and social dimensions, and help them unlock their potential in decision-making through capacity building, advocacy, leadership development, and humanitarian intervention programs. Core Values and Belief · Humanity · Gender sensitive · Accountability · Equity · Teamwork and Excellence · Partnership and networking Job Purpose The Social Worker will support the implementation of community-based protection interventions at woreda and community level. The position will work directly with individuals, families, communities, and community structures to identify protection and social needs, strengthen community participation, facilitate access to appropriate services, and promote safe and inclusive community environments. The Social Worker will contribute to strengthening community protection mechanisms, prevention of harmful practices, community mobilization, referral and follow-up, community action, and the effective functioning of protection-related services. The position will apply social work principles, confidentiality, dignity, informed consent, safeguarding, PSEA, gender equality, disability inclusion, child protection, accountability, and Do No Harm throughout all activities. Key Responsibilities A. Community-Based Social Work Establish and maintain constructive relationships with community members and community structures. Identify protection and social concerns affecting individuals, families, and communities. Support communities to identify their own protection priorities and solutions. Promote participation of women, girls, children, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups. Provide appropriate basic social support within the scope of professional competence. Maintain professional boundaries and confidentiality. B. Community Mobilization and Engagement Mobilize and engage communities in project interventions. Support community structures to participate effectively in protection activities. Facilitate community dialogue and awareness activities. Work with community and religious leaders to promote positive attitudes and practices that protect women, girls, and children. Promote community ownership and sustainability of protection interventions. Ensure community engagement is inclusive, conflict-sensitive, and culturally appropriate. C. Protection Identification and Referral Identify individuals and groups experiencing or at risk of protection concerns. Provide information on available services and support options. Facilitate safe and appropriate referrals through established referral pathways. Follow up on referrals when appropriate and in accordance with confidentiality and consent requirements. Coordinate with service providers and relevant authorities as required. Immediately report serious protection and safeguarding concerns through established procedures. D. Support to Community Protection Mechanisms Support the Protection Officer in strengthening community protection structures. Provide regular follow-up and technical support to community-based protection actors. Support community structures to identify and address protection concerns. Encourage community-based prevention and referral practices. Document community concerns, actions, and feedback and share relevant information with the Protection Officer. E. Support to Women and Girls Safe Space Support the safe and effective functioning of the WGSS. Promote safe access and participation of women and girls. Provide information and basic social support within the scope of the role. Support linkages between WGSS users and appropriate specialized services. Promote confidentiality, dignity, safety, accessibility, and respect. Identify operational or protection concerns affecting women and girls and report them to the Protection Officer. F. Community Prevention and Social Support Support community initiatives aimed at preventing protection risks and harmful practices. Facilitate discussions that promote positive social norms and protective behaviors. Support communities to develop and implement locally identified protection solutions. Encourage positive family and community support systems. Provide appropriate information and awareness on available protection and social services. G. Monitoring, Documentation and Reporting Maintain accurate records of activities and community engagement. Provide regular updates to the Protection Officer. Support collection of project monitoring information and community feedback. Document referrals and follow-up actions in accordance with confidentiality requirements. Contribute to project reports, lessons learned, success stories, and case documentation where appropriate and ethically permissible. Ensure all records are safely stored and protected. H. Safeguarding and Accountability Comply with NMWEO safeguarding, PSEA, child protection, code of conduct, data protection, and other relevant policies. Maintain confidentiality and protect the privacy and dignity of community members. Promote safe reporting of protection and safeguarding concerns. Ensure that activities are implemented according to Do No Harm principles. Promote accessibility and inclusion of persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups Inform communities about available feedback and complaint mechanisms.

Our mission is to empower Ethiopian women, girls, and youth in economic, political, and social dimensions, and help them unlock their potential in decision-making through capacity building, advocacy, leadership development, and humanitarian intervention programs.

Core Values and Belief

·       Humanity

·       Gender sensitive

·       Accountability

·       Equity

·       Teamwork and Excellence

·       Partnership and networking

Job Purpose

The Social Worker will support the implementation of community-based protection interventions at woreda and community level. The position will work directly with individuals, families, communities, and community structures to identify protection and social needs, strengthen community participation, facilitate access to appropriate services, and promote safe and inclusive community environments.

The Social Worker will contribute to strengthening community protection mechanisms, prevention of harmful practices, community mobilization, referral and follow-up, community action, and the effective functioning of protection-related services.

The position will apply social work principles, confidentiality, dignity, informed consent, safeguarding, PSEA, gender equality, disability inclusion, child protection, accountability, and Do No Harm throughout all activities.

Key Responsibilities

A.   Community-Based Social Work

  • Establish and maintain constructive relationships with community members and community structures.
  • Identify protection and social concerns affecting individuals, families, and communities.
  • Support communities to identify their own protection priorities and solutions.
  • Promote participation of women, girls, children, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
  • Provide appropriate basic social support within the scope of professional competence.
  • Maintain professional boundaries and confidentiality.

B.   Community Mobilization and Engagement

  • Mobilize and engage communities in project interventions.
  • Support community structures to participate effectively in protection activities.
  • Facilitate community dialogue and awareness activities.
  • Work with community and religious leaders to promote positive attitudes and practices that protect women, girls, and children.
  • Promote community ownership and sustainability of protection interventions.
  • Ensure community engagement is inclusive, conflict-sensitive, and culturally appropriate.

C.   Protection Identification and Referral

  • Identify individuals and groups experiencing or at risk of protection concerns.
  • Provide information on available services and support options.
  • Facilitate safe and appropriate referrals through established referral pathways.
  • Follow up on referrals when appropriate and in accordance with confidentiality and consent requirements.
  • Coordinate with service providers and relevant authorities as required.
  • Immediately report serious protection and safeguarding concerns through established procedures.

D.   Support to Community Protection Mechanisms

  • Support the Protection Officer in strengthening community protection structures.
  • Provide regular follow-up and technical support to community-based protection actors.
  • Support community structures to identify and address protection concerns.
  • Encourage community-based prevention and referral practices.
  • Document community concerns, actions, and feedback and share relevant information with the Protection Officer.

E.   Support to Women and Girls Safe Space

  • Support the safe and effective functioning of the WGSS.
  • Promote safe access and participation of women and girls.
  • Provide information and basic social support within the scope of the role.
  • Support linkages between WGSS users and appropriate specialized services.
  • Promote confidentiality, dignity, safety, accessibility, and respect.
  • Identify operational or protection concerns affecting women and girls and report them to the Protection Officer.

F.    Community Prevention and Social Support

  • Support community initiatives aimed at preventing protection risks and harmful practices.
  • Facilitate discussions that promote positive social norms and protective behaviors.
  • Support communities to develop and implement locally identified protection solutions.
  • Encourage positive family and community support systems.
  • Provide appropriate information and awareness on available protection and social services.

G.  Monitoring, Documentation and Reporting

  • Maintain accurate records of activities and community engagement.
  • Provide regular updates to the Protection Officer.
  • Support collection of project monitoring information and community feedback.
  • Document referrals and follow-up actions in accordance with confidentiality requirements.
  • Contribute to project reports, lessons learned, success stories, and case documentation where appropriate and ethically permissible.
  • Ensure all records are safely stored and protected.

H. Safeguarding and Accountability

  • Comply with NMWEO safeguarding, PSEA, child protection, code of conduct, data protection, and other relevant policies.
  • Maintain confidentiality and protect the privacy and dignity of community members.
  • Promote safe reporting of protection and safeguarding concerns.
  • Ensure that activities are implemented according to Do No Harm principles.
  • Promote accessibility and inclusion of persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups
  •   Inform communities about available feedback and complaint mechanisms.

company.name: Repi Soap & Detergent PLC
company.description:
REPI SOAP & DETERGENT PLC formerly known as REPI Soap factory was established 1974 by the name Bianil Ethiopia Share Company by foreign investors of Swiss & Greek origin aiming to produce and distributed powdered detergent to East Africa market which was dominantly by Uniliver brand OMO. Less than a year after its formation, it was owned by the Ethiopian government & was managed under the direct supervision of the National Chemical Corporation and was re-established as a public enterprise in 1992 by the council of Ministers and was recapitalized by Birr 1,525,000.00.

 

At that time, the company main vision was  to compete  against  local & imported powder detergent through its famous brand “ROL” , due to the machinery age and technological issues there was an issue of wastage which nearly bankrupted the company but thanks to a pioneering idea of creating detergent bar (cake) in 1979, Repi gave birth to a new line of product and a new brand  “Ajax”. Again in 1994 production of a liquid detergent was introduced under the brand name ‘LARGO”

Following the earmarking of REPI Soap factory by the government for joint venture partnership , LINA PLC having registered its interest in the joint venture Commissioned Vision Consultancy PVT LTD CO to undertake a series of studies on the factory with the aim of concluding a joint venture agreement with the factory management and the E.F.D.R Privatization & Public Enterprise Supervising Authority.

 

A joint venture partnership between “LENA PLC” and E.F.D.R Privatization & Public Enterprise Supervising Authority (PESSA) was then established  during the fiscal  period 2007/2008 after intensive negotiation was carried out between both parties involved which there after paved the way for the establishment of REPI SOAP & DETERGENT SHARE COMPANY.

 

LINA PLC is a share company  mainly involved  in trading ,real estate  and small scale manufacturing of corrugated steel & tea and added REPI SOAP & DETERGENT PLC to its portfolio of investment by acquiring 51% of share amounting to Birr 9,360,000.00 of the total share amounting to 18,360 ,000 while the remaining 49% amounting to birr 9,000,000 was raised by PESSA in the form of assets based on business evaluation of the factory.

The joint venture arrangement lasted one year followed by a full takeover of the share company by

LENA PLC after settling of the remaining 49% share previously held by the Ethiopian government.

 

 In response to the growing demands of the soap & detergent, today our company is a leading player  and well respected organization in the country detergent industry. The current market demand for our product and the fact that the current factory could not provide us the product volume due to imperfect condition and age of machinery and equipment’s therefore not supplying the capacity required ,we are committed to exciting expansion project  which is in a final phase ,would be beneficial for the shareholder ,employees local businesses and overall the company. In this sector REPI has positioned itself at the fore-front of the market.

In July,2014 Repi Soap and Detergent S. Co. (Repi) and Wilmar International Limited (Wilmar) have signed a joint investment agreement for the upgrading of an existing manufacturing facility in Sebeta Road, Kolfe Karenio Sub City and building of a new integrated manufacturing complex in Dima, Sebeta Town, Oromia Region in Ethiopia that will house an edible oil refinery and packing plant, production plants for specialty fats, soft oils, soaps and detergents, as well as a facility for sesame seed processing. Repi and Wilmar will each have a 50%participation in the joint investment.

Repi is a sister company of AL-SAM Private Limited Company, incorporated and existing under the laws of the Democratic Republic of Ethiopia. It engages in the manufacturing of soap and detergent products. Headquartered in Singapore, Wilmar is Asia’s leading agribusiness group engaging in oil palm cultivation, oilseed crushing, edible oils refining, sugar milling and refining, specialty fats, oleo-chemical, biodiesel and fertilizer manufacturing, and grain processing. It has a presence in 14 countries across Africa. This joint investment marks Wilmar’s first operations in Ethiopia.

Combining the expertise of both parties, the joint investment will have a positive impact on the development of the manufacturing and export sector, as well as create employment opportunities in Ethiopia.



About Wilmar

﻿

Wilmar International Limited, founded in 1991 and headquartered in Singapore, is today Asia’s leading agribusiness group. Wilmar is ranked amongst the largest listed companies by market capitalisation on the Singapore Exchange.Wilmar’s business activities include oil palm cultivation, oilseed crushing, edible oilsrefining, sugar milling and refining, specialty fats, oleochemical, biodiesel and fertiliser manufacturing, and grain processing.

At the core of Wilmar’s strategy is a resilient integrated agribusiness model that encompasses the entire value chain of the agricultural commodity processing business, from origination and processing to branding, merchandising and distribution of a wide range of agricultural products. It has over 450 manufacturing plants and an extensive distribution network covering China, India, Indonesia and some 50 other countries. The Group is backed by a multinational workforce of about 90,000 people. Wilmar’s portfolio of high quality processed agricultural products is the preferred choice of the food manufacturing industry, as well as the industrial and consumer food businesses. Its consumer-packed products occupy a leading share in its targeted markets. Through scale, integration and the logistical advantages of its business model, Wilmar is able to extract margins at every step of the value chain, thereby reaping operational synergies and cost efficiencies.

Wilmar remains a firm advocate of sustainable growth and is committed to its role as a responsible corporate citizen.

raw_data.title: Deputy Project Director / Chief of Party
raw_data.description:
About Opian

Opian is an Ethiopian health-technology and innovation company building decision infrastructure for stronger health systems. We combine deep knowledge of how care and supply chains operate, human-centred product design, data engineering and responsible artificial intelligence. Our work helps health workers, managers and public institutions turn fragmented data into timely decisions—so essential medicines, vaccines and services are available where and when people need them.

Our philosophy

We believe useful innovation is not novelty for its own sake. It is the disciplined work of understanding a real problem, challenging assumptions, building and testing a better response, measuring what changes, and strengthening the institutions that must sustain the result. Technology is valuable only when it improves a decision, a workflow or an outcome in the real operating environment.

· Start with reality: design around the health workers, workloads, incentives, infrastructure and constraints that actually exist—not an imported ideal workflow.

· Build with people, not for them: government counterparts and frontline users are co-designers, decision-makers and eventual owners, not passive recipients.

· Strengthen the system, not a standalone application: connect workflows, data, institutions and incentives so information can lead to action across every level.

· Push boundaries responsibly: make ambitious but testable bets, protect safety and privacy, and change direction quickly when evidence contradicts the original idea.

· Make capability local and durable: transfer knowledge, product ownership and operational responsibility so progress continues without permanent dependence on an external project team.

· Be honest about impact: distinguish deployment from adoption and activity from results; make claims specific, measurable and open to verification.

What this means for candidates

Opian is looking for accomplished specialists who are also builders. Candidates should bring exceptional depth in their discipline, intellectual courage, practical judgment and the humility to learn from users and evidence. We value people who can move from ambiguity to a testable approach, from a workshop to an operating routine, and from a promising pilot to an institutionally owned system. The standard is simple: show not only what you know, but what you personally built, changed, tested, learned and left stronger.

· Work across public health, supply chain, policy, product, technology and field implementation boundaries.

· Turn expertise into usable products, processes, decisions and measurable improvements—not reports alone.

· Operate with urgency while preserving quality, public trust, data protection, service continuity and government ownership.


Role purpose

Translate the program strategy into disciplined day-to-day execution. The Deputy Project Director will run the integrated delivery system, coordinate technical and field teams, manage dependencies, maintain delivery standards and act for the Project Director when delegated.

Key responsibilities

· Maintain the integrated master workplan, milestone schedule, dependency map, decision log, risk register and action tracker.

· Coordinate product, supply-chain, interoperability, implementation, government-partnership, finance and evaluation teams around a single delivery cadence.

· Chair weekly delivery reviews and ensure that unresolved constraints are escalated with clear options and accountable owners.

· Oversee recruitment, onboarding, deployment and performance management of program personnel and partner teams.

· Ensure that regional and facility implementation experience is incorporated rapidly into product and policy decisions.

· Manage operational readiness for assessments, workshops, releases, field deployments, training, supervision and evaluation activities.

· Ensure complete and timely technical, operational and financial reporting, supported by verifiable evidence.

· Coordinate procurement, subaward administration, logistics, safety and project-specific compliance requirements.

· Lead continuity planning and maintain effective operations during leadership absences or periods of rapid scale-up.

Expected results

· One integrated delivery plan connecting technical releases, field readiness, governance decisions and evaluation milestones.

· Predictable delivery with early identification and resolution of cross-workstream dependencies.

· Accurate management information and timely corrective actions.

· Well-functioning teams and partners with clear roles, standards and performance expectations.

fields.title: AI Automation Consultant
fields.description: AI Automation Consultant Remote · Full-time We build and run software that schedules work crews, texts them their jobs, and handles what they get paid. It runs live every day for real businesses. If it breaks, real people don't get told where to go, and real money goes to the wrong place. An AI writes most of the code. We need someone to decide what gets built, and to catch the AI when it gets it wrong -- because it does, and it always sounds confident. What we pay $1,000 a month to start. We review it after your first few weeks, and again once you've shown what you can do. The step up from this job is Client Lead -- you'd run a client on your own and be the person they talk to. It pays significantly more, and we fill it by promoting someone who's already doing this job well. That's where this role is meant to lead. What you'll do Take a vague complaint -- "the schedule is wrong sometimes" -- and work out what's actually happening before changing anything. Write down what a new feature should do, and just as importantly what it should not do, before any code is written. Use the AI to build it, then check its work properly. Read the code like someone is trying to slip something past you. Test on real data with the feature switched off, then switch it on and watch. Nothing goes straight to texting a hundred people. When something breaks: stop the damage, find everything affected, then fix the cause -- not just the one thing that got reported. Write short, clear updates. Most days that's how your team knows what's going on. Who does well here You've built something real. One thing is enough. Something messy, that other people ended up depending on. We'd rather hear about that than a list of technologies. You don't take "it works" for an answer. A passing test and a green dashboard don't settle it for you. You go and check. You think about what happens when things go wrong -- bad input, the same job running twice, someone in a different timezone, a message that says "sent" but never arrived. You're fine saying "I don't know yet, here's how I'd find out." You don't need a degree, a particular language, or years of experience. You do need good judgment, and we test for that directly instead of guessing from your CV. This isn't for you if you want tickets handed to you with the thinking already done, or if you'd ship the AI's first answer because it looked right. How to apply https://volt-os-production-4bc9.up.railway.app/apply Fill in a short form, verify who you are with Telegram, and a 20-minute timed test starts straight away. Do it when you have twenty quiet minutes and decent internet -- you only get one go at it. In the form, tell us about one thing you built that mattered. What was unclear at the start, what you got wrong, and how you found out. That's the part we read closely. What happens after Timed test -- arithmetic, patterns, following written instructions (20 min) Written questions about real situations from the system (~2 hrs) A repo with a bad change hidden in it, and some unfamiliar code to get into (~4-5 hrs) A conversation -- real problems, out loud (~2 hrs) Paid trial, real work, everything reviewed (2-4 weeks) Steps 1-4 are unpaid. The trial is paid from your first day. Most people don't get past step 3. That's expected -- the whole job is about holding a high bar, so we'd rather find out early than three months in. If you need something changed to take this fairly -- extra time, a screen reader, a different format -- just tell us before you start. Asking costs you nothing and isn't part of the test.

The step up from this job is Client Lead -- you'd run a client on your own and be the person they talk to. It pays significantly more, and we fill it by promoting someone who's already doing this job well. That's where this role is meant to lead.

What you'll do

  • Take a vague complaint -- "the schedule is wrong sometimes" -- and work out what's actually happening before changing anything.

  • Write down what a new feature should do, and just as importantly what it should not do, before any code is written.

  • Use the AI to build it, then check its work properly. Read the code like someone is trying to slip something past you.

  • Test on real data with the feature switched off, then switch it on and watch. Nothing goes straight to texting a hundred people.

  • When something breaks: stop the damage, find everything affected, then fix the cause -- not just the one thing that got reported.

  • Write short, clear updates. Most days that's how your team knows what's going on.

Who does well here

  • You've built something real. One thing is enough. Something messy, that other people ended up depending on. We'd rather hear about that than a list of technologies.

  • You don't take "it works" for an answer. A passing test and a green dashboard don't settle it for you. You go and check.

  • You think about what happens when things go wrong -- bad input, the same job running twice, someone in a different timezone, a message that says "sent" but never arrived.

  • You're fine saying "I don't know yet, here's how I'd find out."

You don't need a degree, a particular language, or years of experience. You do need good judgment, and we test for that directly instead of guessing from your CV.

This isn't for you if you want tickets handed to you with the thinking already done, or if you'd ship the AI's first answer because it looked right.

How to apply

https://volt-os-production-4bc9.up.railway.app/apply

Fill in a short form, verify who you are with Telegram, and a 20-minute timed test starts straight away. Do it when you have twenty quiet minutes and decent internet -- you only get one go at it.

In the form, tell us about one thing you built that mattered. What was unclear at the start, what you got wrong, and how you found out. That's the part we read closely.

What happens after

  1. Timed test -- arithmetic, patterns, following written instructions (20 min)

  2. Written questions about real situations from the system (~2 hrs)

  3. A repo with a bad change hidden in it, and some unfamiliar code to get into (~4-5 hrs)

  4. A conversation -- real problems, out loud (~2 hrs)

  5. Paid trial, real work, everything reviewed (2-4 weeks)

Steps 1-4 are unpaid. The trial is paid from your first day.

Most people don't get past step 3. That's expected -- the whole job is about holding a high bar, so we'd rather find out early than three months in.

If you need something changed to take this fairly -- extra time, a screen reader, a different format -- just tell us before you start. Asking costs you nothing and isn't part of the test.

About Opian

Opian is an Ethiopian health-technology and innovation company building decision infrastructure for stronger health systems. We combine deep knowledge of how care and supply chains operate, human-centred product design, data engineering and responsible artificial intelligence. Our work helps health workers, managers and public institutions turn fragmented data into timely decisions—so essential medicines, vaccines and services are available where and when people need them.

Our philosophy

We believe useful innovation is not novelty for its own sake. It is the disciplined work of understanding a real problem, challenging assumptions, building and testing a better response, measuring what changes, and strengthening the institutions that must sustain the result. Technology is valuable only when it improves a decision, a workflow or an outcome in the real operating environment.

· Start with reality: design around the health workers, workloads, incentives, infrastructure and constraints that actually exist—not an imported ideal workflow.

· Build with people, not for them: government counterparts and frontline users are co-designers, decision-makers and eventual owners, not passive recipients.

· Strengthen the system, not a standalone application: connect workflows, data, institutions and incentives so information can lead to action across every level.

· Push boundaries responsibly: make ambitious but testable bets, protect safety and privacy, and change direction quickly when evidence contradicts the original idea.

· Make capability local and durable: transfer knowledge, product ownership and operational responsibility so progress continues without permanent dependence on an external project team.

· Be honest about impact: distinguish deployment from adoption and activity from results; make claims specific, measurable and open to verification.

What this means for candidates

Opian is looking for accomplished specialists who are also builders. Candidates should bring exceptional depth in their discipline, intellectual courage, practical judgment and the humility to learn from users and evidence. We value people who can move from ambiguity to a testable approach, from a workshop to an operating routine, and from a promising pilot to an institutionally owned system. The standard is simple: show not only what you know, but what you personally built, changed, tested, learned and left stronger.

· Work across public health, supply chain, policy, product, technology and field implementation boundaries.

· Turn expertise into usable products, processes, decisions and measurable improvements—not reports alone.

· Operate with urgency while preserving quality, public trust, data protection, service continuity and government ownership.

Role purpose

Own the future-state technical architecture and ensure that ForLab+ and related components integrate securely and sustainably with Ethiopia’s national digital-health ecosystem, authoritative registries and existing transactional systems.

Key responsibilities

· Assess current applications, infrastructure, registries, standards, data flows, interfaces, ownership and technical debt relevant to the supply chain.

· Define the target architecture, integration patterns, data contracts, security model, deployment model and phased transition roadmap.

· Ensure authoritative use of the Master Facility Registry, National Product Catalog and other approved registries without creation of competing internal sources of truth.

· Design interoperability with logistics, warehouse, enterprise-resource, cold-chain, service-delivery and health-information systems as prioritized.

· Set engineering standards for APIs, messaging, identity and access, auditability, offline synchronization, observability, testing and documentation.

· Lead architecture reviews, technical risk decisions, integration testing, performance testing, security assurance and release readiness.

· Ensure traceable transformation from source transactions to integrated datasets, alerts and downstream analytics.

· Design for intermittent connectivity, realistic support capacity, open standards, maintainability and reasonable recurrent costs.

· Develop technical documentation, source-code and configuration custody arrangements, administrator training and government handover plans.

Expected results

· A stakeholder-approved current-state assessment and future-state architecture.

· Secure, documented and tested integrations with prioritized national systems and registries.

· A production-ready platform with observable performance, auditable data flows and reliable offline operation where required.

· Government technical teams able to administer, support and evolve the deployed solution.

The overall role of the field medic is to provide medical support to DRC NTS/EPRE field teams and medical advisory to HDP humanitarian mine action operations.

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

The DRC Humanitarian Disarmament and Peacebuilding (HDP) Field Medic shall:

  • Provide emergency medical aid to deployed teams in accordance with IMAS ICP level requirements.
  • Offer medical support and guidance to deployed teams on all health-related concerns.
  • Provide the Operations Manager with oversight and updates on all medical matters.
  • Ensure that NTS/EORE teams are fully equipped and trained in accordance with the in DRC HDP SOP on Medical Support in Mine Action.
  • Ensure the ability to perform all medical duties professionally and effectively in line with operational standards.
  • Verify that all staff are qualified and competent to carry out their assigned duties in support of clearance operations, in accordance with the definition of qualified personnel.
  • Maintain accurate reporting mechanisms and produce timely records and reports on all medical activities, in line with the DRC HDP SOP on Medical Support in Mine Action.
  • Conduct regular casualty evacuation (CASEVAC) drills in coordination with the Technical Field Manager (TFM) and Team leader (TL).
  • Provide direction, supervision, and advice to DRC HDP personnel regarding health and medical issues.
  • Support the Operations Manager in the investigation of accidents or incidents, ensuring all relevant medical reports are compiled accurately.

It is the disciplined work of understanding a real problem, challenging assumptions, building and testing a better response, measuring what changes, and strengthening the institutions that must sustain the result. What this means for candidates Opian is looking for accomplished specialists who are also builders. raw_data.title: Chief Solution Architect and Interoperability Lead
raw_data.description:
About Opian

Opian is an Ethiopian health-technology and innovation company building decision infrastructure for stronger health systems. We combine deep knowledge of how care and supply chains operate, human-centred product design, data engineering and responsible artificial intelligence. Our work helps health workers, managers and public institutions turn fragmented data into timely decisions—so essential medicines, vaccines and services are available where and when people need them.

Our philosophy

We believe useful innovation is not novelty for its own sake. It is the disciplined work of understanding a real problem, challenging assumptions, building and testing a better response, measuring what changes, and strengthening the institutions that must sustain the result. Technology is valuable only when it improves a decision, a workflow or an outcome in the real operating environment.

· Start with reality: design around the health workers, workloads, incentives, infrastructure and constraints that actually exist—not an imported ideal workflow.

· Build with people, not for them: government counterparts and frontline users are co-designers, decision-makers and eventual owners, not passive recipients.

· Strengthen the system, not a standalone application: connect workflows, data, institutions and incentives so information can lead to action across every level.

· Push boundaries responsibly: make ambitious but testable bets, protect safety and privacy, and change direction quickly when evidence contradicts the original idea.

· Make capability local and durable: transfer knowledge, product ownership and operational responsibility so progress continues without permanent dependence on an external project team.

· Be honest about impact: distinguish deployment from adoption and activity from results; make claims specific, measurable and open to verification.

What this means for candidates

Opian is looking for accomplished specialists who are also builders. Candidates should bring exceptional depth in their discipline, intellectual courage, practical judgment and the humility to learn from users and evidence. We value people who can move from ambiguity to a testable approach, from a workshop to an operating routine, and from a promising pilot to an institutionally owned system. The standard is simple: show not only what you know, but what you personally built, changed, tested, learned and left stronger.

· Work across public health, supply chain, policy, product, technology and field implementation boundaries.

· Turn expertise into usable products, processes, decisions and measurable improvements—not reports alone.

· Operate with urgency while preserving quality, public trust, data protection, service continuity and government ownership.

Role purpose

Own the future-state technical architecture and ensure that ForLab+ and related components integrate securely and sustainably with Ethiopia’s national digital-health ecosystem, authoritative registries and existing transactional systems.

Key responsibilities

· Assess current applications, infrastructure, registries, standards, data flows, interfaces, ownership and technical debt relevant to the supply chain.

· Define the target architecture, integration patterns, data contracts, security model, deployment model and phased transition roadmap.

· Ensure authoritative use of the Master Facility Registry, National Product Catalog and other approved registries without creation of competing internal sources of truth.

· Design interoperability with logistics, warehouse, enterprise-resource, cold-chain, service-delivery and health-information systems as prioritized.

· Set engineering standards for APIs, messaging, identity and access, auditability, offline synchronization, observability, testing and documentation.

· Lead architecture reviews, technical risk decisions, integration testing, performance testing, security assurance and release readiness.

· Ensure traceable transformation from source transactions to integrated datasets, alerts and downstream analytics.

· Design for intermittent connectivity, realistic support capacity, open standards, maintainability and reasonable recurrent costs.

· Develop technical documentation, source-code and configuration custody arrangements, administrator training and government handover plans.

Expected results

· A stakeholder-approved current-state assessment and future-state architecture.

· Secure, documented and tested integrations with prioritized national systems and registries.

· A production-ready platform with observable performance, auditable data flows and reliable offline operation where required.

· Government technical teams able to administer, support and evolve the deployed solution.
