fields.title: Account Manager
fields.description: The Account Manager – Enterprise Segment is responsible for driving enterprise sales by developing and managing strategic relationships with government institutions, large corporations, financial institutions, and international organizations. The role focuses on promoting and selling enterprise IT solutions, including servers, storage solutions, networking equipment, workstations, and related technologies. The successful candidate will identify new business opportunities, manage key accounts, support tender activities, and collaborate with internal teams to deliver tailored enterprise solutions that maximize customer value and business growth. Key Responsibilities Develop and execute sales strategies to drive growth in the enterprise segment. Identify, pursue, and secure new business opportunities with government, corporate, financial, and international clients. Manage key enterprise accounts to ensure customer satisfaction, retention, and business growth. Build and maintain strong relationships with C-level executives, IT leaders, procurement teams, and other key stakeholders. Prepare and deliver sales presentations, proposals, quotations, and negotiate commercial agreements. Collaborate with the Tender Manager on identifying, preparing, and responding to enterprise tenders. Work closely with pre-sales and technical teams to deliver tailored enterprise IT solutions. Promote enterprise products, including servers, storage solutions, networking equipment, switches, and workstations. Develop and maintain strategic relationships with technology vendors and partners. Monitor market trends, competitor activities, and customer needs to identify new opportunities. Achieve sales targets while maintaining accurate sales forecasts, pipeline updates, and CRM records. Qualifications Education Bachelor's Degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business Management, Marketing, Electrical Engineering, or a related field. Experience working with enterprise, government, or private sector clients is highly preferred. Experience participating in tender processes is an advantage. Required Skills & Competencies Strong knowledge of enterprise IT products and solutions. Proven ability to achieve sales targets and manage enterprise accounts. Excellent communication, negotiation, presentation, and relationship-building skills. Strong business acumen with the ability to engage executive-level stakeholders. Experience preparing proposals, quotations, and tender documents. Proficiency in Microsoft Office and CRM systems. Strong organizational, time management, and multitasking skills. Ability to work independently, collaborate across teams, and travel as required.

About the company

WE ASPIRE TO BE BEST IN CLASS BANK IN AFRICA

Dashen is the most reputable brand in the domestic banking market; a reputation earned through consistent delivery of values and preeminence unmatched by its competitors and aspires to be "Best In Class Bank in Africa". The Bank also works in partnership with leading brands in the electronic payments industry


OUR PROFILE

Dashen Bank was founded in September 1995. Dashen Bank coined its name from the highest peak in Ethiopia, mount Dashen, and aspires to be the Best in Class Bank in Africa. Headquartered in Addis Ababa, the Bank is among the biggest private Banks in Ethiopia. Dashen is the most reputable brand in the domestic banking market; a reputation earned Ethiopia. It operates through a network of more than 900 plus Branches, nine dedicated Forex Bureaus, 1100 plus ATMs and 2,000 plus Point-of-Sale (POS) terminals spread across the length and breadth of the nation. Wherever business takes customers around the world, Dashen Bank is already there.

.

Our Mission

To provide efficient customer-centric banking service using the expertise of inspired professionals and cutting-edge technology, while creating sustainable value for our stakeholders


Vision

To be the best-in-class bank in Africa


Our Values

  • Customer centricity
  • Diversity
  • Professionalism
  • Teamwork
  • Integrity
  • Social responsibility

Why work for us

Dashen Bank is one of the most renowned leading financial giants in the industry. Dashen Bank has received several accolades for its operation and financial achievements. Dashen is also known for introducing breakthrough technologies to the financial industry. Apart from its financial success, Dashen is also prominent in supporting different causes and actively engaging in different CSR initiatives donating millions of birr to social, economic, and environmental causes.


When you work for Dashen, you are working for a leading financial institution and winning team of bankers. Moreover, you will be part of our CSR initiative. Dashen Bank provides you with a conducive environment to work learn and grow. Moreover, It will also provide you with fringe benefits along with attractive remuneration.


TRAINING AND DEVELOPMENT

Training and development are identified as one of the key strategic success factors in the organization. To this end, Dashen Bank Invests in millions to training and development. Immense training is conducted for employees and executive managers through partnering with renowned domestic and foreign training companies. Dashen Bank also sends employees abroad for an exposure visit and to equip them with the necessary knowledge and skills.

Team Benefits

Dashen Bank Provides several benefit package for its employees. Among other things the following are the major ones:-

  • Medical coverage (including family)
  • Attractive Remuneration
  • Allowances (transportation, representation, and others)
  • Credit opportunities (residence and vehicle)
  • Emergency Salary Allowances



WORK ENVIRONMENT

Dashen Bank provides employees with a conducive environment to carry out their tasks properly. Its 21 stories high-rise building in Addis Ababa is regarded as one of the modern buildings in Ethiopia. The Bank provides better corporate and Job conditions whereby employees are valued.

fields.title: IYCF Supervisor
fields.description: Medical Teams Calling Daring to love like Jesus, we boldly break barriers to health and restore wholeness in a hurting world. Medical Teams International holds strict child and vulnerable adult safeguarding principles and a zero-tolerance policy for misconduct related to sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse in the workplace and other places where the organization’s activities are rendered. Parallel to technical competence, recruitment & selection, hiring decisions will give due emphasis to assessing candidates' eligibility thorough background checks, police clearance, and professional reference check processes. JOB SUMMARY The IYCF Supervisor will contribute to the mission of Medical Teams by ensuring the integration of IYCF in emergency with overall Nutrition and Health services for vulnerable refugee and host populations in Ethiopia. This role will support Health Centers, Health Posts, and communities, coordinating IYCF in emergency strategies, providing nutrition education, and enhancing health outcomes for mothers and children in the project areas. ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES Serve as the primary point of contact between Medical Teams and local beneficiaries involved in IYCF activities. Assist Government staff and lead mothers on counsel and strengthen the ECD/IYCF project in the OTP and SC sites and community level. Promote gender equity and equality through each level of nutrition activities. Plan with HEWs and other health workers working in Health posts to conduct complimentary feeding demonstrations for effective, sustainable, and efficient implementation of IYCF interventions. Will provide support for integration of IYCF from screening to discharge (admission, treatment, follow up and referral) to provide care to under five years old malnourished children and PLWs. Ensure the appropriate referral system between SCs, OTPs TSFPs and IYCF Ensure the cards, GMP registration books and other necessary formats are filled in and documented properly. Ensure the IYCF coverage reaches above 60% for rural and above 70% for urban community and the other standard performance indicators are met appropriately. Support the integration of accountability practices into program activities by following established procedures during planning, implementation, monitoring, and reporting. Help ensure that accountability is reflected in day-to-day tasks, team interactions, and when working with partners or communities. Support safeguarding of program participants and employees through promoting an environment of awareness and upholding the code of conduct provisions of Medical Teams Protection from Sexual Exploitation & Abuse, Child & Vulnerable Adult protection, and harassment-free workplace policies. Incumbents will remain alert and responsive to any child and adult safeguarding risks, acquire relevant knowledge and skills which will enable you to promote strong safeguarding practices, understand the child and adult safeguarding policy and procedures, and conduct yourself in a manner consistent with the Safeguarding. Perform another Other duty as required.

fields.description: Job Description Position: Talent Development Specialist Department Human Resources Reports To HR Manager Location Addis Ababa, Ethiopia Employment Type Full-time About the Role We are looking for a Learning & Talent Development Specialist to lead the design, delivery, and evaluation of organization-wide learning initiatives — and to own our Management Trainee (MT) Program from end to end. In this role, you will build a culture of continuous learning, develop future leaders, and ensure our people have the skills and capabilities to drive Transsion's growth across emerging markets. You will collaborate closely with department heads, HR Business Partners, external trainers, and university partners to deliver impactful learning experiences at scale. Key Responsibilities Learning & Development Conduct Training Needs Assessments (TNA) across all departments and country offices. Develop and execute the annual Learning & Development plan aligned with business strategy. Design training curricula, presentations, manuals, and blended learning materials (classroom + digital). Organize and coordinate internal and external training programs, including e-learning initiatives. Deliver training sessions on company policies, soft skills, leadership, and professional development. Develop and maintain the annual training calendar and ensure timely execution. Monitor employee participation and maintain accurate training records in the LMS/HRIS. Evaluate training effectiveness through assessments, surveys, Kirkpatrick-level metrics, and performance data. Manage the training budget and optimize resource allocation for maximum ROI. Promote a culture of continuous learning through internal campaigns, learning platforms, and knowledge-sharing initiatives. Management Trainee (MT) Program Develop and manage the annual MT recruitment plan in alignment with workforce and succession needs. Partner with department heads to identify future leadership and specialist talent requirements. Support employer branding at universities, career fairs, and graduate recruitment events. Coordinate end-to-end MT candidate sourcing, assessments, interviews, and selection. Design and continuously improve the MT curriculum, rotation plans, and development roadmap. Coordinate structured onboarding and orientation for each MT cohort. Assign mentors and coaches; monitor mentoring quality and progress. Track trainee performance, learning milestones, and competency development against defined benchmarks. Organize leadership workshops, business simulations, case studies, and cross-functional project assignments. Prepare progress reports and presentations for HR leadership and senior management. Measure MT program effectiveness and ROI; recommend improvements each cycle. Recommend confirmation, promotion, extension, or reassignment based on performance reviews. Maintain a talent pipeline and succession plan for future leadership positions. Build and sustain partnerships with universities and educational institutions to attract top graduates. Key Performance Indicators KPI Target Annual training coverage rate ≥ 90% of employees Training satisfaction score ≥ 4.2 / 5.0 MT program retention rate ≥ 80% through completion MT post-program placement rate ≥ 70% in target roles within 6 months Training budget utilization Within ±10% of approved budget

company.name: Transsion Manufacturing PLC
company.description:
TRANSSION MANUFACTURING PLC.

Background

Transsion Holdings is a manufacturer of mobile phones based in Shenzhen, China. It was the largest smartphone manufacturer by sales in Africa in 2017, and also sells mobile phones in South Asia. Its brands include phone brands, Itel and Infinix after-sales service brand Carlcare and accessories brand Oraimo. It manufactures phones in China, Pakistan, Ethiopia, and Bangladesh and recently at India.

Transsion Holdings Pvt. Ltd was founded as Transsion Technology in Hong Kong in 2006, with a focus on the development, manufacturing, sales, and services of mobile communication products. Transsion entered the African market with its Tecno and Itel brands, and started focusing on the African market in July 2008, initially with feature phones Transsion released its first smartphone in 2014.Transsion set up its Nigerian subsidiary in June 2008, and had subsidiaries in seven countries in Africa by October that year. Transsion set up a manufacturing plant in Ethiopia in 2011. Transsion entered the Indian market in 2016. The market share of Transsion's smartphone brands in Africa combined surpassed that of Samsung in 2017, making Transsion the largest manufacturer of smartphones for the African market in the fourth quarter of 2017.Transsion was also the largest manufacturer of mobile phones in Africa in the first half of 2017.Transsion's 2018 attempt at a reverse takeover failed. In October 2018, Transsion Holdings started producing smartphones in their new manufacturing plant in Bangladesh.Transsion Holdings became a public listed company in September 2019 by listing on the STAR Market section of the Shanghai Stock Exchange.

Operations

Transsion sells mobile phones in Africa and South Asia. It operates mobile phone brands Tecno, Itel, and Infinix, as well as after-sales support service Carlcare and accessories brand Oraimo. Spice Digital, an Indian phone brand, was acquired in 2017. Transsion manufactures its phones in China, Ethiopia, Bangladesh, India, and Pakistan. Transsion was the first non-African mobile phone company to set up an after-sales support network in Africa.Transsion's success in the African market has been attributed to tailoring its phones' features to the needs of the African market. Transsion's phones offer a featurethat calibrates camera exposures for darker skin tones, allowing face details to be retained. Transsion developed phones with dual SIM functionality, which were well received because African users commonly used more than one SIM card at a time save money. Transsion released phones with long battery life, which are suited to low electrification rates in Africa and the propensity of blackouts. The phones included support for multiple African languages, and Tecno was the first major mobile phone brand in Ethiopia to include support for an Amharic keyboard. Transsion heavily advertises its mobile phone brands in Africa.

Vision

To become the most popular provider of smart devices and mobile services for

consumers in global emerging markets

Mission

To improve the lives of as many people as possible through technology and

innovation

CORE VALUES

·      Customer

Customers are both the starting point and the end point for all work of TRANSSIONers

·      Respect

Respect defines how we treat each other and our differences.

·      Openness

Staying open connects us to the future and its possibilities.

·      Innovation

Innovation is essential to achieving breakthroughs on different levels, both

personal and organizational.

·      Sharing

Sharing invites every “I” to become “we”.

·      Bottom line

We always show compassion, even if it puts us at a disadvantage.

fields.title: Senior Project Manager
fields.description: Role purpose: The Senior Project Manager (SPM) is responsible for the overall leadership, management, successful delivery, and achievement of results of the Ethiopia Local Governance Project (ELGP). The position provides strategic, technical, operational, financial, and partnership oversight to ensure that project objectives, outcomes, donor requirements, and Helvetas quality standards are achieved across the Amhara and Sidama regions. The SPM directly supervises the Governance Officer and the two Partnership and Capacity Development Officers, and oversees the performance, compliance, and capacity strengthening of sub-grantees (i.e. local CSO implementing partners). The role serves as the primary focal point for engagement with government signatories, including regional councils, planning bureaus, bureaus of finance, sector offices, and other strategic stakeholders, ensuring strong collaboration, ownership, and institutionalisation of project approaches. The SPM provides leadership in adaptive management, risk management, conflict-sensitive programming, Gender and Social Equity (GSE), localisation, and accountability processes, while promoting the sustainability and scaling of Integrated Community-Based Participatory Planning (ICBPP), social accountability, and participatory local governance systems. The position is ultimately accountable for the effective utilisation of project resources, achievement of project results, organisational learning, and the overall success of ELGP. Key Responsibilities: 1. Provide strategic leadership and ensure effective delivery of ELGP results in Amhara and Sidama regions: Lead the overall planning, implementation, coordination, and adaptive management of ELGP in line with project objectives, donor requirements, annual work plans, budgets, and Helvetas policies. Provide strategic direction to project staff, sub-grantees, and partners to achieve project outcomes related to citizen participation, effective council oversight, and responsive public service delivery. Oversee project progress against targets, milestones, budgets, and contractual obligations, ensuring timely delivery of outputs and outcomes. Lead annual, quarterly, and monthly planning processes and ensure quality implementation across all project locations. Assess operational, programmatic, political, and security risks and ensure appropriate mitigation measures are implemented. Ensure Gender and Social Equity (GSE), conflict sensitivity, safeguarding, accountability, and localisation principles are integrated throughout project implementation. 2. Strengthen partnerships, institutional capacity, and local governance systems for sustainable impact: Provide leadership and oversight for engagement with regional councils, planning bureaus, finance bureaus, WCSA offices, sector bureaus, CSOs, CBOs, and other strategic stakeholders. Supervise and support Governance, Partnership and Capacity Development Officers and other project staff to ensure quality technical assistance and partner support. Oversee the selection, management, performance monitoring, and capacity strengthening of sub-grantees and local partners. Promote institutionalisation of Integrated Community-Based Participatory Planning (ICBPP), grievance redress mechanisms, Financial Transparency and Accountability (FTA), Gender Responsive Budgeting (GRB), and other governance approaches within government systems. Facilitate collaboration and learning among government institutions, civil society organisations, community structures, and development partners. Represent Helvetas and ELGP in steering committee meetings, GO-NGO forums, Communities of Practice on Local Governance (CoP-LG), donor meetings, and other strategic platforms. 3. Ensure quality assurance, accountability, learning, and evidence-based decision-making: Lead project performance monitoring, review progress against indicators, and ensure effective use of MEAL data for decision-making and adaptive management. Ensure timely preparation and submission of high-quality technical, financial, donor, and organisational reports. Oversee budget management, financial compliance, resource allocation, and efficient use of project funds. Ensure implementation quality standards, operational procedures, manuals, and technical approaches are consistently applied across project locations and partners. Promote documentation and dissemination of lessons learned, best practices, success stories, and governance innovations from ELGP and its predecessor ALGP+. Support evidence-based advocacy, policy engagement, and scaling of successful governance approaches to strengthen accountable and participatory local governance systems in Ethiopia.

raw_data.title: Monitoring, Evaluation, Learning and Data Quality Lead
raw_data.description:
About Opian

Opian is an Ethiopian health-technology and innovation company building decision infrastructure for stronger health systems. We combine deep knowledge of how care and supply chains operate, human-centred product design, data engineering and responsible artificial intelligence. Our work helps health workers, managers and public institutions turn fragmented data into timely decisions—so essential medicines, vaccines and services are available where and when people need them.

Our philosophy

We believe useful innovation is not novelty for its own sake. It is the disciplined work of understanding a real problem, challenging assumptions, building and testing a better response, measuring what changes, and strengthening the institutions that must sustain the result. Technology is valuable only when it improves a decision, a workflow or an outcome in the real operating environment.

· Start with reality: design around the health workers, workloads, incentives, infrastructure and constraints that actually exist—not an imported ideal workflow.

· Build with people, not for them: government counterparts and frontline users are co-designers, decision-makers and eventual owners, not passive recipients.

· Strengthen the system, not a standalone application: connect workflows, data, institutions and incentives so information can lead to action across every level.

· Push boundaries responsibly: make ambitious but testable bets, protect safety and privacy, and change direction quickly when evidence contradicts the original idea.

· Make capability local and durable: transfer knowledge, product ownership and operational responsibility so progress continues without permanent dependence on an external project team.

· Be honest about impact: distinguish deployment from adoption and activity from results; make claims specific, measurable and open to verification.

What this means for candidates

Opian is looking for accomplished specialists who are also builders. Candidates should bring exceptional depth in their discipline, intellectual courage, practical judgment and the humility to learn from users and evidence. We value people who can move from ambiguity to a testable approach, from a workshop to an operating routine, and from a promising pilot to an institutionally owned system. The standard is simple: show not only what you know, but what you personally built, changed, tested, learned and left stronger.

· Work across public health, supply chain, policy, product, technology and field implementation boundaries.

· Turn expertise into usable products, processes, decisions and measurable improvements—not reports alone.

· Operate with urgency while preserving quality, public trust, data protection, service continuity and government ownership.

Role purpose

Build a credible measurement, evaluation and learning system that distinguishes implementation outputs from real operational outcomes and provides decision makers with timely evidence on what works, for whom, under what conditions and at what cost.

Key responsibilities

· Develop the theory of change, results framework, indicator reference sheets, learning agenda and evaluation questions.

· Define baselines, targets, denominators, data sources, disaggregation, collection frequency and accountability for each indicator.

· Design a feasible evaluation approach that strengthens attribution through comparison, phased rollout, interrupted time series or other appropriate methods.

· Measure system use, transaction completeness, latency, inventory accuracy, stock availability, stockout duration, wastage, alert closure and decision response.

· Establish routine data-quality assurance, reconciliation, verification and audit procedures across source and integrated systems.

· Ensure ethical, secure and documented management of evaluation and operational data.

· Work with implementation teams to create rapid learning cycles while maintaining independence in outcome assessment.

· Manage baseline, periodic review and end-line activities, including evaluation subawards or consultants.

· Communicate findings honestly, including null results, implementation limitations, unintended effects and remaining evidence gaps.

Expected results

· An approved, auditable measurement and evaluation plan with credible baselines and targets.

· Regular data-quality and implementation-performance findings used for course correction.

· A defensible pilot evaluation that separates deployment claims from verified operational effects.

· A learning package that informs scale-up, cost, sustainability and future investment decisions.

የቀጣሪ ድርጅት ስም ጌት ሃብ እንጨት  ፣ ብረትና አልሙኒየም ስራዎች ድርጅት

የስራ መደቡ ረዳት አካዉንታንት

የስራ ተግብርና ኃላፊነት

  •  የዕለት ተዕለት የወጪና ገቢ መረጃዎችን በሂሳብ መዝገብ ወይም በፋይናንስ ሶፍትዌር ላይ መዝግቦ መያዝ፣

  • ደረሰኞችን፣ የክፍያ ትዕዛዞችንና የባንክ ሰነዶችን ማዘጋጀትና ትክክለኛነታቸውን ማረጋገጥ፣

  •  የተሰበሰበን ጥሬ ገንዘብና ቼክ በወቅቱና በደህንነቱ በተጠበቀ ሁኔታ ወደ ድርጅቱ የባንክ ሒሳብ ገቢ ማድረግ፣

  •  ከሽያጭ ወይም ከሌሎች የገቢ ምንጮች የሚሰበሰቡ የጥሬ ገንዘብና የቼክ ክፍያዎችን በአግባቡ መቀበል፣

  •  ከንብረት ክፍልና ከግዥ ክፍል እንዲሁም ከሌሎች የፋይናን ክፍል ባለሙያዎችና ኃላፊዎች ጋር ተግባብቶና ተባብሮ መስራት፣

  •  የወርሃዊ፣ የሩብ ዓመትና የዓመታዊ የፋይናንስ ሪፖርቶችን ማዘጋጀት፣

  •  የሂሳብ ሰነዶችን በተገቢ መልኩ መያዝና ማዘጋጀት፣

  • ሁሉንም የሂሳብ ሰነዶች ለኦዲት በሚመች መልኩ ማዘጋጀት፣

  •  ከፍተኛ ሂሳብ ባለሙያዎች ጋር የሂሳብ ሥራዎችን በጋራ መስራት፣

  • ሌሎች ከስራው ጋር ተያያዥ የሆኑ ተግባራትን መፈጸም፣
    የስራ ልምድ

  •  የመጀመሪያ ዲግሪ በአካውንቲንግ ፣ በአካዉንቲንግና ፋይናንስ የትምህርት መስክ የተመረቀች አግባብነት ካለው የፈርኒቸር ተቋም ላይ ከ1(አንድ) ዓመት በላይ የስራ ልምድ ያላት፣

  •  የስራ ልምድ ማስረጃ ማቅረብ የምትችል።

 ሌሎች መስፈርቶች

  •  የፈርኒቸር ድርጅት የሂሳብ አሰራሮችን የምታዉቅ፣

  •  በቀላሉ የመግባባት ችሎታ ያለዉ፣

  • የፒች ትሪ ሶፍትዌር ችሎታ ያላት እና የስልጠና ሰርተፍኬት ያላት፣

  • የማይክሮሶፍት ወርድ ፣ ኤክሴልና በሌሎችን የኮፒዉተር እዉቀት ያላት፣

  •  ጥሩ ስነ ምግባር ያለዉ፣

  •  የድርጅቱን ሚስጥር ጠባቂ የሆነ

  •  የድርጅቱን ደንብና መመሪያ አክብራ መስራት የምትችል፣

  •  ከዚህ በፊት በፈርኒቸር ድርጅት ዉስጥ ከ1 ዓመት በአካዉንታንት ወይም በረዳት አካዉንታንት የስራ መደብ ላይ የሰራች ፣

  • ጎሮ ፣ መብራት ሃይል ፣ ሳሊተምህረትና ለጃክሮስ ቅርብ የሆነች አመልካች ብትሆን ይመረጣል፣

BACKGROUND                                                                                                                                                                                                                          YADAM Foundation is seeking a Senior Nutrition Manager/Officer to provide technical leadership on nutrition and food-systems programming — combining nutrition policy advocacy and evidence generation with the design, resource mobilization, and coordination of nutrition-sensitive agriculture and food systems projects across Ethiopia

PURPOSE OF THE ASSIGNMENT

YADAM Foundation, in partnership with UNICEF, is seeking a Senior Nutrition Specialist Consultant to provide technical leadership on advocacy and evidence-generation activities, translating national commitments (FNS 2021–2030, Seqota Declaration, N4G Paris 2025) into concrete regional policy and action to reduce child food poverty.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Provide technical leadership on nutrition-sensitive food systems and agriculture programming, integrating approaches such as crop diversification, homestead gardening, and value chain strengthening
  • Align project activities with Ethiopia's Food and Nutrition Policy/Strategy, Seqota Declaration, N4G commitments, SDGs, and the UNICEF Child Food Poverty Framework
  • Synthesize evidence on drivers of child food poverty and malnutrition, and translate findings into policy briefs and advocacy recommendations
  • Lead resource mobilization: identify funding opportunities and draft concept notes, technical proposals, budgets, and partnership agreements
  • Design and co-facilitate policy dialogues, roundtables, workshops, and multi-stakeholder consultations with government, donors, and communities
  • Coordinate with the Ministry of Health, Ministry of Agriculture, regional bureaus, UN agencies, and development partners to align activities with national priorities
  • Represent YADAM Foundation in technical working groups, donor coordination forums, and sector-level meetings
  • Support the design, planning, and implementation of food systems and agriculture projects, integrating nutrition-sensitive approaches such as crop diversification, homestead gardening, and value chain strengthening
  • Proactively identify, track, and screen calls for proposals (CFPs), grants, and funding opportunities from bilateral, multilateral, UN, and foundation donors relevant to food systems, agriculture, and nutrition
  • Organize and facilitate workshops, trainings, and stakeholder consultations for government counterparts, farmer groups, cooperatives, and development partners

Monitor project implementation against work plans, track indicators, and prepare periodic progress and donor reports

  • Support monitoring, evaluation, accountability, and learning (MEAL) activities, including data collection and documentation of results
  • Contribute to knowledge products, case studies, and communications materials showcasing project results and lessons learned

Duty Station: One of the following intervention woredas: Mai(t)sebri, Dima, Sheraro, Tahtay-Adyabo, Irob, Gulo-Mekeda, Sanja, Dabat, and Debark

Number of Positions: 9 (one per intervention woreda)

  • Duration: 12 months

Report To: Protection Officer

Organization: New Millennium Women Empowerment Organization (NMWEO)

Organizational Profile
1.1 General Information

New Millennium Women Empowerment Organization (NMWEO) is an indigenous, non-governmental, non-profit humanitarian organization established in 2007 in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. The organization was previously registered at the Ministry of Justice under registration number 3018 and later registered and licensed by the Federal Charities and Societies Agency as an Ethiopian resident’s charity by the Charities and Societal Proclamation No. 621/2009 by registration No. 0539. NMWEO has been re-registered according to the Civil Society Organizations Proclamation No.113/2019 with registration No. 0539.

Vision 

We envision a country in which women and girls have equal opportunity, claim their rights and free from any violence, and become effective social change agents.

Mission

Our mission is to empower Ethiopian women, girls, and youth in economic, political, and social dimensions, and help them unlock their potential in decision-making through capacity building, advocacy, leadership development, and humanitarian intervention programs.

Core Values and Belief

·       Humanity

·       Gender sensitive

·       Accountability

·       Equity

·       Teamwork and Excellence

·       Partnership and networking

Job Purpose

The Social Worker will support the implementation of community-based protection interventions at woreda and community level. The position will work directly with individuals, families, communities, and community structures to identify protection and social needs, strengthen community participation, facilitate access to appropriate services, and promote safe and inclusive community environments.

The Social Worker will contribute to strengthening community protection mechanisms, prevention of harmful practices, community mobilization, referral and follow-up, community action, and the effective functioning of protection-related services.

The position will apply social work principles, confidentiality, dignity, informed consent, safeguarding, PSEA, gender equality, disability inclusion, child protection, accountability, and Do No Harm throughout all activities.

Key Responsibilities

A.   Community-Based Social Work

  • Establish and maintain constructive relationships with community members and community structures.
  • Identify protection and social concerns affecting individuals, families, and communities.
  • Support communities to identify their own protection priorities and solutions.
  • Promote participation of women, girls, children, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
  • Provide appropriate basic social support within the scope of professional competence.
  • Maintain professional boundaries and confidentiality.

B.   Community Mobilization and Engagement

  • Mobilize and engage communities in project interventions.
  • Support community structures to participate effectively in protection activities.
  • Facilitate community dialogue and awareness activities.
  • Work with community and religious leaders to promote positive attitudes and practices that protect women, girls, and children.
  • Promote community ownership and sustainability of protection interventions.
  • Ensure community engagement is inclusive, conflict-sensitive, and culturally appropriate.

C.   Protection Identification and Referral

  • Identify individuals and groups experiencing or at risk of protection concerns.
  • Provide information on available services and support options.
  • Facilitate safe and appropriate referrals through established referral pathways.
  • Follow up on referrals when appropriate and in accordance with confidentiality and consent requirements.
  • Coordinate with service providers and relevant authorities as required.
  • Immediately report serious protection and safeguarding concerns through established procedures.

D.   Support to Community Protection Mechanisms

  • Support the Protection Officer in strengthening community protection structures.
  • Provide regular follow-up and technical support to community-based protection actors.
  • Support community structures to identify and address protection concerns.
  • Encourage community-based prevention and referral practices.
  • Document community concerns, actions, and feedback and share relevant information with the Protection Officer.

E.   Support to Women and Girls Safe Space

  • Support the safe and effective functioning of the WGSS.
  • Promote safe access and participation of women and girls.
  • Provide information and basic social support within the scope of the role.
  • Support linkages between WGSS users and appropriate specialized services.
  • Promote confidentiality, dignity, safety, accessibility, and respect.
  • Identify operational or protection concerns affecting women and girls and report them to the Protection Officer.

F.    Community Prevention and Social Support

  • Support community initiatives aimed at preventing protection risks and harmful practices.
  • Facilitate discussions that promote positive social norms and protective behaviors.
  • Support communities to develop and implement locally identified protection solutions.
  • Encourage positive family and community support systems.
  • Provide appropriate information and awareness on available protection and social services.

G.  Monitoring, Documentation and Reporting

  • Maintain accurate records of activities and community engagement.
  • Provide regular updates to the Protection Officer.
  • Support collection of project monitoring information and community feedback.
  • Document referrals and follow-up actions in accordance with confidentiality requirements.
  • Contribute to project reports, lessons learned, success stories, and case documentation where appropriate and ethically permissible.
  • Ensure all records are safely stored and protected.

H. Safeguarding and Accountability

  • Comply with NMWEO safeguarding, PSEA, child protection, code of conduct, data protection, and other relevant policies.
  • Maintain confidentiality and protect the privacy and dignity of community members.
  • Promote safe reporting of protection and safeguarding concerns.
  • Ensure that activities are implemented according to Do No Harm principles.
  • Promote accessibility and inclusion of persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups
  •   Inform communities about available feedback and complaint mechanisms.

Report To: Protection Officer

Organization: New Millennium Women Empowerment Organization (NMWEO)

Organizational Profile
1.1 General Information

New Millennium Women Empowerment Organization (NMWEO) is an indigenous, non-governmental, non-profit humanitarian organization established in 2007 in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. The organization was previously registered at the Ministry of Justice under registration number 3018 and later registered and licensed by the Federal Charities and Societies Agency as an Ethiopian resident’s charity by the Charities and Societal Proclamation No. 621/2009 by registration No. 0539. NMWEO has been re-registered according to the Civil Society Organizations Proclamation No.113/2019 with registration No. 0539.

Vision 

We envision a country in which women and girls have equal opportunity, claim their rights and free from any violence, and become effective social change agents.

Mission

Our mission is to empower Ethiopian women, girls, and youth in economic, political, and social dimensions, and help them unlock their potential in decision-making through capacity building, advocacy, leadership development, and humanitarian intervention programs.

Core Values and Belief

·       Humanity

·       Gender sensitive

·       Accountability

·       Equity

·       Teamwork and Excellence

·       Partnership and networking

Job Purpose

The Social Worker will support the implementation of community-based protection interventions at woreda and community level. The position will work directly with individuals, families, communities, and community structures to identify protection and social needs, strengthen community participation, facilitate access to appropriate services, and promote safe and inclusive community environments.

The Social Worker will contribute to strengthening community protection mechanisms, prevention of harmful practices, community mobilization, referral and follow-up, community action, and the effective functioning of protection-related services.

The position will apply social work principles, confidentiality, dignity, informed consent, safeguarding, PSEA, gender equality, disability inclusion, child protection, accountability, and Do No Harm throughout all activities.

Key Responsibilities

A.   Community-Based Social Work

  • Establish and maintain constructive relationships with community members and community structures.
  • Identify protection and social concerns affecting individuals, families, and communities.
  • Support communities to identify their own protection priorities and solutions.
  • Promote participation of women, girls, children, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
  • Provide appropriate basic social support within the scope of professional competence.
  • Maintain professional boundaries and confidentiality.

B.   Community Mobilization and Engagement

  • Mobilize and engage communities in project interventions.
  • Support community structures to participate effectively in protection activities.
  • Facilitate community dialogue and awareness activities.
  • Work with community and religious leaders to promote positive attitudes and practices that protect women, girls, and children.
  • Promote community ownership and sustainability of protection interventions.
  • Ensure community engagement is inclusive, conflict-sensitive, and culturally appropriate.

C.   Protection Identification and Referral

  • Identify individuals and groups experiencing or at risk of protection concerns.
  • Provide information on available services and support options.
  • Facilitate safe and appropriate referrals through established referral pathways.
  • Follow up on referrals when appropriate and in accordance with confidentiality and consent requirements.
  • Coordinate with service providers and relevant authorities as required.
  • Immediately report serious protection and safeguarding concerns through established procedures.

D.   Support to Community Protection Mechanisms

  • Support the Protection Officer in strengthening community protection structures.
  • Provide regular follow-up and technical support to community-based protection actors.
  • Support community structures to identify and address protection concerns.
  • Encourage community-based prevention and referral practices.
  • Document community concerns, actions, and feedback and share relevant information with the Protection Officer.

E.   Support to Women and Girls Safe Space

  • Support the safe and effective functioning of the WGSS.
  • Promote safe access and participation of women and girls.
  • Provide information and basic social support within the scope of the role.
  • Support linkages between WGSS users and appropriate specialized services.
  • Promote confidentiality, dignity, safety, accessibility, and respect.
  • Identify operational or protection concerns affecting women and girls and report them to the Protection Officer.

F.    Community Prevention and Social Support

  • Support community initiatives aimed at preventing protection risks and harmful practices.
  • Facilitate discussions that promote positive social norms and protective behaviors.
  • Support communities to develop and implement locally identified protection solutions.
  • Encourage positive family and community support systems.
  • Provide appropriate information and awareness on available protection and social services.

G.  Monitoring, Documentation and Reporting

  • Maintain accurate records of activities and community engagement.
  • Provide regular updates to the Protection Officer.
  • Support collection of project monitoring information and community feedback.
  • Document referrals and follow-up actions in accordance with confidentiality requirements.
  • Contribute to project reports, lessons learned, success stories, and case documentation where appropriate and ethically permissible.
  • Ensure all records are safely stored and protected.

H. Safeguarding and Accountability

  • Comply with NMWEO safeguarding, PSEA, child protection, code of conduct, data protection, and other relevant policies.
  • Maintain confidentiality and protect the privacy and dignity of community members.
  • Promote safe reporting of protection and safeguarding concerns.
  • Ensure that activities are implemented according to Do No Harm principles.
  • Promote accessibility and inclusion of persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups
  •   Inform communities about available feedback and complaint mechanisms.

company.name: Marie Stopes International Ethiopia
company.description:
About the company

Marie Stopes International (MSI) is one of the largest international Sexual Reproductive Health (SRH) and Family Planning (FP) organizations in the world. We are a results oriented social enterprise that develop efficient, effective and sustainable SRH/FP programmes around the world.

Marie Stopes International Ethiopia (MSIE), a partner of MSI, is currently undertaking a dramatic scale-up of health service delivery for low income women and couples in Ethiopia. This includes expanding services in clinics and rural outreach programs into new regions of Ethiopia and creating social franchising networks of private quality service providers.  MSIE announces information about job vacancies widely and encourages applications from all sectors of the community.  MSIE considers all applicants based on their abilities and will ensure no group is disadvantaged on the basis of disability, gender, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race (which includes colour, nationality and ethnic or national origins), religion or belief, economic or social class, sex, HIV/AIDs status and political affiliation.

MSIE also implements a Safeguarding Policy to safeguard and protect the rights of staff, children, young people and vulnerable sections of the community and to this end, successful candidates will need to sign MSIE’s ‘code of conduct’ and undergo a background check. The Safeguarding Policy includes an adult Safeguarding, dignity at work place, child safeguarding, human trafficking and anti-slavery, sexual harassment, equality and diversity.  MSIE applies zero tolerance approach for the violation such policies. 

MSIE is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to hiring and retaining female employees. The organization has flexible policies including: travel policy for pregnant and lactating women, flexible work hour for non-clinic staff without reducing the total working hour. Women employees have access to on-job mentorship which aim to create gender-sensitive and inclusive work environment. As such, qualified women are encouraged to apply 

 

Our Mission

Ensuring the Individual’s Right to Children by Choice not Chance.

Vision
To become a sustainable nationwide provider of high quality, integrated reproductive health/family planning services.

Our Values

1 Mission driven
With unwavering commitment, we exist to empower women and men to have children by choice not chance.

2 Client centred
We are dedicated to our clients and work tirelessly to deliver high-quality, high-impact services that meet their individual needs.

3 Accountable
We are accountable for our actions and focus on results, ensuring long term sustainability and increasing the impact of the Partnership.

4 Courageous
We recruit and nurture talented, passionate and brave people who have the courage to push boundaries, make tough decisions and challenge others in line with our mission.
 

Why work for us

MSI works in 37 countries around the world to help women and girls to have children by choice, not chance.

For an individual woman or girl, being able to choose when she has children means having the power to take control of her future.
It can mean having the ability to finish her education, pursue a career, look after the children she already has and ensure she remains healthy. MSI was founded in 1976 to provide the contraception and safe abortion services that give women and girls a choice. Since then, choice has been at the heart of everything that we do and our mission remains clear: to help women and girls to have children by choice, not chance.

MSI is a global organisation with 11,000 team members working in 37 countries to deliver our mission. Starting from one single clinic in London, our organisation has grown from one clinic in central London to become one of the world’s largest providers of high quality, affordable contraception and safe abortion services.
Over the last 40 years, we have touched the lives of more than 120 million women and girls, giving them the power to take control of their futures. But we know that there is much more to do, today there are over 230 million women who want to use contraception but can't and that number continues to grow.

fields.title: DevOps & Cloud Infrastructure Engineer
fields.description: Birrama Digital Commerce PLC is seeking a skilled and hands-on DevOps & Cloud Infrastructure Engineer to manage, secure, automate, and continuously improve the company's technology infrastructure. The successful candidate will work across Linux systems, local/private and public cloud environments, networking, containerized applications, Kubernetes, CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure security, monitoring, and observability. This is a practical engineering role suited for someone who is comfortable working directly with production environments, troubleshooting complex infrastructure issues, automating deployments, and ensuring that systems and applications remain secure, reliable, scalable, and highly available. Strong practical experience with local/private cloud infrastructure is particularly valued for this position. Key Responsibilities 1. Operating Systems & Networking Administer and maintain Linux-based environments, particularly Ubuntu, RHEL, and Alpine Linux . Manage operating system packages, updates, patches, system services, and dependencies. Monitor and optimize server performance and resource utilization. Configure and maintain users, groups, directories, file permissions, and access controls. Troubleshoot Linux server, operating system, and application-level issues. Configure and manage DNS, TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, SSH, and related network protocols . Install, renew, configure, and troubleshoot SSL/TLS certificates . Manage SSH keys and secure remote access. Configure and maintain firewall rules and network access controls. Diagnose network connectivity, routing, DNS, ports, latency, and service availability issues. 2. Cloud Infrastructure & Services Deploy, configure, maintain, and troubleshoot virtual machines and cloud compute resources. Manage infrastructure hosted primarily on local/private cloud environments , as well as public cloud platforms where required. Administer object storage solutions such as S3-compatible storage, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob Storage , or similar platforms. Configure and manage: Virtual Private Clouds (VPCs) Subnets Routing NAT gateways Load balancers Security groups Firewall rules Implement and maintain secure Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies. About the company

Coca-Cola was first bottled in Ethiopia’s capital, Addis Ababa, in 1959 by the Ethiopian Bottling Share Company, which later opened a second branch in Dire Dawa in 1965.

The two plants were nationalized in 1975 and ran as public companies until 1996 when they were bought by Ethiopian entrepreneurs through privatization. Just prior to this, in 1995, Coca-Cola Sabco bought shares in the business and, in 1999, signed joint venture agreement with Ethiopian owners. With its leadership working hand in hand with employees, the business has seen significant growth over the years. Processes and functions have improved, resulting in considerable sales increases. On July 02, 2016, SABMiller plc, The Coca-Cola Company and Gutsche Family Investments (controlling 80% of Coca-Cola South African Bottling Company (Sabco) officilay merged and created Africa’s largest Coca-Cola bottler - Coca-Cola Beverages Africa (CCBA)

With the aim of increasing its foot prints across the nation, a new plant was commissioned in 2016 at Bahir Dar having state-of-the-art production facility.

East Africa Bottling Share Company as a Coca Cola Franchise Bottler in Ethiopia under Coca-Cola Beverages Africa (CCBA) has three production plants in Addis Ababa, Dire Dawa and Bahir Dar with an aggressive expansion plan throughout the country, hence bringing the total number of employees to more than 1,800.


Our Vision

To Refresh Africa and Create Shared Value


Our Mission

• to be the Leading and Most admired Company in Africa


Refresh Africa every day and make our continent a better place for all 

Our Values

➢   We have a passion for the coca-cola business and for the brand

➢   We think and act like “owners” at all times

➢   We work and win in teams across the business

➢   Accountability is clear and personal

➢   We hare humble but confident in all we do

➢   Safety, quality, the environment, and our communities are integral to our working lives All of this we do it with the highest integrity

Why work for us

Why join us?

  • We always act with the belief of Growing our people, "grows the busi­ ness". Our people will always be our competitive advantage. Become part of a large community where employees get a chance to network and build connections.
  • We empower our people to learn a new skill on the job through self-direction. Work with many talented and experienced people who are able to guide employees' career development.
  • Our leaders possess ample expertise in the Industry making them ideal Mentors & Coaches. As we are made up of small teams, employees will get unique opportunities to learn a variety of skills.
  • Our Genetic make-up highly values teamwork, positive attitude, effective communication, diversity, innovative mindset, agility, and continuous learning.
  • We engage in executing our social responsibility where we operate making sure we play our part in alleviating social challenges with respect to community education, women entrepreneurship, environmental protection - This is the basis for a brighter future, built on a hand up, not a handout.
  • Work for a brand that is well-known internationally and instantly recognizable. Our brand has been a leading brand for over 130 years and still continues to grow because We are not constrained by traditional thinking but prefer to "think like a consumer" and take risks.

Team Benefits

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

We are true believers of pay for performance principle which is why we continuously review our packages towards motivating our people to pursue excellence in their duties and drive business productivity.


PROFESSIONAL ADVANCEMENT

company.name: Marie Stopes International Ethiopia
company.description:
About the company

Marie Stopes International (MSI) is one of the largest international Sexual Reproductive Health (SRH) and Family Planning (FP) organizations in the world. We are a results oriented social enterprise that develop efficient, effective and sustainable SRH/FP programmes around the world.

Marie Stopes International Ethiopia (MSIE), a partner of MSI, is currently undertaking a dramatic scale-up of health service delivery for low income women and couples in Ethiopia. This includes expanding services in clinics and rural outreach programs into new regions of Ethiopia and creating social franchising networks of private quality service providers.  MSIE announces information about job vacancies widely and encourages applications from all sectors of the community.  MSIE considers all applicants based on their abilities and will ensure no group is disadvantaged on the basis of disability, gender, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race (which includes colour, nationality and ethnic or national origins), religion or belief, economic or social class, sex, HIV/AIDs status and political affiliation.

MSIE also implements a Safeguarding Policy to safeguard and protect the rights of staff, children, young people and vulnerable sections of the community and to this end, successful candidates will need to sign MSIE’s ‘code of conduct’ and undergo a background check. The Safeguarding Policy includes an adult Safeguarding, dignity at work place, child safeguarding, human trafficking and anti-slavery, sexual harassment, equality and diversity.  MSIE applies zero tolerance approach for the violation such policies. 

MSIE is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to hiring and retaining female employees. The organization has flexible policies including: travel policy for pregnant and lactating women, flexible work hour for non-clinic staff without reducing the total working hour. Women employees have access to on-job mentorship which aim to create gender-sensitive and inclusive work environment. As such, qualified women are encouraged to apply 

 

Our Mission

Ensuring the Individual’s Right to Children by Choice not Chance.

Vision
To become a sustainable nationwide provider of high quality, integrated reproductive health/family planning services.

Our Values

1 Mission driven
With unwavering commitment, we exist to empower women and men to have children by choice not chance.

2 Client centred
We are dedicated to our clients and work tirelessly to deliver high-quality, high-impact services that meet their individual needs.

3 Accountable
We are accountable for our actions and focus on results, ensuring long term sustainability and increasing the impact of the Partnership.

4 Courageous
We recruit and nurture talented, passionate and brave people who have the courage to push boundaries, make tough decisions and challenge others in line with our mission.
 

Why work for us

MSI works in 37 countries around the world to help women and girls to have children by choice, not chance.

For an individual woman or girl, being able to choose when she has children means having the power to take control of her future.
It can mean having the ability to finish her education, pursue a career, look after the children she already has and ensure she remains healthy. MSI was founded in 1976 to provide the contraception and safe abortion services that give women and girls a choice. Since then, choice has been at the heart of everything that we do and our mission remains clear: to help women and girls to have children by choice, not chance.

MSI is a global organisation with 11,000 team members working in 37 countries to deliver our mission. Starting from one single clinic in London, our organisation has grown from one clinic in central London to become one of the world’s largest providers of high quality, affordable contraception and safe abortion services.
Over the last 40 years, we have touched the lives of more than 120 million women and girls, giving them the power to take control of their futures. But we know that there is much more to do, today there are over 230 million women who want to use contraception but can't and that number continues to grow.

company.name: Hope Enterprise’s University College
company.description:
Hope Enterprises or Hope is a local NGO that was established in 1971 in Addis Ababa to help the needy help themselves through basic needs, education, competence, job and business mediation and value education. As Hope was completing its 32 years of humanitarian service in 2003, it’s then Executive Director, Dr. Minas Hiruy, recommended to the Board the establishment of an outstanding liberal arts university college by submitting a full-fledged proposal. After some discussion, the Board and the General Assembly of Hope accepted the proposal, establishing Hope University College as the first public benefits institution of higher learning in the country on November 25, 2003.  Soon after, the Board adopted a new structure comprising the Ladders of Hope that subsumed the existing and non-college activities of Hope as one division and Hope University College as another division, opening the way for the university college to operate autonomously.
 

Values

The University College believes in goodwill to humankind and to nature and in the concretization of this concern as a step to making the world a community of hope, justice, peace and progress. The University College holds dear the advancement of liberal education as a means of personal and social transformation and regards the provision of education to all as an important public responsibility.

Vision

The vision of the University College is to contribute to the renewal and transformation of society through knowledge and value based education and graduates who can make a difference using what they had gained in the university college.

Mission

The University College, having a mission to provide aspiring leaders the option of pursuing world-class education without leaving their country and cultural setting, shall enable the development of leaders, who being capable of independent work, problem solving, analysis, innovation and reflection, can make a difference in the development of society and in mutually and sustainably supportive relations between man and nature.

Mission Statement

Developing leadership for a world of hope

fields.title: Access and Safety Officer
fields.description: Medical Teams Calling Daring to love like Jesus, we boldly break barriers to health and restore wholeness in a hurting world. Medical Teams International holds strict child and vulnerable adult safeguarding principles and a zero-tolerance policy for misconduct related to sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse in the workplace and other places where the organization’s activities are rendered. Parallel to technical competence, recruitment & selection, hiring decisions will give due emphasis to assessing candidates' eligibility thorough background checks, police clearance, and professional reference check processes. JOB SUMMARY The Access and Safety Officer contributes to the calling of Medical Teams by assisting in the implementation of safety, access, and security policies and procedures to support the organization’s operations. This field-based role involves building and maintaining relationships with local authorities and stakeholders, conducting risk assessments, and ensuring staff are trained in access and security protocols to create a safe working environment. ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES Create and maintain professional relationships with local authorities, community leaders, and other stakeholders in project locations to ensure community acceptance and collaboration. Create and maintain a network of security contacts and information sources for triangulation purposes. Monitor local government requirements and processes for travel and project implementation, ensuring up-to-date knowledge of regulations. Administrate access, registration, or movement permission requests for field staff, ensuring necessary letters are obtained and renewed on time. Uphold Medical Teams image positively to external stakeholders, highlighting the value and results of its work. Establish and maintain positive working relationships with sector personnel with other local NGOs/UN. Attend relevant inter-agency security coordination meetings to stay informed of regional security dynamics as required by the Field Coordinator. Conduct desktop and on-the-ground risk assessments for new locations, evaluating risks to staff, beneficiaries, and assets. Assess safety and security conditions of potential facilities, reconciling recommendations for necessary improvements. Coordinate with Field program staff on how security concerns impact project plans and work implementation. Ensure that all vehicles, facilities, and equipment comply with Medical Teams' security standards, administrating improvements when necessary. Uphold the Field Operations Safety and Security Policy, creating recommendations on SOPs, protocols, and practices to mitigate risks. Review and update safety and security SOPs regularly, ensuring approval and dissemination across the team. Collaborate on the development and implementation of contingency plans, including for crisis management, evacuation, relocation, and medical evacuation. Lead and train Field staff in security simulations and drills to ensure preparedness for emergency situations. Collect, analyze, and communicate security information from various sources, producing weekly access and security updates. Organize and lead regular security briefings for field staff, visitors and stakeholders. Maintain a clear and organized filing system for all access and security-related documentation. Track and map all security incidents, providing timely analysis to inform security management strategies. Ensure staff are checking in and that movement information is recorded and updated regularly. Brief new staff on safety procedures and security updates, ensuring regular refresher briefings for existing staff. Document and report on security incidents, drafting incident reports promptly for submission to Country Access and Safety Manager and to senior leadership. Assist in identifying training needs for staff, leading safety and security training according to the Medical Teams Safety and Security Training Manual. Provide regular training and scenario drills on personal security, compound security management, defensive driving, and communications procedures. Administrate the line management of the guards, ensuring that they have everything they need to fulfill their role and perform well. Promote the conditions for effective teamwork and commitment to Medical Teams’ values and operating principles. Lead by example regarding Medical Teams’ safety and security procedures. Ensure accountability is integrated into country strategies, program design, monitoring and evaluations, recruitment, staff onboarding, training and performance management, partnership agreements, and highlighted in reporting. Support safeguarding of program participants and employees through promoting an environment of awareness and upholding the code of conduct provisions of Medical Teams Protection from Sexual Exploitation & Abuse, Child & Vulnerable Adult protection, and harassment-free workplace policies. Incumbents will remain alert and responsive to any child and adult safeguarding risks, acquire relevant knowledge and skills which will enable you to promote strong safeguarding practices, understand the child and adult safeguarding policy and procedures, and conduct yourself in a manner consistent with the Safeguarding code of conduct and behavior expectations.

company.name: Repi Soap & Detergent PLC
company.description:
REPI SOAP & DETERGENT PLC formerly known as REPI Soap factory was established 1974 by the name Bianil Ethiopia Share Company by foreign investors of Swiss & Greek origin aiming to produce and distributed powdered detergent to East Africa market which was dominantly by Uniliver brand OMO. Less than a year after its formation, it was owned by the Ethiopian government & was managed under the direct supervision of the National Chemical Corporation and was re-established as a public enterprise in 1992 by the council of Ministers and was recapitalized by Birr 1,525,000.00.

 

At that time, the company main vision was  to compete  against  local & imported powder detergent through its famous brand “ROL” , due to the machinery age and technological issues there was an issue of wastage which nearly bankrupted the company but thanks to a pioneering idea of creating detergent bar (cake) in 1979, Repi gave birth to a new line of product and a new brand  “Ajax”. Again in 1994 production of a liquid detergent was introduced under the brand name ‘LARGO”

Following the earmarking of REPI Soap factory by the government for joint venture partnership , LINA PLC having registered its interest in the joint venture Commissioned Vision Consultancy PVT LTD CO to undertake a series of studies on the factory with the aim of concluding a joint venture agreement with the factory management and the E.F.D.R Privatization & Public Enterprise Supervising Authority.

 

A joint venture partnership between “LENA PLC” and E.F.D.R Privatization & Public Enterprise Supervising Authority (PESSA) was then established  during the fiscal  period 2007/2008 after intensive negotiation was carried out between both parties involved which there after paved the way for the establishment of REPI SOAP & DETERGENT SHARE COMPANY.

 

LINA PLC is a share company  mainly involved  in trading ,real estate  and small scale manufacturing of corrugated steel & tea and added REPI SOAP & DETERGENT PLC to its portfolio of investment by acquiring 51% of share amounting to Birr 9,360,000.00 of the total share amounting to 18,360 ,000 while the remaining 49% amounting to birr 9,000,000 was raised by PESSA in the form of assets based on business evaluation of the factory.

The joint venture arrangement lasted one year followed by a full takeover of the share company by

LENA PLC after settling of the remaining 49% share previously held by the Ethiopian government.

 

 In response to the growing demands of the soap & detergent, today our company is a leading player  and well respected organization in the country detergent industry. The current market demand for our product and the fact that the current factory could not provide us the product volume due to imperfect condition and age of machinery and equipment’s therefore not supplying the capacity required ,we are committed to exciting expansion project  which is in a final phase ,would be beneficial for the shareholder ,employees local businesses and overall the company. In this sector REPI has positioned itself at the fore-front of the market.

In July,2014 Repi Soap and Detergent S. Co. (Repi) and Wilmar International Limited (Wilmar) have signed a joint investment agreement for the upgrading of an existing manufacturing facility in Sebeta Road, Kolfe Karenio Sub City and building of a new integrated manufacturing complex in Dima, Sebeta Town, Oromia Region in Ethiopia that will house an edible oil refinery and packing plant, production plants for specialty fats, soft oils, soaps and detergents, as well as a facility for sesame seed processing. Repi and Wilmar will each have a 50%participation in the joint investment.

Repi is a sister company of AL-SAM Private Limited Company, incorporated and existing under the laws of the Democratic Republic of Ethiopia. It engages in the manufacturing of soap and detergent products. Headquartered in Singapore, Wilmar is Asia’s leading agribusiness group engaging in oil palm cultivation, oilseed crushing, edible oils refining, sugar milling and refining, specialty fats, oleo-chemical, biodiesel and fertilizer manufacturing, and grain processing. It has a presence in 14 countries across Africa. This joint investment marks Wilmar’s first operations in Ethiopia.

Combining the expertise of both parties, the joint investment will have a positive impact on the development of the manufacturing and export sector, as well as create employment opportunities in Ethiopia.



About Wilmar

﻿

Wilmar International Limited, founded in 1991 and headquartered in Singapore, is today Asia’s leading agribusiness group. Wilmar is ranked amongst the largest listed companies by market capitalisation on the Singapore Exchange.Wilmar’s business activities include oil palm cultivation, oilseed crushing, edible oilsrefining, sugar milling and refining, specialty fats, oleochemical, biodiesel and fertiliser manufacturing, and grain processing.

At the core of Wilmar’s strategy is a resilient integrated agribusiness model that encompasses the entire value chain of the agricultural commodity processing business, from origination and processing to branding, merchandising and distribution of a wide range of agricultural products. It has over 450 manufacturing plants and an extensive distribution network covering China, India, Indonesia and some 50 other countries. The Group is backed by a multinational workforce of about 90,000 people. Wilmar’s portfolio of high quality processed agricultural products is the preferred choice of the food manufacturing industry, as well as the industrial and consumer food businesses. Its consumer-packed products occupy a leading share in its targeted markets. Through scale, integration and the logistical advantages of its business model, Wilmar is able to extract margins at every step of the value chain, thereby reaping operational synergies and cost efficiencies.

Wilmar remains a firm advocate of sustainable growth and is committed to its role as a responsible corporate citizen.

company.name: Marie Stopes International Ethiopia
company.description:
About the company

Marie Stopes International (MSI) is one of the largest international Sexual Reproductive Health (SRH) and Family Planning (FP) organizations in the world. We are a results oriented social enterprise that develop efficient, effective and sustainable SRH/FP programmes around the world.

Marie Stopes International Ethiopia (MSIE), a partner of MSI, is currently undertaking a dramatic scale-up of health service delivery for low income women and couples in Ethiopia. This includes expanding services in clinics and rural outreach programs into new regions of Ethiopia and creating social franchising networks of private quality service providers.  MSIE announces information about job vacancies widely and encourages applications from all sectors of the community.  MSIE considers all applicants based on their abilities and will ensure no group is disadvantaged on the basis of disability, gender, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race (which includes colour, nationality and ethnic or national origins), religion or belief, economic or social class, sex, HIV/AIDs status and political affiliation.

MSIE also implements a Safeguarding Policy to safeguard and protect the rights of staff, children, young people and vulnerable sections of the community and to this end, successful candidates will need to sign MSIE’s ‘code of conduct’ and undergo a background check. The Safeguarding Policy includes an adult Safeguarding, dignity at work place, child safeguarding, human trafficking and anti-slavery, sexual harassment, equality and diversity.  MSIE applies zero tolerance approach for the violation such policies. 

MSIE is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to hiring and retaining female employees. The organization has flexible policies including: travel policy for pregnant and lactating women, flexible work hour for non-clinic staff without reducing the total working hour. Women employees have access to on-job mentorship which aim to create gender-sensitive and inclusive work environment. As such, qualified women are encouraged to apply 

 

Our Mission

Ensuring the Individual’s Right to Children by Choice not Chance.

Vision
To become a sustainable nationwide provider of high quality, integrated reproductive health/family planning services.

Our Values

1 Mission driven
With unwavering commitment, we exist to empower women and men to have children by choice not chance.

2 Client centred
We are dedicated to our clients and work tirelessly to deliver high-quality, high-impact services that meet their individual needs.

3 Accountable
We are accountable for our actions and focus on results, ensuring long term sustainability and increasing the impact of the Partnership.

4 Courageous
We recruit and nurture talented, passionate and brave people who have the courage to push boundaries, make tough decisions and challenge others in line with our mission.
 

Why work for us

MSI works in 37 countries around the world to help women and girls to have children by choice, not chance.

For an individual woman or girl, being able to choose when she has children means having the power to take control of her future.
It can mean having the ability to finish her education, pursue a career, look after the children she already has and ensure she remains healthy. MSI was founded in 1976 to provide the contraception and safe abortion services that give women and girls a choice. Since then, choice has been at the heart of everything that we do and our mission remains clear: to help women and girls to have children by choice, not chance.

MSI is a global organisation with 11,000 team members working in 37 countries to deliver our mission. Starting from one single clinic in London, our organisation has grown from one clinic in central London to become one of the world’s largest providers of high quality, affordable contraception and safe abortion services.
Over the last 40 years, we have touched the lives of more than 120 million women and girls, giving them the power to take control of their futures. But we know that there is much more to do, today there are over 230 million women who want to use contraception but can't and that number continues to grow.

Ensure community engagement approaches are conflict-sensitive, inclusive, and culturally appropriate. E.
